title: Situation Awareness for Intelligent Data Distribution in Connected Vehicles
abstract: The limitations of on-board sensors and blind spots caused by occlusion cause the reduction of perception quality in autonomous vehicles. In such cases, cooperative perception provides additional data via Vehicle-to-Everything communication to enhance local perception, causing a large volume of data transmission. The vehicle can focus on acquiring and utilizing relevant data according to the prevailing road context by identifying the current traffic situation. To achieve this, we propose a concept for the situation identification of the vehicle using Bird's-Eye-View images. Firstly, the situation around the vehicle is identified using object detection with semantic segmentation, followed by understanding the context of the traffic using a situation identification module consisting of an open-source projective transformation network Cam2BEV and a situation identification neural network. The concept was evaluated and validated by running the software on the CARLA simulator using the in-built RGB camera and the semantic segmentation camera. Additionally, the portability of the situation identification module for real-world applications was verified on Cityscapes and nuScenes urban driving datasets. Overall, the proposed situation identification approach enables efficient sensor data management by prioritizing relevant data to the current traffic situation. The source code is available in the following link: https://github.com/akshaynarla/DySi_Select

title: A Study of Bengali Grapheme-to-Phoneme Conversion
abstract: Grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) conversion is a foundational component of speech technology, yet the languages for which it has been carefully studied remain a small fraction of the world's languages. Bengali is spoken by over 230 million people, making it one of the world's most widely used languages, but it remains comparatively understudied in natural language processing, and G2P for Bengali in particular has received less attention. In this dissertation, we use neural architecture comparison, error analysis, and explicit correction techniques to identify and address the sources of G2P error in Bengali. First, we train and compare four neural G2P architectures, including attentive recurrent models, a transducer, and a transformer, on a Bengali pronunciation lexicon, and use a finite-state error analysis to attribute most remaining errors to inherent vowel realization rather than to other properties of Bengali orthography. Based on this finding, we design a correction classifier that predicts vowel presence and quality as a post-hoc correction layer, and show that it substantially reduces word error rate when applied to the earlier models. We then examine whether performance improves with additional data. We present the first multi-source G2P corpus for Bengali, combining two independently constructed lexicons through several fusion strategies, and find that the transcription consistency of a training resource matters more than its raw lexical coverage. We also present the first systematic evaluation of large language models on Bengali G2P, and find that even the strongest model tested substantially underperforms a purpose-built baseline, extending prior findings about general-purpose language models on phonological tasks to a morphologically complex, low-resource language. Finally, we introduce the first publicly available Bengali diacritization corpus, and show that restoring diacritics that disambiguate pronunciation, rather than inferring it implicitly, allows both a recurrent model and a fine-tuned byte-level transformer to resolve the ambiguity directly.

title: Enterprise Transitions to the Agentic Era: A Qualitative Study of How Open Source AI Innovators and Enterprise Practitioners are Navigating the Shift from Cloud-first to Agent-first
abstract: What is the reality of enterprise agent adoption, as we approach the last few months of 2026? In partnership with Futurewei, Guru Technologies, LF AI & Data, the Tokenomics Foundation, and the Agentic AI Foundation, LF Research completed a qualitative study on how open source innovators and practitioners are navigating the shift from cloud-first to agent-first. The key takeaway is that trust, governance, and cost are more important gatekeepers than model capability. Agents are becoming an enterprise orchestration layer and human-in-the-loop accountability must be built into the plumbing. Meanwhile, volatile token economics are causing new methods for metering usage and controlling consumption. Download the full report to explore the roadmap for managing tokenomics, setting up governance control layers, and securing long-term digital sovereignty!

title: Distributed Multimodal Data Fusion and Privacy Protection Strategies for Smart Healing Spaces: Towards Facility Operation and Maintenance Support
abstract: Smart healing spaces rely on continuous environmental, physiological, behavioral, and feedback data to keep therapeutic facilities operating reliably and support timely maintenance decisions. Existing approaches suffer from weak multimodal fusion, poor edge coordination, and heavy communication overhead from centralized raw-data upload. This study proposes a privacy-preserving federated multimodal fusion framework for scalable, low-latency smart healing space monitoring and decision support, with facility operation and maintenance as a prospective extension: edge nodes preprocess environmental, physiological, behavioral, and feedback data, extract modality-specific latent representations, and fuse them via mask-aware temporal attention into a unified status representation for healing-state recognition and, prospectively, equipment assessment and maintenance scheduling; local updates are clipped, DP-perturbed, and securely aggregated into a reliability-weighted global model. Results show 93.2% accuracy and 92.9% F1 in healing-state recognition (5.1/4.5 points above prior methods), 88.2% F1 under severe non-IID conditions, 38.9% lower communication overhead versus FedAvg, and membership-inference attack success reduced from 71.8% to 38.7%. These results validate healing-state recognition and the communication-latency-privacy trade-offs; facility-maintenance tasks such as sensor-fault diagnosis are an architectural extension, not separately benchmarked here.

title: PROSPECTS FOR THE APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN THE SERVICE SECTOR OF THE ECONOMY IN AZERBAIJAN
abstract: Artificial intelligence technologies are acting as a driving force of change in the world economy. This technology has a significant impact in areas such as increasing efficiency in the service sector, automation, and strengthening customer service. This article examines the application opportunities, directions, challenges, and future prospects of artificial intelligence in the service sector in Azerbaijan. The study covers the areas of banking and finance, healthcare, retail, tourism, transport and logistics, and public services. The level of AI readiness, key challenges, and expected economic impact of each sector are analyzed in a comparative table format. As a result of the study, recommendations on policy in the field of artificial intelligence have been developed.

title: The Mahapatra-Kronecker-Hermite MKH Algorithm: A Deductive Linear Algebra from First Principles
abstract: The Mahapatra-Kronecker-Hermitian (MKH) Algorithm is derived from first principles—withoutassuming a Hermitian matrix, without importing external constants, and without relyingon quantum phase estimation.The algorithm begins with the Majorana Conjugate Zero x = −x = 0, derives theimaginary unit i from the entanglement of natural numbers N and −N, and forces theprimordial invariant ∆ = 4 ln 99 through the Dalvi Dictact.The quadratic regulator Q(x) = (x − 99)(396 − x) constructs the finite lattice Z396,from which the Hilbert space H396 = L2(Z396) ⊗ C2is formed. The Kronecker OperatorK = D + 99 · I is the Hermitian matrix—derived exactly, not assumed. Its eigenvaluesλn = 99 + γn are real and positive, and all trajectories terminate in at most 7 steps.The Mahapatra Identity ei·e∆/22√2 Sbounded(∆) = i2 proves that i, π, and e are emergent, notprimitive. Geometry emerges from arithmetic recursion.The MKH Algorithm is not a modification of existing quantum algorithms. It is anindependent, self-contained, arithmetic-first algorithm that ensures the operator is knownbefore computation begins. The scaffolding is removed. The edifice stands alone. The seed is Mahapatra Topological Control Invariant MTCI ∆ = 4 ln 99. Fromit, everything follows.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Computational Complexity
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a fundamentally different approach to computation than classical systems. This research explores the potential of leveraging entanglement as a core building block for computational complexity, proposing a novel method for quantifying the difficulty of algorithms through the development of an entanglement metric. The core claim is that certain computational tasks exhibit inherent complexity that cannot be adequately explained by classical complexity theory, and that this approach could lead to a deeper understanding of the limits of computation. The paper details the creation of an entanglement metric, a mathematical framework designed to directly relate entanglement properties to computational resource requirements, and demonstrates its ability to accurately estimate the complexity of specific algorithms. This work represents a significant step towards a more rigorous and predictive analysis of computational challenges, potentially uncovering previously unrecognized limitations within the realm of algorithmic complexity.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Tensor Integration and Quantum Computing Association
abstract: This paper explores the integration of non-linear geometry tensor representations into quantum computing, aiming to develop a novel quantum computation algorithm capable of dynamic state manipulation and a deeper theoretical foundation for the field. The core mechanism involves introducing a dynamic topology tensor, which intricately links geometric tensors with quantum state structure, enhancing stability, controllability, and computational efficiency. This approach offers a fundamentally different pathway to quantum processing compared to existing quantum algorithms. The research investigates the potential of this integration to unlock new capabilities within quantum systems, particularly in the realm of state manipulation and entanglement.

title: 基于自组织矩阵的动态量子算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic quantum algorithm framework based on self-organizing matrices. The core idea is to dynamically adjust quantum algorithm parameters through the inherent properties of these matrices, enabling automated optimization and enhanced performance. We detail the framework's architecture, the mechanisms driving parameter adjustments, and the advantages it offers over traditional approaches. The paper explores the potential of this approach to achieve more efficient and scalable quantum computations. The research focuses on the practical implications of this design, emphasizing its ability to adapt to a wider range of quantum systems and problems.

title: Neural Time-Space Networks (NSN) – A Novel Computational Framework for Complex System Simulation
abstract: Neural Time-Space Networks (NSN) represent a novel computational framework for automating the design and optimization of neural network topologies, offering a powerful approach to simulating complex biological systems and physical phenomena. This paper introduces NSN, a framework that leverages the inherent topological properties of neural networks to generate and refine complex network configurations, enabling more effective and robust simulation of intricate systems. The core mechanism centers on integrating a computational model with the network topology, allowing for automated optimization and the discovery of optimal configurations. This approach addresses limitations of traditional methods by providing a flexible and automated pathway to complex system modeling. We demonstrate the efficacy of NSN through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to generate topologically diverse and functionally relevant neural network structures. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future directions of this innovative computational methodology.

title: Dimension Generalization and the Correlation of Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the potential synergy between dimensionality generalization and the correlation of quantum entanglement, focusing on the development of a novel computational framework that leverages entanglement to address the limitations of classical computation. We propose a new approach to quantum computing centered around the "dimension mapping" mechanism, which dynamically translates quantum states across multi-dimensional spaces to extract information. This research investigates the feasibility of utilizing entanglement as a key element in enabling the processing of ultra-high-dimensional spaces and ultimately contributes to exploring quantum computation's potential for enhanced capabilities. The core claim centers on the construction of a fundamentally new computational paradigm that extends beyond the constraints of conventional algorithms, potentially unlocking novel quantum applications.

title: Quantum Neural Turing Machines with Adaptive Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Quantum Neural Turing Machines (QNTMs) to enhance performance in complex sequential tasks through adaptive entanglement control. The core concept is that traditional QNTM architectures often rely on static entanglement, limiting their ability to efficiently process long-range dependencies. We propose a novel QNTM architecture incorporating a trainable quantum circuit designed to dynamically adjust entanglement between the quantum memory and processor units. This adaptive entanglement mechanism allows for optimized resource allocation and improved performance in tasks requiring intricate sequential reasoning. The proposed system utilizes a modified Turing machine framework within a quantum computing environment, leveraging quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to achieve enhanced data storage and retrieval. The theoretical framework outlines the key components and operational principles, emphasizing the crucial role of trainable entanglement parameters in shaping the network's behavior. The system is designed to learn optimal entanglement patterns through a differentiable training process, mimicking the dynamic adaptation observed in biological neural networks. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the effectiveness of the adaptive entanglement control mechanism in improving task performance compared to static entanglement QNTMs. We conclude that adaptive entanglement control represents a significant advancement in QNTM research, unlocking the full potential of quantum computing for complex sequential learning problems.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络架构
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph neural network (GNN) architecture based on adaptive connection weights. Traditional GNNs often rely on predefined structural representations, limiting their ability to effectively model dynamic graph structures and information flow. This work proposes a self-adaptive connection weight mechanism that allows the network to dynamically adjust the weights of connections based on the graph's evolving characteristics. We demonstrate that this adaptive approach significantly improves the expressiveness and generalization capabilities of GNNs compared to existing methods. The proposed architecture incorporates a novel learning strategy for weight adaptation, focusing on minimizing the discrepancy between predicted and actual graph connectivity. We present a series of experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrating the effectiveness of our design in various graph-based tasks.

title: ## Buffy Broad-nosed Bat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Echolocation
abstract: This paper introduces Buffy, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the echolocation behavior of the Buffy broad-nosed bat (Syrinx nebulosa). Echolocation, a sophisticated sensory adaptation employed by these bats, involves emitting high-frequency sound pulses and interpreting the returning echoes to navigate and locate prey in darkness. Buffy leverages this process by employing a population of "bats" (potential solutions) that iteratively adjust their "calls" (parameter vectors) based on the received "echoes" (fitness evaluations). The algorithm utilizes a combination of a momentum-based velocity update, a distance-based exploration strategy mimicking the bat's flight path, and a local search mechanism resembling the bat's prey capture behavior. We present a detailed description of Buffy's methodology, including the core components of the algorithm, the rationale behind each design choice, and a theoretical analysis of its convergence properties. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with a relatively low computational cost. Keywords: Metaheuristic, Echolocation, Bat Algorithm, Optimization, Evolutionary Algorithm, Search Algorithm.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Topology Control for Quantum Path Exploration
abstract: Quantum state adaptive topology control offers a novel approach to quantum computation, addressing the limitations of traditional algorithms reliant on static path design. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum state's inherent self-adjoint nature to dynamically adjust quantum states, enabling proactive exploration of potential quantum paths. We introduce a framework that utilizes a dynamically evolving topology, guided by quantum state properties, to enhance the efficiency of quantum path discovery. The core mechanism centers around the concept of 'quantum topology' – a mathematical framework describing the interconnectedness and transformation of quantum states – and its application to optimization of quantum computation. We present a theoretical model and initial experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in guiding quantum path exploration, ultimately offering a significant advancement in quantum algorithm performance. The significance of this work lies in its potential to overcome the inherent challenges in quantum computation through active, self-adaptive topology manipulation.

title: Bonthain Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bonthain Rat
abstract: This paper introduces Bonthain Rat, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bonthain Rat, a small rodent known for its complex and seemingly random navigation patterns within a maze. The algorithm combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) to create a robust search strategy. Bonthain Rat utilizes a dynamic population of "rats" navigating a problem space, with each rat's movement influenced by both its own best-known solution and the best solution found by the entire swarm. Furthermore, a temperature parameter analogous to SA is incorporated to allow for exploration and escape from local optima. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a "tunneling" strategy mimicking the Bonthain Rat's ability to quickly traverse short distances, significantly accelerating convergence. Performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's adaptability and ability to handle complex, multi-dimensional search spaces make it a promising tool for various optimization applications.

title: Black-tailed Prairie Dog Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Prairie Dog Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Black-tailed Prairie Dog Algorithm (BTPDA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of black-tailed prairie dogs. Prairie dogs exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in a dynamic environment, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies. The BTPDA mimics these behaviors through a population-based search, incorporating key elements such as territory marking, resource competition, and adaptive movement patterns. The algorithm employs a novel fitness evaluation function that considers both the quality of the solution and its distance from previously visited locations, promoting effective exploration and exploitation. Mathematical formulations are provided to detail the core components of the algorithm, including the population update rule, the territory marking mechanism, and the adaptive movement strategy. The algorithm is demonstrated through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its efficiency and adaptability compared to established metaheuristic methods. The key performance indicators, such as convergence rate and solution quality, are analyzed, providing insights into the algorithm's strengths and potential applications. The BTPDA offers a promising approach to tackling complex optimization challenges across diverse fields.

title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithm for Optimal Packing of Data Streams
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum-inspired algorithm for optimizing the packing of data streams, addressing the limitations of classical packing algorithms when faced with large, dynamic datasets and limited prior knowledge of data distribution. The algorithm leverages concepts inspired by quantum superposition to explore multiple packing configurations concurrently. A key element is a fitness function derived from quantum state overlap, which guides the search process towards solutions exhibiting optimal packing efficiency. The algorithm's core mechanism relies on iteratively refining a set of potential packing arrangements, evaluating them based on the fitness function, and selecting arrangements with higher overlap with a target quantum state. Simulation results demonstrate the algorithm's ability to outperform traditional packing methods in scenarios characterized by high data volume and evolving data patterns. This approach represents a significant step towards adapting quantum-inspired techniques for practical data management challenges.

title: Legal Protection Mechanisms for Intellectual Property Rights in Generative AI Prompts
abstract: With the widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI), prompts have become an important medium of interaction between users and AI models. They not only influence the direction of AI-generated content but may also embody users’ creative intentions and expressive choices. However, existing discussions of intellectual property protection for generative AI tend to conflate the prompt itself, its influence on the generation process, and human contributions to AI-generated outputs. This has resulted in unclear protected objects and assessment standards, leaving prompts subject to both regulatory gaps and divergent judicial interpretations. This article demonstrates the necessity of legal protection for prompts from both technological and legal perspectives. By analyzing the role of prompts within the technological process, it clarifies their potential legal significance. Interests associated with generative-AI prompts do not constitute a protected object with a single legal characterization but should be classified according to their different stages in the creative process: first, the prompt itself as an independent form of expression; second, the user’s control and creative contribution to the AI-generation process embodied in the prompt; and third, new expression created through the user’s editing, modification, or supplementation of the initial AI-generated output. Generative AI produces final outputs through model training, semantic prediction, and probabilistic calculation. Although prompts can influence the direction of model generation, they generally do not directly determine the specific content or form of the resulting expression. Therefore, entering a prompt cannot automatically give rise to copyright protection or determine copyright ownership. The focus should instead be on whether the user makes a legally meaningful creative contribution through prompt design, adjustment of the generation process, and subsequent editing. Intellectual property protection for generative-AI prompts should be established within the existing intellectual property framework by developing a classified protection model based on human creative contributions at different stages and establishing protection standards and institutional mechanisms consistent with the technological characteristics of AI. Establishing a clear framework for the independent protection of prompts is not only a key component of developing the intellectual property system in the age of AI but also a necessary measure for upholding the legal principle of human-centeredness and protecting human intellectual contributions. It is of significant theoretical and practical importance for promoting the healthy and orderly development of the generative-AI industry.

title: Ontological Approach to Knowledge Graph Assessment in the Domain of Mechanical Product Lifecycle Management Systems
abstract: Abstract— This paper examines the application of an ontological approach to constructing a dataset for evaluating and comparing context enrichment systems for large language models using knowledge graphs in the domain of management systems for mechanical product lifecycles. In this domain, obtaining the required amount of textual data with a formal logical structure to form an evaluation set without using generated synthetic data is challenging. To avoid introducing distortions and hallucinations when generating evaluation data, a novel solution to the data deficiency is proposed. This solution involves extracting ontology directly from product and assembly files compliant with the STandard for Exchange of Product Model Data. This potentially enables the use of all product data as a source for scaling evaluation data. The goal of this paper is to create a dataset of structured textual data in the domain of mechanical product lifecycle management systems, develop an evaluation methodology, and implement context enrichment pipelines for large language models with and without knowledge graphs to analyze the contribution of data-structure-extracting systems to the quality of generated responses. In this paper: a new source of evaluation data is proposed, a new methodology for generating text evaluation data while preserving the logical structure is developed, a pipeline for using the generated evaluation data is implemented, and evaluation results are obtained that confirm the positive contribution of systems with the extraction of structured data to the quality of generated responses in the domain of mechanical product lifecycle management systems.

title: A Study on Human-Centric Explainable Ai Auditing Systems for Financial Inclusion, Digital Empowerment, and Trust-Building in Emerging Economies
abstract: This paper investigates human-centred XAI resolutions for financial inclusiveness, digital enablers and responsibility and confidence in AI-enabled finance in emerging markets. It examines how AI aids financial audit across credit, fraud, regulation, audit, compliance, digital payment services and risk classification; and it enables exclusionary hazards of unequal data, unaccountable tools, inscrutable docs and opaque management; ultimately aiming to develop an Human-Centred XAI Trust Structure for contextually-appropriate audibility and contestability in identifying if financial audit is technically reliable, intelligible, challengeable, socially inclusive and institutionally accountable. It employs qualitative secondary data-based conceptual research using an integrative literature review, thematic investigation, qualitative content analysis, stakeholder examination, case-based comparative analysis, risk-control activity mapping and conceptual synthesis; drawing evidence from open access academic journals, policy papers, financial innovation policies, AI ethical codes, fintech management policies, emerging markets exemplars. Its essentials signify that AI-enabled financial audit provides dual accountability due to the double nature of financial activity and its automated audit; and technical transparency even cannot generate peoples' understanding, capability, correction and inquiry of the automated decisions. Financial digital exclusion can arise from incomplete and unrepresentative data, proxy-based bias, uneven error rate, opaque docs, natural language translation, human fragility, disintegrated accountability lines and weak grievance response. The context-sensitive human-centred trust structure weights up contextual perception, data and modeller integrity, human-centred explication, auditability, participation, inclusive management and empowerment outcomes. It documents Stakeholder-centred explication, responsible decisions, Trust calibration and Guide to contextual implementation for responsible AI in digital finance.

title: Developing an explainable artificial intelligence framework for patient-reported outcomes: an interpretable approach for understanding patient experiences in vascular care
abstract: Background: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems can autonomously generate insights from healthcare data, yet there remains a need for transparent, reproducible, and clinically interpretable approaches for translating patient-reported outcomes into actionable improvements. This study evaluated an explainable machine learning (ML) framework applied to structured survey data to identify drivers of perceived care quality following coronary and peripheral treatment.Methods: A four-step analytic pipeline was applied to the United States (U.S.) cohort (n=131) of the Beyond Intervention (BI) Year 3 survey. Natural language processing aligned BI survey items with validated Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (HCAHPS) domains. Patient-level features (n=31) were then used to train a stacked ensemble ML model (Support Vector Machine + Random Forest + Gradient Boosting → logistic regression meta-learner) for predicting survey responses. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified feature impact, and subgroup likelihood analyses evaluated demographic and clinical variation.Results: Three BI survey items were most semantically aligned with HCAHPS quality domains. The stacked model achieved test set area under the curve values of 0.774 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.680–0.867] for Question 1, 0.761 (95% CI: 0.634–0.887) for Question 2, and 0.717 (95% CI: 0.594–0.840) for Question 3. Age and digital health familiarity were consistent associative factors across outcomes. Younger patients (aged 35–44 years) were 4.7 (95% CI: 2.1–8.3) times more likely to report negative perceptions, while patients with greater digital health experience more often expressed uncertainty or feelings of burden. Socioeconomic status (SES) and prior cardiovascular events also emerged as important modifiers.Conclusions: In the era of autonomous AI, interpretable ML frameworks are essential for clarifying why patient groups perceive care differently. Digital health literacy, age, and SES were consistently associated with patient experience, underscoring the need for explainable approaches that support targeted interventions and trustworthy feedback loops. Brier scores (0.197–0.224) confirm well-calibrated predictions.

title: Impact of homomorphic encryption schemes on the performance of data handling in machine learning
abstract: Integrating encryption into Machine Learning (ML) pipelines allows organizations to leverage data-driven intelligence without compromising user privacy, ensuring confidentiality across data storage, transmission, and computation. However, encrypting data during both training and testing phases introduces significant computational overhead. To mitigate this cost, this paper analyses a hybrid paradigm: training models on plaintext data and performing inference on encrypted data. While Homomorphic Encryption (HE) enables secure computation, it often requires modifying ML algorithms to be compatible. This study evaluates ML performance metrics, including accuracy, inference time, latency, and throughput, by benchmarking multiple HE schemes across diverse datasets. Our dual-advantage approach reduces training overhead while maintaining flexibility in selecting encryption-ML pairs. The results show that Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) offers better privacy protections than Partial Homomorphic Encryption (PHE). However, it comes with higher computational costs, including longer delays and lower processing speed. These trade-offs should be considered according to the performance needs of the specific machine learning application. This research, in the broader development of artificial intelligence, not only provides a systematic guide based on evidence for the matching between different machine learning algorithms and cryptographic schemes, but also pushes forward the transformation of trustworthy AI from theory to engineering practice.

title: Semantic-aware cross-granularity contrastive learning for Chinese named entity recognition
abstract: Chinese Named Entity Recognition (CNER) aims to identify and classify entity mentions from Chinese text and serves as a fundamental task for many downstream natural language processing applications. Recently, word-character lattice frameworks have been widely used to incorporate word-level information into CNER models. However, existing methods typically integrate lexical information through dedicated encoder architectures, such as Flat-Lattice Transformer , while overlooking the complex interactions across different granularities between character-level and word-level representations. Consequently, these methods do not fully exploit lexical knowledge and semantic dependencies, particularly their interactions with character representations. In this paper, we propose A noveL cross-granulariTy contrAstive learnIng network (ALTAI), which integrates lexical and semantic knowledge at multiple granularities. Specifically, ALTAI employs a Cross Transformer to explicitly model interactions among character representations, word-level lexical representations, and semantic representations, enabling effective information exchange across different granularities. Meanwhile, Cross-Granularity Contrastive Learning is introduced to align character representations with their corresponding lexical and semantic views, encouraging consistent representations across character, word, and semantic spaces. Together, these components produce discriminative entity representations by modeling cross-granularity interactions. Experiments on four benchmark datasets show that ALTAI consistently outperforms strong baseline models.

title: DIBOS: Dynamic Identity‐Based Ordered Signatures With Timeout‐Skip for Blockchain Document Approval
abstract: ABSTRACT In a document approval system, multiple signers must approve a document in strict chronological order. We propose a blockchain‐based document approval system that integrates a dynamic identity‐based ordered signature (DIBOS) scheme built on Sakai's identity‐based signature. The DIBOS scheme supports two critical real‐world features: (i) dynamic signer updates (insertion, deletion, or replacement of signers mid‐approval while preserving prior signature validity) and (ii) timeout‐skip with backup signers (automatic skipping of unresponsive signers with immutable audit logging). We formalize a strengthened Order‐Unforgeability with Skip (OUf‐S) security model and prove our scheme secure under it. Three smart contracts handle signer registration, document request delivery, and batch verification. We implement the off‐chain signing on both Intel X64 and ARM64 platforms; dynamic operations add less than 12% overhead, making the system suitable for resource‐constrained IoT devices. A full cost analysis on the Ethereum Goerli testnet demonstrates the practicality of the approach.

title: SVP Is NP-Hard for Some Rank-2 Cyclotomic Modules
abstract: Let $q$ range over primes congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. Let $ζ_q$ be a primitive $q$th root of unity, and put $K=\mathbb{Q}(ζ_q)$, with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K=\mathbb{Z}[ζ_q]$. We prove that the decision version of the Shortest Vector Problem ($\mathrm{SVP}$) in the $\ell_2$-norm is $\mathrm{NP}$-complete on full-rank free submodules of $\mathcal{O}_K^2$ by a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction from Exact Cover by 3-Sets (X3C). The module rank is fixed at two. As a $\mathbb{Z}$-lattice, the module has rank $2(q-1)$, which grows with $q$. The main obstacle is closure under the action of $\mathcal{O}_K$. A module containing a nonzero vector also contains every scalar multiple of that vector by a nonzero element of $\mathcal{O}_K$, and some of these multiples may be shorter. Three ideas overcome this obstacle. First, we map the Bennett--Peikert Reed--Solomon lattice to a principal cyclotomic ideal and use Wan's point-count estimates to prove that a coset of this ideal contains many binary coefficient representatives. Second, a checker based on a quadratic Gauss sum turns the X3C equations into a canonical squared norm. Third, the checker and a second module coordinate combine with a separation bound for ideal cosets to rule out every unintended vector created by the $\mathcal{O}_K$-action. Each constructed instance consists of a prime $q\equiv3\pmod4$, two integral generators whose $2\times2$ generator matrix has nonzero determinant, and an integer squared threshold. The construction also gives $\mathrm{NP}$-hardness of search-$\mathrm{SVP}$ under polynomial-time Turing reductions.

title: GazeRefine: Expert Gaze as a Test-Time Prompt for Training-Free Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation remains difficult to scale because high-performing methods typically rely on dense expert annotations and task-specific training. We introduce GazeRefine, a training-free framework that uses gaze as an inference-time prompt for zero-shot medical image segmentation. Sparse, duration-weighted fixations are converted into foreground and background priors that initialize semantic prototypes in frozen DINOv3 feature space. These prototypes are iteratively refined through foreground-background discrimination, feature-space affinity propagation, and anchoring to the initial gaze guidance, allowing segmentation to extend beyond directly fixated regions while limiting semantic drift. GazeRefine requires no segmentation masks, fine-tuning, adapters, prompt encoders, or gradient updates. We evaluate the method on gaze-annotated polyp segmentation and prostate MRI segmentation. The results show strong performance on colonoscopy images and competitive performance on prostate MRI, supporting gaze-guided prototype refinement as a promising approach for segmentation-label-efficient, human-in-the-loop medical image segmentation. Our tools and code can be found in the following repository: https://github.com/MohammedOussamaBEN/GazeRefine.git

title: AgentFactory: Towards Automated Agentic System Design and Optimization
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities as powerful components in agentic systems, enabling sophisticated reasoning and complex task execution. However, current approaches to manually designing and optimizing agentic systems heavily rely on manual effort, limiting their adaptability and scalability. Recent work has explored the automated optimization of workflow designs. However, these approaches often overlook the crucial role of model capabilities and focus on single performance metrics, failing to address real-world deployment constraints. In this paper, we present AgentFactory, a framework that jointly optimizes both foundation models and workflow structures in agentic systems while considering multiple objectives including performance, cost, and efficiency. AgentFactory leverages advanced LLMs as optimizers to navigate the vast search space of possible configurations, employing a three-stage optimization pipeline to automatically discover effective combinations of fine-tuned models and optimized workflows. Through an iterative optimization process, our framework systematically explores and evaluates different agentic system designs, adapting to task-specific requirements while maintaining operational efficiency. We evaluate AgentFactory across eight benchmarks spanning five domains, including general reasoning, coding, mathematics, medicine, and finance. Our experiments demonstrate that AgentFactory consistently outperforms both manually designed methods and existing automated approaches, achieving an average improvement of 9.1% across all benchmarks, with particularly significant gains in domain-specific tasks (19.6% on MedQA and 18.7% on FinEval). These results establish AgentFactory as a promising approach for developing more capable and efficient agentic systems through automated optimization.

title: Towards a Reliable and Practical Eval Pipeline
abstract: LLM-based software systems increasingly require effective "evals" as quality gates in the development lifecycle. However, existing work typically addresses individual aspects of eval reliability rather than the full set of practical requirements. We present an end-to-end eval pipeline that combines eval checklist creation, with learned aggregation for checklist responses, to improve agreement across LLM judges and accuracy against human judgments. The framework additionally pro- vides self-consistency, explanations, and prediction uncertainty, and we empirically demonstrate its effectiveness.

title: Real-Time Neuromorphic Spectrum Intelligence Simulator
abstract: We present the Real-Time Neuromorphic Spectrum Intelligence Simulator (RT-NuSIS), a modular framework to study spiking neural network (SNN) and memristor-inspired agents for dynamic spectrum access under constrained energy budgets and adversarial conditions. RT-NuSIS couples leaky integrate-and-fire neuronal dynamics, memristive synaptic models, physics-informed energy-harvesting models (triboelectric and RF), and adversary models including jamming and Byzantine behavior. We formalize the simulator mathematically, prove boundedness, present a mean-field adversary threshold, analyze per-step complexity, and provide a reproducible benchmark harness for energy-per-inference, latency, and robustness metrics. The codebase is modular, deterministic by seed, and designed for large-scale event-driven simulations.

title: Regular fat linear sets
abstract: Abstract In this work, we introduce ( r , i )-regular fat linear sets, which are defined as linear sets containing exactly r points of weight i and all other points of weight one. This notion generalizes and unifies existing constructions; scattered linear sets, clubs, and other previously studied families are special cases. We present new classes of regular fat linear sets in $${{\,\textrm{PG}\,}}(k-1,q^n)$$ PG ( k - 1 , q n ) for composite n and study their equivalence classes. Finally, we show that regular fat linear sets naturally yield three-weight rank-metric codes, which we use to obtain bounds on their parameters.

title: Applications of Entanglement in Quantum Information
abstract: Entanglement is the resource that most sharply distinguishes quantum information processing from its classical counterpart, and this thesis examines it from two complementary directions: how it can be detected and quantified, and how it, together with the broader machinery of quantum correlations, interference, and measurement, can be put to use. We first study two simple, measurable conditions that detect bipartite entanglement, and show that the extent to which either is violated yields a lower bound on the negativity of a state. The bound is established for two qubits, extended to systems of arbitrary finite dimension, and sharpened when partial knowledge of the Schmidt vectors is available. We then turn to discrete-outcome quantum sensor networks, in which one seeks only to determine which detectors, or which group or spatial pattern of detectors, has responded to a signal. Working in the weak-interaction regime, where the output states are nonorthogonal, we use minimum-error and unambiguous state discrimination to show that entangled initial states and collective measurements confer an advantage when detectors are grouped, and we develop a shift-operator formalism that gives closed-form success probabilities for the detection of shifted patterns in one- and two-dimensional arrays. Next we consider the problem of learning two unknown pure qubit states, together with their probabilities of occurrence, from a scrambled stream; we show that receiving the systems in identically prepared pairs supplies exactly the extra quantum information needed, since the resulting two-qubit state in the symmetric subspace has a unique decomposition into pure product states, which we recover by tomography. Finally, we show how interference and measurement can convert information encoded in the phases of quantum amplitudes into information encoded in their magnitudes, amplifying the amplitudes that carry useful information and suppressing those that do not, and we apply this technique to states produced by the quantum approximate optimization algorithm for the MaxCut and minimum-vertex-cover problems. Throughout, a single theme recurs: the correlations and superpositions permitted by quantum mechanics are at once something to be measured and something to be exploited.

title: New Entanglement-Assisted Codes and Mathematical Structures in Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum information processing promises exponential advantages for certain computational and communication tasks, but practical quantum devices are inherently vulnerable to decoherence and operational imperfections. This thesis develops new algebraic and analytical tools for quantum error correction (QEC) aimed at unifying entanglement-assisted coding theory with operator-algebra frameworks, while also providing mathematically rigorous insights for continuous-variable photonic implementations. First, we introduce the framework of entanglement-assisted operator algebra quantum error correction (EA-OAQEC), extending entanglement-assisted QEC in an operator-algebra context. Built on a stabilizer-based formalism, EA-OAQEC unifies and generalizes subspace, subsystem, and hybrid classical-quantum entanglement-assisted codes. We establish a master error-correction theorem, define a generalized distance notion, and develop constructive techniques including gauge fixing, clean-qubit transformations, and entanglement-assisted gauge-fixing procedures. Second, we study general logical operators: unitaries that preserve a stabilizer codespace beyond the traditional Pauli normalizer. We derive explicit structure theorems for the centralizer and normalizer in the full unitary setting and show how normalizer transformations can be parameterized via classical bit matrix multiply complement (BMMC) permutations. Finally, motivated by photonic quantum computing, we analyze finite-rank compressions of the continuous position and momentum operators relevant to Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. We prove that the spectra of these compressions are governed by the roots of classical Hermite polynomials and connect the compressed operators to physically realizable approximations of displacement operations and finite-energy GKP states.

title: Anatomical Assessment of Six Diagnostic Questions for Identifying the Next Artificial-Intelligence Winner: Continual Learning, Capital–Experience Duality, and the Unstoppable AI Hypothesis Volume I of the KSCCN Working Paper Series on Architectural Diagnostics
abstract: This first volume undertakes an anatomical assessment of six diagnostic questions posed by Srini Pagidyala (2026) as a scoreboard for identifying the next artificial-intelligence (AI) winner. The questions contrast architectures that improve through use with those that improve only through laboratory retraining; intelligence that scales with accumulated experience rather than with capital expenditure; the adequacy of incumbent benchmarks; the economic inversion of capital intensity; the distinction between structural repair and scaffolding; and the obsolescence test for today's training–inference stack. For each question the paper compares and contrasts the principal competing theories—scaling-law orthodoxy and the bitter lesson; continual and lifelong learning; catastrophic interference and synaptic consolidation; cognitive-first and neurosymbolic programmes; Goodhartian benchmark theory; general-purpose-technology and stranded-asset economics; Henderson–Clark architectural innovation; and Kuhnian and Christensenian accounts of paradigm shift. The assessment concludes that the six questions are analytically important: they isolate a genuine architectural fault line between frozen, capital-intensive foundation models and systems that compound capability through experience. They do not, however, license a prediction of field-level arrest. Also available on Academia.edu: https://www.academia.edu/attachments/134108293/download_file?s=portfolio

title: CleitonForge: differential testing for quantum compilers, with declared oracle power
abstract: A differential fuzzer for quantum compilers, and a measurement of what its oracles can actually detect. A negative result in differential testing has no meaning without a declared oracle power. This release measures that power instead of asserting it, on 284,595 mutants across 216 configurations, and reports two blindness results. Blindness 1 — outcome counts and the Rz sign convention Over the gate family {H, X, Z, Ry, Rz, CX, CZ}, an outcome-counts oracle has zero power against a global Rz sign convention fault: 0 of 16,418 non-equivalent mutants, 95% Wilson interval [0.000%, 0.023%], across three widths and three depths. The state oracle flags the same mutants at 72.8%, which is what proves they are not equivalent. Inverting every Rz conjugates a circuit built from otherwise real gates, and |z|² = |conj(z)|², so no measurement probability moves. Inverting a single Rz conjugates nothing and is ordinarily visible at 52.0%. These are two fault classes, not one. Blindness 2 — error correction and deterministic Paulis On a rotated surface code memory experiment, an oracle that derives its reference from the circuit under test has zero power against a deterministically inserted Pauli: | fault | non-equivalent | self-referential oracle | |---|---|---| | insert X | 321 | 0.0% | | insert Z | 211 | 0.0% | | insert S | 211 | 100% | | insert H | 357 | 100% | | drop CX, drop H, swap CX qubits | 30 | 100% | False positives 0.0% on the 328 equivalent mutants, so the zeros are not an insensitive test. Adding the logical observable does not help and is also 0.0%, because the observable is computed self-referentially too. research/qec_minimal_witness.py reduces this to four instructions and one qubit, where the detector error models are identical, both self-referential rates are 0.0000, and the cross-referential rates are 0.0000 and 1.0000. Reported as https://github.com/Deltakit/deltakit/issues/347 Method Power is measured against non-equivalent mutants only. A mutation that leaves the operator unchanged up to global phase cannot be detected by any correct oracle, so counting it as a miss understates every oracle at once. The reference oracle is validated by a known-answer battery before use (research/qec_sanity.py, seven cases). Four earlier designs of the reference oracle failed that battery while printing perfectly plausible numbers; a previously published figure of 81–89% for the operator oracle turned out to be circuits containing no Rz at all, and is retracted in research/README.md. Sampled oracles are scored for false positives on the equivalent mutants, which are a free negative control.

title: L=4 [[1536,6,16]] 4D toric code — circuit-level logical error rate and phenomenological exponent
abstract: Circuit-level logical error rate measurement for the L=4 [[1536,6,16]] 4D toric code under independent X/Z phenomenological noise, with full BP+OSD decoding. Two error rates tightened to usable precision after a long interrupted measurement saga on a volatile shared box (14 attempts across the p=0.005 leg alone, ~14,350 new shots, auto-retry + per-25-shot checkpointing + genuine resume preserving zero shots lost across the whole run). Results. p=0.006: 54 fails / 3000 shots → p_L = 0.01800, 95% Poisson CI [0.01352, 0.02349] (tightening run, 9 attempts, clean finish after ~4.4 h). p=0.005: 31 fails / 15375 shots → p_L = 0.00202, 95% Poisson CI [0.00137, 0.00286] (tightening run completed, 14 attempts, final attempt clean start-to-finish in 28 min after a decoder-contention stall was fixed). Phenomenological exponent across the two tightened points: e = ln(p_L(0.006)/p_L(0.005)) / ln(0.006/0.005) ≈ 12.01, 95% CI [8.52, 15.59]. What this is. A two-point local exponent between p=0.006 and p=0.005, a narrow window near where L=4 first shows measurable (non-saturated, non-zero) circuit-level failures. Real and citable for this window; not yet cross-validated against a third point, and a two-point slope this close to the edge of the measurable window can describe local flattening rather than the true asymptotic physics. p=0.004 and below remain explicitly unpriced/unattempted. What this is not. Not a claim about the asymptotic exponent at much lower p. Not a host-viability verdict for [[1536,6,16]] (that is downstream of L3_EXPONENT_RESULT.md's existing L=3-based verdict, which already says L=4 survives). Not a claim about code-capacity numbers (these are circuit-level direct Monte Carlo, not the binom-model circuit-level estimate or the code-capacity quantity — see the discriminator note in the writeup). Honest findings carried into the measurement. Data syndrome matrices are weight-4 (pymatching-incompatible); single-shot metacheck repair works at q≤0.01; the ensemble does not beat its best member (robustness value, not accuracy gain). Logical error rate 0.38–0.43 at (p,q)=(0.02,0.01). All code, results, control arms verified. Provenance. Every quoted p_L in the writeup traces to l4_stats.json via provenance_audit.py (status: AUDITED, 0 unlabeled quoted values). The writeup keeps superseded intermediate readings struck through rather than deleted, per this project's standing rule. Companion record. The full-stack hive implementation this measurement belongs to is deposited separately at 10.5281/zenodo.21863879 (canonical of a triple-duplicate cluster resolved 2026-08-31).

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: ## Central American Fringe-lipped Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Fringe-lipped Bat (FLB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Central American fringe-lipped bat (Antrozous belzebuth). The algorithm leverages the bat's unique echolocation and exploration strategy to effectively navigate complex optimization landscapes. The core mechanics of the FLB algorithm are modeled using a system of differential equations, representing the bats' flight dynamics. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates parameters analogous to the bat's pulse rate, frequency, and angle of emission to dynamically adjust the search process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results demonstrate that the FLB algorithm exhibits strong convergence properties and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm. The algorithm's adaptability and efficient exploration capabilities make it a promising candidate for tackling a wide range of complex optimization challenges. The key mathematical formulations and algorithmic procedures are detailed within this document.

title: Cadena's Tailless Bat
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, "Cadena's Tailless Bat," inspired by the foraging behavior of tailless bats (Vespertilionidae). The algorithm mimics the bats' efficient searching strategy, utilizing a combination of random flight and systematic exploration. The core of the algorithm relies on a modified version of the bat algorithm, specifically focusing on the bats' ability to converge to optimal solutions while minimizing premature convergence issues. We present the algorithm's detailed formulation, including the key parameters and their roles in the search process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations and comparisons with established metaheuristic methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in solving various benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that Cadena's Tailless Bat exhibits promising performance and robustness across different problem landscapes.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Spin State Prediction
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic topology-based quantum spin state prediction algorithm designed to enhance the accuracy of quantum spin state prediction. Traditional prediction methods often rely on classical calculations, while this approach capitalizes on the inherent quantum properties of spin states to achieve improved predictions. The core mechanism involves mapping the quantum spin state to a dynamic topology, allowing for a more nuanced and comprehensive analysis of the state's possible configurations. This algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to existing methods, offering a promising avenue for advancements in quantum spin dynamics.

title: ## Brown Big-eared Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Echolocation Search" (ES), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brown Big-eared Bat (Corynorhinus crassicus). Bats utilize sophisticated echolocation techniques to navigate and locate prey in complex and dynamic environments. ES mimics this process by employing a multi-dimensional search space, representing environmental characteristics, and utilizing a probabilistic 'pulse' emission strategy to explore and exploit potential solutions. The algorithm incorporates key features of bat echolocation, including frequency modulation, amplitude modulation, and spatial mapping, to guide the search process. Specifically, ES utilizes a population of candidate solutions, each represented by a vector of parameters. Each solution 'emits' a 'pulse' – a vector of probabilities – that is adapted based on the fitness of the solution and the landscape gradient. The algorithm employs a 'spatial mapping' mechanism, where solutions are clustered based on their similarity, and the emission probability is influenced by the density of neighboring solutions. The core of ES is a dynamically adjusted 'frequency' parameter, which controls the exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results suggest that ES offers a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios requiring robust exploration and efficient exploitation of complex solution spaces.

title: 基于自适应的图论的图嵌入算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph embedding algorithm based on adaptive graph theory. Traditional graph embedding methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively capture dynamic graph characteristics. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts embedding parameters based on the graph's inherent properties, resulting in improved representation learning performance. We detail the core mechanism – a self-adaptive parameter adjustment process – and demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of benchmark examples. The algorithm's adaptability and potential for enhanced representation learning make it a significant advancement in the field of graph embedding.

title: The Dynamic Adjustment Algorithm for Topological Cryptography
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topological cryptography algorithm designed to enhance security through adaptive structure manipulation. Traditional cryptographic schemes often rely on static designs, limiting their resilience against attacks. This research proposes a method that dynamically adjusts the underlying topological structure during encryption, creating a significantly more robust and resistant encryption protocol. The core mechanism involves the continuous modification of the topology, making it computationally challenging for adversaries to break the encryption without knowing the initial structure or the algorithm's parameters. The algorithm's security is predicated on the difficulty of reverse engineering the initial topology, which, in turn, makes it highly resistant to known attacks. This advancement holds significant promise for secure communication and data protection in the face of evolving cryptographic threats.

title: Wave Function Collapse for Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, including artificial intelligence and data analysis. A fundamental challenge in QML lies in efficiently exploring complex solution spaces, especially during optimization processes. This paper investigates the application of wave function collapse, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, as a potential mechanism to accelerate these exploration processes. We explore the feasibility of incorporating this concept into an algorithm designed for optimization tasks within quantum machine learning, aiming to reduce the computational burden and enhance the speed of training and inference. The core of our work centers on demonstrating the potential of wave function collapse to guide the algorithm towards optimal solutions through a novel, iterative process. This paper presents a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation illustrating the potential of this approach.

title: AgentDojo Trace Audit
abstract: AgentDojo Trace Audit is a benchmark-specific research-software layer for reconstructing and auditing a frozen AgentDojo v1.2.1 corpus. It links source-content identity, deterministic record selection, population accounting, denominators, derived records, official-evaluator replay, reported results, and claim locators. It also evaluates a declared provenance-fault model. For the declared corpus, the software reconstructed and traced 11,624 selected records, comprising 11,236 attack-present records and 388 no-injection records, with cells 6,893 / 200 / 3,727 / 416. Official-evaluator replay passed for 11,624/11,624 records. Frozen Catalog B detected and classified 408/408 mutations and localized 336/408; all 72 localization failures are preserved. Post-repair Catalog C was developmental and achieved 330/330. Preregistered post-repair Catalog D was a confirmatory regression challenge and detected, classified, and localized 360/360 mutations in its one-shot run. Two frozen benign-control suites produced 0/120 alarms. The release contains owner-authored software, documentation, schemas, and synthetic fixtures. It does not redistribute AgentDojo source code, raw traces, or model outputs. Users must separately obtain official AgentDojo commit 089ed468cf3ed0322acc66b0211f26d9d90dbf60. The tested environment is CPython 3.12.13 on Linux. External replicability has not been established. title: Improving Sentiment Classification Performance Using Pseudo-Labeling with Naive Bayes and Random Forest
abstract: Sentiment analysis has been applied to understand users' opinions expressed in unstructured text on various online platforms. Supervised machine learning approaches typically require large amounts of labeled data; however, annotation is expensive and laborious. This research aims to implement semi-supervised learning via pseudo-labeling to reduce reliance on labeled data and improve the performance of sentiment classification models relative to a supervised baseline. Contributions of this research include a pseudo-labeling framework implemented with limited labeled data, benchmarking of Naive Bayes and Random Forest algorithms across three Indonesian-language datasets with different linguistic characteristics (IndoNLU, E-commerce, and BCA Mobile app reviews), and an analysis of model performance sensitivity to the pseudo-labeling threshold. Count Vectorizer and TF-IDF were utilized for feature extraction with unigram and bigram parameters. Accuracy and F1-score were measured to benchmark model performance. Results show that pseudo-labeling improved performance across all classification models compared to the baseline by an average of 0.005–0.010, and up to 0.030 on the E-commerce dataset. Naive Bayes was found to have more consistent results across datasets, while Random Forest capitalized more on the implementation of pseudo-labeling under the right circumstances. Overall, TF-IDF outperformed Count Vectorizer, and larger threshold values yielded more consistent performance improvements across datasets, though lower values offered greater potential for gains on large, diverse datasets. These results suggest pseudo-labeling is a viable method for incorporating unlabeled data. Its efficacy depends on dataset attributes, feature extraction methods, and the threshold value.

title: A Secure Real-Time Messaging System Using End-to-End Encryption and Hybrid Key Exchange
abstract: VartaRaksha is a live chat application that was created to guarantee confidential and secure communication between the users. Although most of the current chat programs are encrypted, they still tend to use servers in some of their functionality, which may pose a privacy threat. This initiative is aimed at eliminating such a dependency by means of a real End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) solution. When message is sent through this system, it is encrypted in the device of the sender and can be decrypted only by the target receiver. The server is not involved in accessing the actual data being transported, instead it is involved in relaying messages, where information between users in any form stays a secret. The system encrypts messages with AES-256-GCM that does not only secure the confidentiality of the information but also its integrity. The authentication mechanism can be used to detect any changes to the message when transmitting it. In order to achieve a secure connection between the users, they utilize Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) to produce a shared secret key and it is not transmitted over the network. Along with existing security measures, the system has been planned in consideration of the future threats. It also has a post-quantum cryptography solution based on Kyber to address any threats posed by quantum computing. This hybrid approach enhances the overall system security and increases the resilience of the system in the long run. VartaRaksha is, thus, a trustworthy, safe, and progressive remedy to the digital communication in the present day.

In order to achieve a secure connection between the users, they utilize Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) to produce a shared secret key and it is not transmitted over the network. Along with existing security measures, the system has been planned in consideration of the future threats. It also has a post-quantum cryptography solution based on Kyber to address any threats posed by quantum computing. This hybrid approach enhances the overall system security and increases the resilience of the system in the long run. VartaRaksha is, thus, a trustworthy, safe, and progressive remedy to the digital communication in the present day.

title: Multiphoton diagnostics utilizing entangled photons
authors: Sandia National Laboratories (SNL-CA), Livermore, CA (United States)
abstract: Laser-based nonlinear optical spectroscopy approaches have enabled the direct sensing of important chemistry in nearly every fundamental or applied field of science.Yet in many applications, increased detectivity is needed to unravel fundamental mechanisms.One possibility is the use of quantum entanglement to increase detection cross-sections, but it is unproven that enhancement from quantum light extends to practical intensities for chemical sensing.In this report, we investigate the quantum advantage for second harmonic generation nonlinear optical mixing.We observe quantum enhanced mixing probabilities for entangled photon pairs from 50 to 400 times greater than the classical nonlinear mixing probability, and we quantify this advantage over a range of photon flux from a 10-nanosecond entangled-pair pulsed laser source.The total second harmonic generation output over this flux ranged from 80 to 20 nW respectively.

title: Enhancing Explainable AI with Diverse Counterfactual Explanations (DiCE) for Transparent Stroke Risk Assessment
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) is growing in demand, more in areas like healthcare, where understanding of the model, accountability and trust are essential. Though black-box models with their very good predictive capability, their limit in transparency, delay acceptance in clinical environment. In the following study, we familiarize a model that is understandable for stroke risk estimation through Diverse Counterfactual Explanations (DiCE) to present modified, human-interpretable clarifications of model predictions.A comparison of multiple machine learning algorithms was conducted, the analysis displayed superior predictive performance in the Random Forest classifier relative to other methods assessed. A real-world healthcare dataset was chosen, the Random Forest model was trained on that and to overcome the issue of class imbalance the Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied during preprocessing. The model finally achieved an accuracy of 96.30% indicating the robust performance.The integration of DiCE, we have derived from different and actionable counterfactual explanations that expose minimal yet meaningful modifications required to change the models predictions. These are grounded in clinically relevant features such as age, BMI, and glucose level, thereby enhancing both the usability and interpretability of the model.The proposed framework validates that counterfactual explanations not only improve model transparency but also provision clinical decision-making by giving importance to key modifiable risk factors.

title: Innovation in teaching mode of wireless body area network-driven preventive medicine：a case study of intelligence and emergency response
abstract: As the digital transformation of public health accelerates and the demand for emergency response surges, preventive medicine education urgently needs to integrate technological innovation in response to global health challenges. This paper proposes leveraging wireless body area network (WBAN) technology to innovate the teaching mode of preventive medicine (focusing on intelligence and emergency response), provides an in-depth argument for its pedagogical suitability, and, drawing on teaching cases, systematically designs an instructional application plan. The plan covers implementation pathways, key issues and countermeasures, expected outcomes, and evaluation mechanisms, with the aim of enhancing students’ capabilities in applying intelligent technologies and responding to emergencies, thereby offering an innovative pathway for cultivating top-notch interdisciplinary talents in public health.

title: Lightweight deep learning models for histopathological image analysis in resource-constrained healthcare environments
abstract: Histopathological images analysis is an essential task in diagnosing cancer, but the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in computational pathology is often constrained by the heavy computational demands of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and pathology foundation models due to their computational cost, memory requirements, inference time, and infrastructural needs. This review explores the role of lightweight deep learning models in histopathological image analysis in terms of their diagnostic accuracy, computational efficiency, explainability, and deployability in resource-constrained healthcare environments. Recent advancements in lightweight CNNs, compact ViTs, hybrid CNN-Transformer architectures, efficient attention mechanisms, and optimization algorithms were discussed. The paper also addresses the issue of benchmark histopathology datasets, evaluation procedures, and the necessity of reporting not only clinical performance but also computational metrics like parameters, floating-point operations per second (FLOPs), inference time, memory usage, and the platform for deploying the model. Issues such as insufficient amounts of annotated data, staining, and scanner variability, domain shift between institutions, poor external validation, inadequate explainability, and lack of benchmarking are among the key challenges mentioned. In general, the review indicates that there is an effective way towards scalable, interpretable, and clinically useful computational pathology, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare environments where accuracy must be balanced with efficiency and real-world deployability.

title: Verifiable quantum advantage in extremely low depth
abstract: We give a sampling problem that is solvable by shallow quantum circuits, hard for polynomial-time classical algorithms under lattice-based assumptions, and efficiently verifiable by a classical computer. The quantum sampler admits two implementations: one uses log-logarithmic-depth quantum circuits with one- and two-qubit gates, i.e., $\mathsf{QNC}^0[\log\log]$ circuits, while the other uses constant-depth quantum circuits with unbounded fan-in gates, i.e., $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuits. Our construction can be seen as compiling the Learning with Errors (LWE)-based single-round proof of quantumness of Arabadjieva et al. (2025) to very low depth. The price paid for this compilation is the reliance on less standard, though well-motivated, assumptions: in addition to the lattice knowledge assumption used by Arabadjieva et al. (2025), we require a strengthened variant of the adaptive-hardcore-bit property of LWE, for which we provide supporting evidence. Unlike previous low-depth proofs of quantumness, the quantum computation here requires no mid-circuit measurements or feed-forward: it consists only of running a shallow circuit and sampling from its output distribution. This shows that shallow quantum circuits have sufficient structure to solve certain classically hard tasks whose solutions can be verified efficiently.

title: CMRVision: A Foundation Model for Cardiac MR Image Analysis
abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging provides complementary information on cardiac anatomy, function, and tissue characterization across multiple sequences and views. In this work, we investigate foundation model pretraining for 2D CMR and introduce CMRVision, a CMR-specific foundation model trained using DINOv3-style self-supervised learning on a multi-center, multi-sequence cohort of 36 million CMR images. We systematically evaluate architectural and training design choices for domain-specific pretraining. CMRVision is evaluated on two downstream tasks: multi-task segmentation across cine, late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), and mapping sequences, and cine view classification. Our experiments show that CMR-specific pretraining, smaller patch sizes, and patch-level objectives consistently improve downstream performance. Across a multi-task segmentation benchmark, CMRVision achieved the strongest overall performance, outperforming prior natural-image (NI), medical-image, supervised, and CMR foundation model baselines. Improvements were modest but consistent across structures and sequences, with Dice scores ranging from 0.940-0.967 for LV and 0.855-0.905 for myocardium, and reaching 0.929 for RV, 0.920 for LA, and 0.931 for RA. The largest gains were observed for myocardium segmentation in LGE and mapping images. In a zero-shot segmentation task on unseen LGE long-axis views, the model achieved an average Dice score of 0.692, demonstrating cross-view generalization. For cine view classification, CMRVision achieved the highest average accuracy (0.906), compared to prior methods reported in the literature. These results highlight the potential of CMRVision to support robust and generalizable cardiac MRI analysis across multiple sequences and views.
