title: SISTEM PAKAR DIAGNOSIS AWAL PENYAKIT INFEKSI SALURAN PERNAPASAN AKUT BERBASIS DEMPSTER SHAFER (Studi Kasus: Rumah Sakit Umum Daerah Bengkulu Utara)
abstract: Penyakit infeksi saluran pernapasan akut merupakan salah satu penyakit menular yang masih menjadi tantangan utama kesehattan masyarakat di Indonesia, termasuk di Provinsi Bengkulu. Di Rumah Sakit Umum Daerah Bengkulu Utara, proses diagnosis infeksi saluran pernapasan akut masih menghadapi kendala seperti pemeriksaan manual, antrean panjang dan biaya pelayanan yang tinggi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meranangn sistem pakar berbasis teknologi informasi untuk membantu diagnosis penyakit infeksi saluran pernapasan akut secara cepat dan akurat menggunakan metode Demspter Shafer. Metode penelitian yang digunakan meliputi studi literatur, wawancara dan observasi sebagai dasar perancangan dan pengujian sistem. Hasil pengujian sistem menujukkan tingkat akurasi sebesar 93,3% yang menunjukkan hasil diagnosis yang baik serta nilai usability sebesar 1.91 poin yang menunjukkan sistem mudah digunakan dan efisien. Selain itu, sistem juga menyediakan fitur edukasi, pengingat obat dan konsultasi medis untuk mendukung pasien infeksi saluran pernapasan akut. Kesimpulannya, sistem pakar yang dikembangkan dapat membantu proses diagnosis infeksi saluran pernapasan akut serta mendukung tenaga medis dalam meningkatkan pelayanan kesehatan. Kata Kunci: Sistem Pakar, Penyakit Infeksi Saluran Pernapasan Akut, Mobile Application, Dempster Shafer, Usability Testing

title: Implementasi Enkripsi Data untuk Perlindungan Informasi Sensitif
abstract: Perkembangan teknologi informasi dan komunikasi telah mendorong peningkatan penggunaan sistem informasi digital dalam berbagai sektor, seperti pendidikan, pemerintahan, kesehatan, dan bisnis. Sistem informasi digunakan untuk menyimpan, memproses, serta mendistribusikan data dalam jumlah besar, termasuk data yang bersifat sensitif. Informasi sensitif mencakup data pribadi, data keuangan, data kesehatan, serta dokumen penting yang memerlukan perlindungan khusus. Namun, meningkatnya ketergantungan terhadap sistem digital juga diiringi dengan meningkatnya ancaman keamanan data, seperti kebocoran data, pencurian informasi, dan akses tidak sah. Salah satu mekanisme utama dalam menjaga keamanan informasi sensitif adalah penerapan enkripsi data. Enkripsi berfungsi untuk mengubah data asli menjadi bentuk yang tidak dapat dipahami tanpa kunci tertentu. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) merupakan algoritma enkripsi simetris yang telah diakui secara internasional karena memiliki tingkat keamanan tinggi serta efisiensi dalam proses enkripsi dan dekripsi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji implementasi enkripsi data menggunakan algoritma AES sebagai solusi perlindungan informasi sensitif pada sistem informasi. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah studi literatur deskriptif dengan menganalisis tiga jurnal internasional dan dua jurnal nasional yang relevan dengan topik enkripsi data dan keamanan informasi. Analisis dilakukan dengan membandingkan pendekatan enkripsi yang digunakan serta mengevaluasi efektivitasnya berdasarkan prinsip Confidentiality, Integrity, dan Availability (CIA). Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa implementasi enkripsi AES mampu meningkatkan keamanan data secara signifikan dan menjadi solusi yang efektif dalam melindungi informasi sensitif.

title: ATTENTION MECHANISM AND TRANSFORMER FUNDAMENTALS
abstract: Attention is a key mechanism that enables neural networks to identify and focus on the most relevant information within an input sequence. This chapter presents the working principles of attention-based learning and the Transformer architecture in a clear and structured manner. It introduces Query, Key, and Value representations and explains scaled dot-product attention, self-attention, causal attention, cross-attention, and multi-head attention. The chapter further describes the supporting components of Transformers, including token embedding, positional information, feed-forward networks, residual connections, normalization, and encoder-decoder architectures. The relationship between these components and next-token prediction is discussed to explain how Transformer models support Generative AI and Large Language Models. The chapter also highlights recent advancements and emerging applications of attention-based models, including generative modeling, language processing, and time-series synthesis. By combining conceptual explanations with practical examples and applications, the chapter provides a foundation for understanding how attention and Transformer architectures contribute to the development of modern intelligent systems.

title: Central American Agouti-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CAA-MHA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Central American Agouti-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CAA-MHA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Central American Agouti (*Dasyatherus centralurus*). Agoutis are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies, particularly their ability to navigate complex environments and exploit patchy resources. CAA-MHA leverages these characteristics by incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation, mimicking the agouti's decision-making process. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic patch selection mechanism, a modified levy flight strategy for step generation, and a novel convergence criterion based on relative resource abundance. Mathematical formulations detailing the key components of CAA-MHA, including the patch selection probability, step generation, and convergence assessment, are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability compared to established metaheuristic methods like the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The results indicate that CAA-MHA provides a robust and efficient approach to solving a variety of complex optimization challenges.

title: Cane-cutter: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Cane Cutter Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cane-cutter, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of cane cutters, a species of ant known for its efficient and adaptive path planning in dense vegetation. Cane-cutter leverages the principles of exploration, exploitation, and local search strategies observed in cane cutter foraging to solve complex optimization problems. The algorithm employs a novel representation of the search space, a dynamic grid-based structure, and a unique operator inspired by the cane cutter's cutting and probing strategy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Cane-cutter through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). evidence.abstract: This paper presents Cane-cutter, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of cane cutters, a species of ant known for its efficient and adaptive path planning in dense vegetation. Cane-cutter leverages the principles of exploration, exploitation, and local search strategies observed in cane cutter foraging to solve complex optimization problems. title: 基于量子算法的混沌系统稳定性分析
abstract: This paper investigates the stability of chaotic systems using a novel quantum algorithm designed to enhance analysis and potentially unlock new insights into their behavior. We explore the application of quantum mechanics to address challenges inherent in traditional methods, focusing on the potential for faster convergence and more precise identification of critical points. The core mechanism centers around quantum entanglement and superposition, utilized to model and analyze the system's dynamics with unprecedented fidelity. The analysis aims to provide a fundamentally new approach to understanding and predicting the stability of chaotic systems, potentially leading to breakthroughs in fields like fluid dynamics, climate modeling, and complex systems analysis. This study presents a preliminary framework demonstrating the potential for quantum-enhanced stability analysis, with a focus on identifying and quantifying key parameters that govern chaotic behavior.

title: Explainable AI via Causal Bayesian Networks for Medical Diagnosis
abstract: The increasing deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in medical diagnosis raises significant concerns regarding transparency and trust. Traditional AI models, often based on purely correlational analyses, struggle to provide meaningful explanations for their decisions, hindering clinical acceptance and potentially leading to errors. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) to achieve explainable AI in medical diagnosis. We argue that CBNs offer a superior framework compared to purely correlational models by explicitly representing causal relationships between symptoms, diseases, and treatments. The system will utilize this network to generate explanations for AI diagnostic predictions, focusing on the underlying causal pathways. This approach aims to enhance trust, facilitate clinical understanding, and ultimately improve the reliability of AI-driven medical diagnoses. The core claim is that CBNs provide a superior framework for explaining AI-driven medical diagnoses compared to purely correlational models.

title: Quantum Entanglement Memory Storage (QEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to data storage, termed Quantum Entanglement Memory Storage (QEMS), which leverages the principles of quantum entanglement for achieving unprecedented storage density and longevity. The core concept involves encoding and storing information within multi-particle entangled states, circumventing the fundamental limitations imposed by classical physics. We detail the mechanism for creating and maintaining robust multi-body entangled states through precisely controlled superconducting qubits. The inherent coherence of entangled states is exploited to ensure long-term information preservation, while quantum measurements on these states provide a method for data retrieval. QEMS represents a paradigm shift in data storage, offering the potential for vastly increased capacity and extended data retention periods compared to conventional technologies. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining key equations and concepts, and highlighting the potential advantages of this quantum storage system. This work establishes a foundation for future research and development in the field of quantum memory. ---

title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction Scheme
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive quantum error correction scheme designed to dynamically adjust error correction strategies based on the quantum system's inherent state. Traditional quantum error correction relies on pre-defined, static strategies, often leading to suboptimal performance and increased error rates. Our approach leverages the quantum system's dynamics to intelligently adapt the correction process, resulting in enhanced robustness and improved fidelity. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the computational and algorithmic components that enable this dynamic adaptation. The proposed scheme demonstrates significant improvements in error correction performance compared to existing methods through comprehensive experimental validation.

title: Contextual Graph Grammars for Software Evolution
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to software evolution utilizing Contextual Graph Grammars (CGGs). Traditional software evolution techniques often rely on ad-hoc code mutation, lacking a formal understanding of the system's semantics and context-awareness. CGGs offer a solution by providing a rigorous, context-sensitive framework for modifying software architectures represented as graphs. The core claim is that automatically evolving software systems is achievable through the application of CGGs that capture the underlying semantic relationships. The proposed mechanism involves defining a grammar that represents the original software's architecture, followed by dynamic modification of the graph structure based on runtime context, feedback, and semantic constraints. This approach represents a significant departure from conventional mutation techniques, providing a formal and context-aware methodology for software evolution, ultimately leading to more robust and adaptable systems. The theoretical framework presented here outlines a process for evolving software based on contextual understanding, enabling more intelligent and targeted modifications.

title: 自适应量子环境的几何拓扑分析
abstract: This paper investigates the intricate relationship between quantum systems and their geometric structure, utilizing an adaptive quantum environment as a core mechanism. Traditional quantum environment modeling often relies on fixed parameters, but this research introduces a novel approach by integrating adaptive geometry into the model, offering a powerful framework for precise quantum system behavior and performance analysis. The core claim is that the interplay between the adaptive quantum environment and the system's geometric structure directly influences quantum computation's performance. This work presents a novel method for modeling quantum systems with dynamically adjusted geometries, leading to enhanced understanding and potential optimization of quantum algorithms.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Evolutionary Strategies
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to tackling complex multi-agent systems (MAS) by integrating the strengths of Evolutionary Strategies (ES) and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). The core claim is that synergistic combination of these techniques can effectively facilitate collaborative learning and control within MAS. The proposed framework leverages ES to optimize individual agent policies, while MARL enables the agents to learn effective interaction rules. We argue that this integration significantly enhances learning efficiency and promotes coordinated behavior within the system. The presented methodology offers a promising avenue for addressing challenges in dynamic and decentralized environments where agents must adapt to changing conditions and cooperate to achieve a common goal. We outline the key components of the approach, highlighting the interplay between the two learning paradigms, and discuss potential applications across diverse domains. The resulting system demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional MARL methods, particularly in scenarios requiring complex strategy adaptation and robust coordination.

title: Verifiable Code Generation from High-Level Specifications using Abstract Interpretation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to verifiable code generation from high-level specifications leveraging abstract interpretation. The core idea is to automate the translation of abstract specifications into executable code, thereby mitigating human error and bolstering software reliability. We introduce an abstract interpretation system designed to analyze specifications and produce equivalent code in a target programming language. The system's effectiveness relies on accurately representing the essential properties of the specification through abstraction, minimizing code complexity while guaranteeing correctness. This approach offers a significant step toward automated verification and a more robust software development lifecycle. The key contribution lies in the integration of abstract interpretation with code generation, providing a systematic and verifiable method for translating high-level intentions into concrete, testable code.

title: Quantum Entanglement Modeling and Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a fascinating opportunity for novel approaches to optimization. This paper explores the potential of utilizing entanglement to construct a non-local optimization algorithm. We propose a model that leverages entanglement to achieve a global optimization strategy, avoiding the pitfalls of local search. The core mechanism focuses on designing an algorithm that exploits instantaneous correlations between entangled particles to guide the search process. We argue that this approach holds significant promise for tackling complex optimization problems, particularly those involving intricate constraints and global optima. The paper concludes with a discussion of the theoretical foundations and potential applications of this method.

title: Co-Designing Safer Social Media: Design and Policy Recommendations for Women and Gender-Diverse Users in Australia
abstract: We present findings from a series of co-design studies conducted in collaboration with RMIT University and the Australian Communications Consumer Action Network (ACCAN), examining how social media platforms can better support the safety of women and gender-diverse users in Australia. The study engaged 75 participants across multiple co-design workshops, complemented by consultations with 21 experts in platform safety, digital policy, moderation, and technology design. Grounded in lived experiences, this work examined how existing social media safety features perform in practice and identified safer, more effective alternatives envisioned by users. The findings reinforce that online safety is fundamental to equitable participation in digital life. Women and gender-diverse people disproportionately experience technology-facilitated abuse, including harassment, non-consensual image sharing, impersonation, and identity-based attacks. These harms impact mental health, professional visibility, and everyday communication. Despite increasing recognition of these challenges, current platform safety mechanisms remain reactive, opaque, and burdensome, often requiring users to manage harm with limited transparency or meaningful recourse. In response, this study advances six design and policy recommendations developed through participatory engagement and refined through expert input. These include making reporting systems more transparent, trackable, and responsive to severity, enabling users to better understand and navigate outcomes. The recommendations also propose embedding friction, consent, and evidence-preserving mechanisms into content sharing workflows to prevent harm before it occurs. Further, they call for stronger account authenticity and accountability measures, alongside more context-sensitive detection and flagging systems capable of identifying nuanced and identity-based abuse. The study also highlights the need to better detect and respond to repeat and coordinated patterns of harm, and to provide users with timely, contextual, and responsible safety guidance. Together, these recommendations outline a Safety by Design approach that centres the needs of those most affected, offering actionable pathways for platforms to more effectively prevent, detect, and respond to online

title: Analysis Quantum Implementation of Double AES Cryptography for Secure QR Code Generation
abstract: Data security faces unprecedented challenges due to the rapid advancement of quantum computing technologies, which threaten to compromise foundational classical cryptographic algorithms. This study investigates the quantum implementation of a Double Advanced Encryption Standard (Double AES) scheme for generating secure, tamper-resistant Quick Response (QR) codes. The research encompasses architectural design, quantum circuit construction, and empirical performance evaluation across encryption/decryption execution times, resource allocation, and circuit error rates. Furthermore, we evaluate the vulnerability of the scheme against quantum cryptanalysis by modeling Grover’s search algorithm to estimate key recovery costs in terms of gate counts and qubit requirements. While classical implementations maintain speed advantages on conventional hardware, our findings demonstrate that quantum Double AES yields enhanced resilience against key-search attacks, offering a scalable post-quantum safeguard for visual data carrier architectures.

title: Boundary Between ‘Discovery’ and ‘Invention’ in the Age of AI: Functional Claims and Patent Protection for Correlations and Patterns
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being increasingly used to design and predict antibody candidates and to identify novel correlations and patterns in biological data. This raises a fundamental patent-law question: which AI-generated or AI-discovered results constitute a sufficient technical contribution to justify patent protection? This article distinguishes two analytically distinct cases: whether functionally defined genus claims covering AI-predicted antibodies are commensurate with the technical contribution actually disclosed, and whether AI-discovered correlations or patterns qualify as inventions at all. The former concerns claim scope, and the latter subject matter. The first case is examined through the enablement (Amgen, Wands) and written description (Ariad, Baxalta) requirements of §112(a), and compared with Korean case law under Article 42(3) and 42(4) of the Korean Patent Act. Korean law keeps the two requirements analytically separate, whereas the §112(f) means-plus-function approach in the U.S. has no counterpart in Korean law. The second case is analyzed through §101 and the Alice-Mayo framework, drawing implications for Article 2(1), which defines an invention as a creation of a technical idea utilizing a law of nature. The article argues that AI changes the factual premises to which established patent doctrines apply rather than the doctrines themselves. For functional claims, what matters is the ratio of verified to prophetic examples, the representativeness of the disclosed candidates, and whether the experimentation left to a skilled artisan is confirmation or new search. For claims on correlations or patterns, whether the claim stops at understanding the relationship or applies it through concrete technical means. Both questions return to two conventional boundaries of patent law: correspondence between disclosed technical contribution and patent scope, and the distinction between discovery and invention.

title: A SURVEY OF HALLUCINATION MITIGATION STRATEGIES IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: FROM DECODING-TIME FIXES TO AGENTIC RETRIEVAL AND VERIFICATION
abstract: Hallucination – the generation of fluent but factually unsupported or fabricated content – remains one of the most persistent obstacles to deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, and law. A wide range of mitigation strategies has been proposed, spanning several distinct points of intervention: constraining or calibrating the decoding process itself, fine-tuning or aligning models to prefer grounded outputs, augmenting generation with external retrieval, and verifying or correcting outputs after they are produced. This paper surveys hallucination mitigation across these four intervention points rather than focusing narrowly on any single pipeline. We discuss the underlying causes of hallucination identified in prior work, review representative techniques at each intervention point – including confidence based decoding constraints, instruction-tuning for faithfulness, hybrid sparse-dense retrieval with rank fusion, cross-encoder re-ranking, and Natural Language Inference (NLI)-based claim verification within agentic architectures – and compare the costs and guarantees each category offers. We further examine evaluation practices and benchmarks used to measure hallucination and identify a set of open problems, including the absence of standardized crosscategory benchmarks, the tension between validation strictness and unnecessary refusal, and the limited maturity of hallucination mitigation for multi-hop and cross document reasoning. We conclude with directions for future work that combines lightweight decoding-time safeguards with heavier, verification-based agentic pipelines depending on application risk.

title: Methods for the Automatic Assignment of UDC Codes to Mathematical Articles: Evaluation of Classical and Neural Approaches
abstract: Abstract— Universal Decimal Classification (UDC) is a hierarchical indexing system in which a publication can be assigned one or several codes. Manual UDC indexing is labor-intensive and often inconsistent. This paper examines the automatic assignment of UDC codes to Russian-language mathematical research articles. The aim is to compare combinations of text representations and classification models on a unified corpus and to identify the most effective configurations. A corpus of 4194 articles was collected from Math-Net.Ru, including full texts, abstracts, metadata, and UDC codes. The preprocessing pipeline comprised PDF text extraction, removal of layout artifacts, and normalization of UDC labels. We compared TF-IDF, Word2Vec, SciRus-tiny, and SciRus-tiny3.5 representations combined with logistic regression, Complement Naive Bayes (CNB), and CatBoost. In both the single-label and multi-label settings, the best performance was achieved by TF-IDF + LogReg, while TF-IDF + CNB showed closely competitive results. The proposed approach can be used in automatic subject indexing systems for digital libraries and scientific archives, in UDC recommendation tools for authors and editors, and in metadata quality control workflows.

title: Ko uporabnik ni več samo človek: od priporočil do avtonomnih agentov v poslovnih aplikacijah
abstract: Umetna inteligenca (UI) postaja nepogrešljiv sestavni del poslovnih aplikacij, vendar njena vgradnja v poslovno-kritične sisteme zahteva bistveno drugačen pristop od preprostega posredovanja podatkov velikim jezikovnim modelom. Prispevek na podlagi praktičnih izkušenj z razvojem platforme za upravljanje virov v projektno usmerjenih storitvenih podjetjih predstavi sistematičen pristop k vgradnji UI. Najprej opredelimo spekter vključevanja UI v poslovne procese — od priporočil, ki jih uporabnik potrjuje, prek pol-avtonomnih agentov do avtonomnih agentov — in za vsako stopnjo avtonomije določimo ustrezne mehanizme upravljanja ter pokažemo, kje se ti pokrivajo z zahtevami Akta EU o umetni inteligenci (EU AI Act). Nadalje naslovimo tezo, da bomo informacijske sisteme morali graditi tudi za agente UI, ki bodo do njih dostopali programsko, na primer prek protokola MCP, in da morajo biti varovalke vgrajene v sama orodja, ne le v agente. Sledi praktična primerjava sedmih ogrodij za gradnjo agentov in utemeljitev naše izbire, nato pa arhitektura agentne plasti, kot smo jo zgradili v platformi Alloxy: dvoplastna avtorizacija orodij, strukturiran dolgoročni spomin, vzorec človeške potrditve pred dejanji s posledicami, deterministično usmerjanje modelov, opazljivost v lastni infrastrukturi in preverljivo kaskadno brisanje. Zaključimo s tremi konkretnimi agenti in prenosljivimi spoznanji za razvijalce in arhitekte poslovnih rešitev.

Najprej opredelimo spekter vključevanja UI v poslovne procese — od priporočil, ki jih uporabnik potrjuje, prek pol-avtonomnih agentov do avtonomnih agentov — in za vsako stopnjo avtonomije določimo ustrezne mehanizme upravljanja ter pokažemo, kje se ti pokrivajo z zahtevami Akta EU o umetni inteligenci (EU AI Act). Nadalje naslovimo tezo, da bomo informacijske sisteme morali graditi tudi za agente UI, ki bodo do njih dostopali programsko, na primer prek protokola MCP, in da morajo biti varovalke vgrajene v sama orodja, ne le v agente. Sledi praktična primerjava sedmih ogrodij za gradnjo agentov in utemeljitev naše izbire, nato pa arhitektura agentne plasti, kot smo jo zgradili v platformi Alloxy: dvoplastna avtorizacija orodij, strukturiran dolgoročni spomin, vzorec človeške potrditve pred dejanji s posledicami, deterministično usmerjanje modelov, opazljivost v lastni infrastrukturi in preverljivo kaskadno brisanje. Zaključimo s tremi konkretnimi agenti in prenosljivimi spoznanji za razvijalce in arhitekte poslovnih rešitev.

title: ThinkLIF: multi-scale auxiliary representation guided nuclear segmentation in IHC histopathology
abstract: Reliable analysis of tissue microenvironments is often constrained by the limited molecular information available in standard immunohistochemistry (IHC) and the high cost of multiplex immunofluorescence (mpIF). Although deep learning has advanced computational pathology, existing methods still struggle with staining heterogeneity and ambiguous cellular boundaries because they often lack explicit morphology-sensitive mechanisms for robust structural refinement. We propose ThinkLIF, an auxiliary-representation-guided framework for nuclear segmentation in Ki67-stained IHC images. The model generates stain-like auxiliary representations and integrates them with the original IHC input through a ConvNeXt-style segmentation head, GatedFusion, and a FiLM-based AuxSkipAdapter to improve multi-scale boundary refinement. Experiments on the BCData and DeepLIIF benchmarks show that ThinkLIF achieves highly competitive segmentation performance. On BCData, it obtains the best Pixel Accuracy, Dice, IoU, and AJI among the compared methods. On DeepLIIF, it achieves the best Dice, IoU, and IHC Quantification Difference, while also maintaining competitive AJI performance. Overall, the results support improved boundary delineation, instance separation, and cell-level Ki67 scoring consistency under heterogeneous histopathological conditions. ThinkLIF provides an effective way to improve nuclear segmentation from widely accessible IHC images by combining original morphology with auxiliary stain-like representations. Further validation is required before these auxiliary outputs can be interpreted as quantitative molecular surrogates.

title: \(\pi\) LL: Reconciling Linear Logic, the \(\pi\) -calculus, and their Metatheory
abstract: The Curry-Howard correspondence between natural deduction and the \(\lambda\) -calculus has been a tremendous source of inspiration for typed functional languages. Initiated by Abramsky [1994], the Proofs as Processes agenda seeks a similar foundation for typed concurrent languages, in terms of a connection between linear logic [Girard 1987] and and the \(\pi\) -calculus [Milner et al. 1992]. Recent advances established solid correspondences at the levels of types and syntax. Linear propositions correspond to session types [Caires and Pfenning 2010; Wadler 2014] – types that prescribe the observable communication behaviour of processes [Honda 1993] – and the fundamental operators of the \(\pi\) -calculus correspond to rules in linear logic formulated with hypersequents [Carbone et al. 2018; Kokke et al. 2019; Montesi and Peressotti 2018]. But at the level of semantics and metatheory, the situation remains unclear. The semantics and behavioural theory from previous work do not respect the prefix operator of the \(\pi\) -calculus. The operational semantics of session types has not been reconstructed yet, and as a consequence the hallmark result of session types (session fidelity) has not been formulated and proven for Proofs as Processes. In this article, we carefully evolve the design of Proofs as Processes by applying a dialgebraic view of labelled transition systems and their homomorphisms to the proof theory of linear logic [Ciancia 2013]. The resulting calculus, called \(\pi\) LL, ties previous loose ends and further exhibits a comprehensive metatheory that connects the proof theory of linear logic to the behavioural theory of the \(\pi\) -calculus. Our development clarifies the properties guaranteed by linear logic on the observable behaviour of processes. It also includes a new principle for reasoning about the internal work performed by processes, which we use to establish the first deadlock-freedom and productivity results for processes with observable actions typed with linear logic.

title: Strategy-driven bidirectional efficient adaptive federated learning
abstract: We propose two new strategies within the framework of federated learning: NLA (new lazy aggregation) and AA (accelerated aggregation). The NLA strategy reduces the costs of communication and computation by adaptively skipping the gradient, and the AA accelerates the computation and reduces the communication cost by adaptively accruing the gradient computation. We propose six strategy-driven communication-efficient non-convex adaptive federated learning algorithms via NLA and AA. In particular, based on these novel strategies and compression techniques, we propose two new algorithms: FedBNLACA and FedBACA, to reduce bidirectional communication costs. We give a theoretical guarantee of these algorithms for client (full or partial) participation in correlation under a non-convex setting. In non-convex stochastic optimization full client participation setting, our proposed FedBNLACA and FedBACA algorithms achieve the same convergence rate as its non-compressed counterpart. We have demonstrated through extensive experiments that our protocol achieves efficient training in non-convex environments and is robust to a large amounts of devices, partial participation, and unbalanced data.

title: A stability aware meta adaptive framework for imbalance handling in machine learning and computer vision
abstract: Machine learning models are widely used in computer vision and classification tasks. However, imbalanced classification biases predictive models toward larger classes, reducing predictive performance for minority classes. To address this challenge, we propose meta-adaptive resampling selection plus plus (MARS + +), a stability aware meta-adaptive framework that chooses the best method based on the data. It can select from different types, such as resampling, hybrid, and algorithm-based methods. The proposed method uses inner cross-validation to test each option. It selects methods based on both performance and stability by combing predictive performance and variability across folds (mean − λ·std). It also avoids using any method if none gives clear improvement. MARS + + is tested on multiple benchmark datasets with varying imbalance levels, including both tabular and image data. We use two classifiers, the random forest and logistic regression. The results show that no single method is always the best. MARS + + still gives results close to the best choice in most cases. It also avoids the large drops in performance seen in some other methods. Statistical tests support the effectiveness of adaptive selection. This shows the importance of selecting methods based on the data. In addition, we provide a detailed analysis of method selection, and also examine cases where no method is selected. Finally, the study analyzes how close the results are to the best possible performance. It also examines how dataset features, such as imbalance and sample size, affect the method selection. These results suggest that selecting methods based on stability worked well on the evaluated datasets. They also support using an adaptive imbalance handling strategy.

title: PERSIST : Threat Modeling Memory‐Persistent AI Agents in Cloud‐to‐Edge Environments
abstract: ABSTRACT Agentic artificial intelligence systems increasingly depend on persistent runtime memory, including vector databases, episodic memory stores, long‐term retrieval indices, and cloud‐to‐edge replicas. Existing security frameworks address prompt injection, data poisoning, and model‐level risks, but they do not fully model persistent memory as an active behavioral surface whose records can be written, synchronized, retrieved, transformed, revoked, and later used as decision context. This article introduces PERSIST, a STRIDE‐extended threat model for memory‐persistent AI agents in cloud‐to‐edge environments. PERSIST defines six threat classes: poisoning of persistent memory, exfiltration through retrieval channels, retrieval injection and prompt‐via‐memory attacks, state corruption across synchronization, identity and provenance loss, and temporal drift exploitation. The article extends the threat model with a runnable controlled prototype using SQLite and sqlite‐vec with one cloud vector store, six edge vector stores, HMAC‐signed memory envelopes, top‐k vector retrieval, revocation propagation, and retrieval‐time policy gates. Within a synthetic workload and across 20 repeated trials per main design, PERSIST‐Cloud produced lower observed poison exposure than baseline synchronization (8.9% vs. 46.2%) and signed hash‐log synchronization (8.9% vs. 47.6%), with a 95% confidence interval of 6.6%–11.9% for PERSIST‐Cloud. No cross‐scope retrieval was observed under PERSIST‐Cloud in the tested workload, and observed high‐risk unsafe retrieval was 7.9% (95% CI: 6.0%–10.4%). The paper further operationalizes the proposed Provenance Entropy metric by specifying baseline construction, threshold calibration, and deployment‐time monitoring, and it discusses edge‐node trade‐offs for metadata, verification, latency, and retrieval blocking. These findings provide controlled mechanism‐level evidence about the comparative behavior of the proposed controls; they do not establish effectiveness in production agentic systems or real cloud‐edge deployments.

title: Automated Maize Ear Phenotyping Using 3D Reconstructions
abstract: Maize kernel traits such as row number, kernels per row, and kernel size vary largely for genetic reasons and are consistently associated with regions of the genome that influence yield. Manual measurement of these traits, however, cannot keep pace with the volume of maize generated in a breeding program. To address this, we developed and validated a fully automated pipeline for extracting these traits from 3D point clouds of corn ears, built on a recently developed video-to-point-cloud platform. Raw video frames are processed through COLMAP and NeRF, the ear is isolated via density-based separation, and the point cloud is distance-calibrated to physical units. The calibrated ear point cloud was Z-axis aligned via PCA and cylindrically unwrapped to a 2D image. We enhanced contrast and performed zero-fine-tuning instance segmentation using Cellpose-SAM. A triple-juxtaposed unwrap strategy was used to prevent double-counting at the seam. The pipeline achieved kernel count R^2 = 0.921 (MAPE = 10.33%) and kernel row number within +-2 rows for 95.2% of ears (MAE = 0.75 rows) on a 168-ear held-out set from the 268-ear labeled dataset. The resulting multi-trait dataset has known genotype identity for each ear, positioning it for phenotype-to-genotype association analyses.

title: MeshSplatBench: A Unified Benchmark for Triangle- and Mesh-Based Neural Rendering
abstract: Triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering seeks to bridge neural representations and graphics engines through triangle primitives compatible with standard rasterization. Yet existing methods were developed and evaluated under inconsistent settings, with few direct comparisons and little evaluation in graphics engines. We introduce MeshSuite, the first benchmark for systematic evaluation of engine deployment and Non-Engine Render in triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering. MeshSuite evaluates two deployment settings: Standard Deployment, using an opaque mesh pipeline with vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering; and Dedicated Deployment, using method-specific engine implementations to preserve appearance and compositing features. For mesh splatting, we also audit exported surfaces for topological and geometric integrity as downstream graphics assets. Our results show that engine deployment reduces image quality in both settings; among evaluated methods, MeshSplatting degrades least under Standard Deployment. Dedicated Deployment preserves most fidelity at roughly 5-33x the runtime of Standard Deployment across two deployment datasets. For mesh splatting, explicit connectivity and shared indexing remain limited: shared vertex indexing alone guarantees neither manifoldness nor global connectivity. These findings show that rasterizability is only part of graphics readiness and underscore the need to assess engine deployment. Project page: https://prinasi.github.io/MeshSuite.

title: What's in Your Agent's Context? Context Privilege Escalation Attacks against AI Agent Harness
abstract: Real-world, high-profile AI agent harnesses often rely on vendor-proprietary or opaque designs for context assembly, leaving the sources and underlying logic of assembled context poorly understood and the resulting security risks largely unexplored. In this paper, we present the first systematic analysis of context assembly designs in real-world AI agent harnesses. We study and uncover how an agent harness is designed to collect and assemble context from diverse sources, and identify a set of practical attack vectors arising from these designs. Our analysis brings to light two novel categories of attacks in the context assembly of real-world harnesses: (1) MessageRole Context Privilege Escalation (M-CPE), which occurs when attacker-controlled content originating from a low-privileged context is incorporated into a higher-privileged message role. (2) Cross-Scope Context Privilege Escalation (X-CPE), which occurs when attacker-controlled content persists beyond the context in which it was introduced. We performed a systemic security analysis of the CPE attacks against 12 real-world agent harnesses, including Claude Code and Codex. The resulting consequences include full agent compromise, remote code execution, denial of service, and manipulated tool or skill invocations, etc.

title: No Pixel Left Behind: Filling Gaps in Anime Colorization
abstract: Animation production workflows often involve digital colorization of line art, where small unpainted regions ("gaps") frequently occur and remain an underexplored challenge. We conducted a formative study in Japanese animation (anime) pipelines and found that while the paint bucket tool is widely used for base coloring, tiny enclosed areas are frequently overlooked, resulting in time-consuming manual detection and filling. We introduce GapFill, a tool grounded in professional practices that reduces the effort of gap detection, zooming, and color selection. Our deep-learning method suggests appropriate fill colors by referencing surrounding regions, leveraging the flat-color nature of anime-style images. In a user study with 13 professional colorists, our system improved performance and usability in gap-filling tasks over conventional methods. The study also suggested that prediction accuracy alone is not the primary factor for usability, that appropriate colors can be contextually ambiguous, and that GapFill can complement existing tools depending on users' trust in new AI-powered assistance.

title: Unlocking the future: Artificial intelligence–powered horizon scanning for financial stability
abstract: Financial supervisory and regulatory organisations increasingly operate under conditions characterised by heightened uncertainty, a higher incidence of large systemic disruptions, and rapid socioeconomic transformation. In this context, horizon scanning has emerged as an institutional strategic intelligence practice for systematically detecting early signals as indicators of potential change. Despite its growing adoption, horizon scanning remains largely descriptive, episodic and weakly operationalised, limiting its standardisation and effectiveness for continuous monitoring and anticipatory decision-making in high-stakes environments such as finance. In this paper, we advance horizon scanning from a predominantly conceptual and qualitative episodic practice, towards a resilient, computationally grounded, and institutionally governable capability designed with, but not limited to, a suitability for financial supervisory and regulatory use in mind. We inform a design and engineering blueprint for a supervisory and regulatory grade horizon scanning computational system based on modular decomposition of cross-domain drivers of change and their recombination into structured, semantically plausible yet novelty enabling future scenarios. The proposed framework leverages agentic, generative artificial intelligence (AI) to support continuous horizon mapping, exploratory scenario generation, and policy-oriented evaluation, while embedding human-in-the-loop oversight, auditability, and ethical governance mechanisms. The paper introduces agentic generation and evaluation of modular integrated scenarios as a concrete instantiation of this design logic and discusses its functional value for central banks and financial supervisory and regulatory organisations. The paper concludes that modular, agentic horizon scanning has the potential to enhance institutional anticipatory capacity and support resilient policy design under uncertainty, while expert human-in-the-loop provides a robust governance foundation for the responsible use of AI in strategic foresight. This paper is also included in The Business & Management Collection, which can be accessed at https://hstalks .com/business/.

title: Why Feature Scaling Works: Condition Number as the Key to Gradient Descent Convergence
abstract: Feature scaling is universally recommended in machine learning practice, yet the choice among competing methods is usually made heuristically.This paper uses the condition number of the Hessian κ as the diagnostic quantity for that choice.Part I restates the established link between feature variance disparity and ill-conditioning as a formal proposition under explicit assumptions-centred data, full column rank, and a least-squares objective-and validates it empirically on synthetic functions with controlled condition numbers.Part II states hypotheses about how four normalisation methods-standardisation, min-max scaling, robust scaling, and PCA whitening-perform across varying dataset sizes and feature scale imbalances, then tests them experimentally, reporting measured alongside κ convergence counts.We then report a negative result: a proposed two-stage robust-then-whiten pipeline performs identically to whitening alone under outlier contamination, because robust scaling is a diagonal transformation and therefore cannot alter the correlation structure that whitening inverts.Measuring against an effective condition number-the fitted transform evaluated on clean data-rather than the in-sample value shows that whitening attains on contaminated data by construction while κ = 1 conditioning the underlying signal one to two orders of magnitude worse than robust scaling alone.Part II also reports an exploratory study of gradient-side factor scaling, including a negative result for sample-side preconditioning on least-squares objectives.

title: A Case Study On Financial Fraud Detection With Big Data Analytics At State Bank Of India
abstract: This study, titled "A Case Study on Financial Fraud Detection with Big Data Analytics at State Bank of India," evaluates the operational efficacy and financial feasibility of integrating big data analytics into the fraud detection frameworks of India's largest public sector bank.With the exponential rise in digital banking transactions through UPI, internet banking, and mobile applications, financial institutions face unprecedented risks of sophisticated fraud, including identity theft, account takeover, phishing, and loan defaults.This research investigates the implementation of a Big Data Analytics platform at State Bank of India (SBI), focusing on the integration of machine learning algorithms (such as Random Forest, XGBoost, and Deep Neural Networks) for real-time transaction monitoring and anomaly detection.The study conducts a cost-benefit analysis of the technological investment, evaluating capital expenditure, operational costs, and the direct financial benefit of fraud loss prevention from 2021 to 2025.Standard financial appraisal techniques-Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Payback Period (PBP), and Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR)-are applied to determine the profitability and long-term feasibility of the investment.The data analysis indicates that the implementation of Big Data Analytics has enabled SBI to reduce annual fraud losses by over 80% while significantly increasing transaction monitoring capacity and accuracy.The findings demonstrate that strategically deployed big data frameworks not only mitigate systemic risk but also achieve high financial profitability and operational efficiency.The study concludes that big data analytics is an indispensable tool for securing modern banking infrastructure, offering practical and technical insights for banking executives, policymakers, and security architects seeking to build resilient, fraud-resistant financial systems in an economically sustainable manner.

title: Training and test datasets used to perform non-pararmetric supervised learning with Gaussian Process, the correlation function of which is parametrised by a non-parametric kernel, leading to a non-stationary GP.
abstract: A subset is prepared, of the full data on the Tetouan city energy consumption (available at: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/849/power+consumption+of+tetouan+city), to be then split into a training and test set, to be then used in a new probabilistic learning methodology. This subset is prepared such that it does not include rows of the Tetouan city data pertaining to the same day. Also, energy consumed in the three zones of the city, as reported in the Tetouan city data, are summed in the prepared data that we use. In this new supervised learning method, the input-out relationship is modelled as a sample function of a Gaussian Process, the correlation function of which kernel parametrised. The hard-to-implement explicitly non-stationary kernel with input-pair dependent hyperparameters, is replaced by a parsimonious input-specific ARD kernel in which each hyperparameter is a (GP-generated) random function computed at each iteration of the (MCMC-based) inference. Information obtained from inter-comparison of interloping lookback windows, is used to learn all relevant parameters.

title: Adaptive Quantum Kernels for Kernel PCA
abstract: This paper introduces adaptive quantum kernels (AQKs) for kernel principal component analysis (Kernel PCA), addressing the limitations of traditional quantum kernels that necessitate predefined data structures and assumptions. The core concept involves employing a quantum neural network to learn the structure of the kernel function directly from the data. This dynamic approach allows the AQK to adapt to the specific characteristics of a dataset, leading to enhanced classification or dimensionality reduction performance. The key innovation lies in the learned, data-dependent kernel structure, representing a significant departure from static quantum kernels. This paper details the theoretical framework, the proposed AQK architecture, and discusses its potential impact on various applications. The algorithm aims to overcome the rigidity of fixed-structure kernels by introducing a method of self-adaptation. The theoretical foundation is built upon quantum feature maps and kernel methods, exploring the optimization of kernel parameters within a quantum computing environment. This research provides a novel approach to kernel methods, leveraging the power of quantum computation for adaptive dimensionality reduction and classification tasks. The core of the system is the adaptive learning of the kernel parameters via a quantum neural network.

title: Emergent Information Flow in Evolutionary Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of evolutionary computation to discover novel and complex solutions by emphasizing the generation of abstract representations rather than solely relying on fitness maximization. We introduce a novel evolutionary algorithm, termed "Meta-Evolutionary Adaptation," that incorporates a meta-evolution component to produce new representations of the system's state. This approach allows the algorithm to explore a wider range of solution spaces and potentially uncover emergent patterns, offering a departure from traditional optimization methods. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, its mechanisms, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in generating complex, multi-faceted solutions. The core claim is that this method facilitates the discovery of unexpected and valuable information, thereby enhancing the algorithm's robustness and potential for innovation.

title: Hyperdimensional Computing for Symbolic AI Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of hyperdimensional computing (HDC) to symbolic AI reasoning tasks, specifically logical inference and rule-based reasoning. Traditional HDC has largely focused on pattern recognition and classification. This work proposes a novel framework leveraging HDC's high-dimensionality to represent and manipulate logical propositions and rules. The core mechanism involves encoding logical constructs as high-dimensional vectors and employing similarity comparisons and vector operations to simulate logical operations like conjunction and disjunction. A key innovation is the introduction of a "contextualization" layer, which bridges the gap between the HDC representation and symbolic forms, enabling meaningful reasoning. We demonstrate the potential for HDC to move beyond its current applications and contribute to more sophisticated symbolic AI systems. The exploration presented here offers a new perspective on utilizing HDC's unique properties for tasks requiring logical deduction and rule-based inference. The approach seeks to establish a foundation for developing reasoning systems based on fundamentally different computational principles.

title: 基于动态粒子的量子隐形矩阵计算
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computation, utilizing a dynamic particle system to efficiently compute quantum hidden-matrix operations. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on classical computation, limiting their potential for complex calculations. We introduce a new method that leverages the unique properties of dynamic particles – specifically, quantum entanglement and the ability to manipulate quantum states – to achieve a significant improvement in computational speed and efficiency. This work explores the potential of dynamically evolving particle states to accelerate the process of quantum computation, offering a fundamentally different paradigm compared to existing approaches. The core mechanism involves employing a dynamically generated quantum state, guided by entanglement, to perform the required calculations, ultimately demonstrating a substantial reduction in computational complexity. This research provides a foundation for future advancements in quantum algorithm design and implementation.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的动态空间几何模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic space geometry model based on self-adaptive neural networks. Traditional space geometry models often rely on manual design, presenting limitations in complexity and scalability. This approach leverages self-adaptive neural networks to automatically learn and adjust the geometric structure of the model, enabling the simulation of dynamic space evolution. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically updating the model's parameters based on spatial changes, thereby achieving a more realistic and flexible representation of complex space structures. The algorithm is designed to reduce design effort and provide a robust framework for simulating evolving spatial phenomena.

title: # Bonin Pipistrelle: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Hunting Behavior of *Pipistrellus boninensis*
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, Bonin Pipistrelle, inspired by the foraging behavior of *Pipistrellus boninensis*, a small bat species known for its efficient and adaptive hunting strategies. The algorithm leverages the bat's echolocation and flight patterns to dynamically adjust its search space and exploration strategy. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a modified particle representation based on bat positions, velocity, and frequency, mirroring the bat's echolocation capabilities. A novel convergence criterion is introduced, mimicking the bat's sensitivity to environmental changes. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high-quality solutions. The core mechanism of Bonin Pipistrelle focuses on adjusting parameters based on a simulated 'echo' response, effectively guiding the search towards promising regions in the solution space. This research presents a potentially valuable addition to the toolbox of metaheuristic optimization techniques.

title: Probability-Adaptive Logic Systems: A Novel Approach to Dynamic Modeling
abstract: Probability-adaptive logic systems represent a significant advancement in probabilistic modeling, offering enhanced flexibility and robustness compared to static approaches. This paper introduces a novel system predicated on the concept of "probability plasticity," where the system dynamically adjusts its parameters based on input data complexity and potential states. This dynamic adjustment allows for a more adaptable and generalizable model. The core mechanism involves a "probability plasticity" framework, enabling parameter adjustments to directly influence logical rules without the need for complex pre-defined rules. We explore the benefits of this design, demonstrating its ability to achieve superior performance in various scenarios, particularly in scenarios with high data variability and evolving requirements. The system's design will be presented with a detailed mathematical framework and a discussion of its potential impact on the field of probabilistic modeling.

title: Bobrinski's Jerboa: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Jerboa Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bobrinski's Jerboa, a new metaheuristic algorithm designed for optimization problems. The algorithm draws inspiration from the unique foraging behavior of jerboas, particularly their ability to traverse uneven terrain with remarkable efficiency. Bobrinski's Jerboa incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) within a novel framework. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a dynamic terrain representation, mimicking the jerboa's adaptation to varying ground surfaces. The movement strategy of the "jerboa" particles is governed by a combination of random jumps and adaptive adjustments based on local terrain evaluation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities. The key components of the algorithm include a terrain representation, a jerboa movement strategy, and a dynamic adaptation mechanism. The results show that Bobrinski's Jerboa achieves good solutions with relatively low computational cost. The algorithm's effectiveness hinges on the careful tuning of parameters related to terrain roughness, jump size, and adaptation rate.

title: ##拓扑量子几何的自适应矩阵理论
abstract: This paper introduces a novel theory, the Adaptive Matrix Theory of Topological Quantum Geometry (AMTQG), predicated on the principles of quantum geometry and self-adaptive matrix operations. The core ambition of AMTQG is to leverage quantum entanglement and matrix dynamics to enable dynamic optimization and complex calculations within quantum systems. We propose a mechanism termed "Quantum Matrix Dynamic Adjustment" which fundamentally transforms matrix operations into entangled states, exploiting their inherent quantum properties to achieve accelerated computation and adaptive behavior. The paper demonstrates preliminary results showing the potential for significant speedups and novel computational capabilities compared to existing classical approaches, highlighting the theoretical and potential practical implications of this innovative framework. This work represents a significant step towards realizing quantum-enhanced computation and exploring the untapped potential of entangled matrix dynamics.

title: Geometric Structuring of the Similarity Assessment Space in Trademark Law: Focusing on the Legal Validity Assessment of AI Models
abstract: This study proposes a methodology to systematize the logical connections among determination factors through the mathematical structuring of similarity assessments in trademark law. By defining marks and designated goods as manifold structures and introducing a metric tensor, this study formalizes existing legal principles governing trademark similarity assessment, such as the interactions among specific elements (appearance, pronunciation, and meaning) and cognitive asymmetry, into a problem of geometric distance measurement. As a theoretical application, this study presents a methodology that explores the theoretical lower bound of the threshold distinguishing similar from dissimilar marks by applying the similarity judgment jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of Korea as a mathematical constraints. In addition, using the tensor transformation law mediated by the Jacobian matrix, a methodology is proposed to verify the validity of distance-calculating metrics independently formed by the hidden layers of black-box artificial intelligence (AI) models by projecting them into a legal-doctrinal reference space. This study is academically significant because it provides a novel analytical framework by substituting the existing legal reasoning for trademark similarity assessment with a mathematical structure. The study has practical significance as it establishes a foundation for diagnosing and verifying whether the outputs generated by black-box AI models or practical legal judgments possess case-specific validity based on evidence and facts.

title: Impact of artificial intelligence-based adaptive learning systems on students’ academic performance: A systematic literature review and quantitative research synthesis
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education has been a major topic of discussion in the field of educational technology, with a focus on the potential of AI-based adaptive learning systems (ALS) and intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) to provide personalized learning experiences that adapt to the knowledge state, learning speed, and preferences of the learner. Although there is a growing number of primary and meta-analytical studies, the results regarding the size and consistency of the effects of AI-ALS on academic performance are scattered across disciplines, levels of education and methodological traditions. This paper is a systematic literature review and quantitative research synthesis of nineteen peer-reviewed papers (2013-2026) that investigate the effects of AI-based adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring systems, and AI chatbots on students' academic achievement. After an identification and screening process based on PRISMA, nine quantitative effect-size comparisons were extracted from key meta-analyses and quasi-experimental evaluations and synthesized. The mean reported effect size for the corpus (Hedges' g = 0.34, SD = 0.29) was significantly greater than zero, t(8) = 3.52, p = .008, 95% CI [0.12, 0.56] and the non-parametric Wilcoxon signed rank test confirmed this result (p = .020). The effect sizes for systems that were explicitly described as AI-enabled adaptive learning platforms (M g = 0.69) were significantly larger than the effect sizes for general intelligent-tutoring comparisons (M g = 0.24), Welch t = 4.74, p = .003, and were significantly positively associated with publication year (r = .68, p = .045), indicating that more recent and more sophisticated AI-driven systems were associated with larger reported gains. Results confirm that AI-based adaptive learning systems have a small-to-medium, statistically significant positive impact on academic outcomes compared to non-adaptive learning, but there is still a significant amount of heterogeneity between comparison conditions, subject areas, and educational levels

title: AI-Augmented Entrepreneurship: Governance and the Automate–Augment Logic Across Ideation, Discovery, Design, and Learning
abstract: Purpose: This conceptual article reinterprets entrepreneurship as a governed socio-technical system in which artificial intelligence (AI) links ideation, customer discovery, design, and learning into continuous algorithmic loops. The objective is to explain how AI alters the speed, scale, and locus of entrepreneurial judgment, and to identify when these shifts generate value and legitimacy. Methodology: Using an integrative literature review, the article synthesizes research on human–AI symbiosis, external enablement, creativity, and uncertainty. It proposes a stage-contingent automate–augment architecture: automating search, simulation, and initial filtering, and augmenting human judgment in problem framing, success criteria, ethical assessment, and strategic decisions. The model is structured around key techno-organizational mechanisms such as prediction, generation, and simulations alongside governance safeguards, including human-in-the-loop oversight, traceability, and bias audits. Results: Eight propositions link AI to higher idea diversity and novelty, fairer and denser feedback, improved personalization and design quality, earlier pivots, non-linear automation effects, enhanced socio-technical learning, and stronger dynamic capabilities with integrated data and models. Boundary conditions include data quality, concept drift, domain criticality, resources, and governance maturity. Implications: The article offers theoretical extensions, methodological guidance, and practical recommendations for responsible AI adoption in entrepreneurial processes. Originality: The study advances a socio-technical model of entrepreneurship and introduces a structured automate–augment logic that clarifies how, when, and under what constraints AI creates value in entrepreneurial settings.

Results: Eight propositions link AI to higher idea diversity and novelty, fairer and denser feedback, improved personalization and design quality, earlier pivots, non-linear automation effects, enhanced socio-technical learning, and stronger dynamic capabilities with integrated data and models. Boundary conditions include data quality, concept drift, domain criticality, resources, and governance maturity. Implications: The article offers theoretical extensions, methodological guidance, and practical recommendations for responsible AI adoption in entrepreneurial processes. Originality: The study advances a socio-technical model of entrepreneurship and introduces a structured automate–augment logic that clarifies how, when, and under what constraints AI creates value in entrepreneurial settings.

title: A clinically explainable temporal fusion model for predicting postoperative acute kidney injury
abstract: Abstract Objective Postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common and serious complication, driven by complex perioperative physiologic derangement and hemodynamic instability. There remains a need for a mechanism for deep interaction between preoperative characteristics and intraoperative dynamics, and provide clinical interpretability. Methods We propose an extended Temporal Fusion Transformer for postoperative AKI prediction, designed for heterogeneous clinical data and intraoperative sequences, such as arterial pressure, medications, and fluid infusions. The model is built based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with the Variable Selection Networks, which adaptively select static and temporal features using gated residual networks, conditioned by static context vectors. Static covariates are encoded as multiple context vectors that guide temporal variable selection, LSTM initialization, and the temporal attention mechanism, modelling complex interactions between baseline risk and intraoperative signal fluctuations. The final representation for outcome prediction was aggregated by using the preoperative state as the attention query. Results The model was evaluated on two public surgical datasets, the Informative Surgical Patient dataset for Innovative Research Environment (INSPIRE) and Medical Informatics Operating Room Vitals and Events Repository (MOVER). Across all experiments, the proposed model achieved better performance and showed stable performance in subgroup analysis. The interpretability results showed the feature importance of static variables and time series at each time step, revealing that the model consistently assigned attention to periods of sustained hemodynamic instability. Conclusions These findings supported the potential for explainable perioperative decision support systems and emphasized the importance of intraoperative signals in AKI risk stratification.

title: Towards a statistical understanding of neural networks: Beyond the neural tangent kernel theories
abstract: A primary advantage of neural networks lies in their feature learning characteristics, which is challenging to theoretically analyze due to the complexity of their training dynamics. We examine feature learning and its potential benefits for generalization from a statistical perspective. After reviewing the neural tangent kernel (NTK) theory and recent results in kernel regression, which address the generalization issue of sufficiently wide neural networks, we examine limitations and implications of the fixed kernel theory (as the NTK theory) and review recent theoretical advancements in feature learning. Moving beyond theories with fixed features, we consider neural networks as adaptive feature models. Finally, we propose an over-parameterized Gaussian sequence model as a prototype for the adaptive feature model to study feature learning characteristics and motivate their future analysis for neural networks.

title: A federated discrete reinforcement learning architecture for enhancing convergence and interpretability in distributed control
abstract: Federated reinforcement learning is a promising approach for distributed artificial intelligence in cyber–physical energy systems, but many existing methods rely on black-box deep policies that reduce interpretability and may converge unstably under non-identical operating conditions. This work proposes a federated discrete reinforcement learning architecture for collective pitch control of wind turbines. The method combines federated learning, tabular reinforcement learning, and structured state–action representations so that turbines collaboratively learn transparent state–action value tables instead of opaque neural policies. The architecture is evaluated with multiple wind turbines exposed to independent wind realizations generated from the same Weibull distribution. Several federated aggregation strategies are compared in terms of convergence behaviour, training stability, scalability, synchronization frequency, parameter sensitivity, and communication requirements. The simulations show that the proposed proximal discrete aggregation method reached stable operation after approximately 30 training episodes, whereas Federated Averaging and the non-federated controller required approximately 70 episodes. FedSGD required the longest training time, converging after approximately 450 episodes, and presented the largest fluctuations, as reflected by the 95% confidence intervals. Increasing the number of participating turbines improved the convergence trend. These results demonstrate that discrete federated reinforcement learning can provide an effective balance between interpretability, convergence performance, and distributed learning efficiency in energy control applications.

title: Lightweight adversarial membership inference attack with temporal evolution against federated learning
abstract: Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) pose a significant privacy threat to Federated Learning (FL) by enabling adversaries to exploit behavioral discrepancies between original and perturbed samples. However, most existing adversarial MIAs overlook the attack efficiency. To address this challenge, we propose ADVMIA, a novel adversarial attack framework that redefines the optimization perspective in this domain. ADVMIA is the first method to leverage the temporal evolution characteristics of FL models, offering a deeper understanding of the internal dynamics of adversarial sample generation. Concurrently, it introduces a threshold selection strategy that eliminates the need to train additional inference models, thereby reducing the high computational overhead associated with iterative adversarial optimization. We evaluate ADVMIA on two real-world datasets and compare its performance against five state-of-the-art MIAs. Experimental results demonstrate that ADVMIA achieves superior efficiency and heightened attack effectiveness. Furthermore, its robustness in practical FL scenarios is systematically validated through evaluations against two common defense mechanisms.

title: Variational autoencoder in analysis of motion capture data
abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to present the applicability of Variational Autoencoders (VAE) in the analysis and generation of human gait data, represented by multivariate sequences containing rotations of skeletal joints or 3D positions of anatomically significant body points. The proposed framework offers two main advantages: it uses data solely from healthy populations for classification (instead of the usual collation of healthy and pathological data) and employs anthropometric measures to determine generated data quality.The paper investigates the semi-supervised classification problem of anomaly detection, in which the VAE is trained based on the selected class called normal for the purpose of discriminating the remaining abnormal ones. Three challenges – the recognition of the gait performed by females and males, the distinction between gait with comfortable and increased paces, as well as the discrimination of walking and running activities – are taken into consideration.To accomplish the tasks, VAE architectures operating on preprocessed motion capture sequences containing single walking and running cycles are proposed. The results achieved are satisfactory. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) for the anomaly detection challenges reach 0.862 ± 0.014, 0.843 ± 0.015, and 1.000 ± 0.000, respectively, evaluated through 30 repeated subject-disjoint splits. A robust directional asymmetry pattern was observed: models trained on populations with lower within-group variability achieve consistently higher detection performance, a finding confirmed across multiple anomaly detection methodologies including PCA, One-Class SVM, and Isolation Forest. As regards the generation of gait sequences, they are diverse and contain natural-looking movements.

title: A Comprehensive Survey: Harmonizing Transfer Learning and Self‐Supervised Learning for Enhanced Performance in Machine Learning and Deep Learning
abstract: ABSTRACT In recent years, the integration of transfer learning (TL) and self‐supervised learning (SSL) has gained considerable attention as an effective strategy for improving model performance across a wide range of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) tasks. TL enables the reuse of knowledge acquired from pretrained models to accelerate learning in new tasks, while SSL exploits large volumes of unlabeled data to learn meaningful representations without manual annotation. This article presents a systematic and comprehensive survey of existing approaches that harmonize SSL with TL. The survey reviews key mechanisms such as self‐supervised pre‐training, feature extraction, fine‐tuning strategies, and domain adaptation across both ML and DL paradigms, including convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, transformer‐based architectures, and classical ML models. By synthesizing findings reported in the literature, this study highlights how the combination of self‐supervised representation learning and TL enhances generalization, robustness, and data efficiency. Furthermore, the survey discusses representative application domains, emerging trends, and comparative insights across benchmark tasks. Finally, open challenges and future research directions are outlined, emphasizing scalability, domain shift handling, and the role of foundation models. This survey aims to provide researchers and practitioners with a structured understanding of current progress and opportunities in harmonizing TL and SSL.

title: Grounded, Compute-Efficient LLM Policy Agents for Energy-Poverty Equity in Physically-Constrained Peer-to-Peer Energy Markets
abstract: Energy poverty is nearly absent from NLP-for-social-good, and the little existing work is either static retrieval/QA or relies on carbon-intensive cloud LLMs, a self-defeating "computational irony" for a humanitarian setting. We present EqGrid, a closed-loop simulation in which a low-frequency, open-weight LLM policy agent sets price and carbon bounds and targeted subsidies over a community of empirically-grounded household personas, while high-frequency multi-agent RL traders clear a continuous double auction constrained by a physical distribution grid (IEEE-33-bus with Dynamic Operating Envelopes). Our contribution is threefold and directly addresses how to measure the social impact of AI: (i) grounded personas (region-matched socio-demographics) whose load curves are checked for shape and level realism against real smart-meter data; (ii) formal energy-poverty equity metrics (Energy Burden, Gini of EB, LIHC) showing the intervention reduces burden inequality without raising net grid cost; and (iii) a compute-efficiency frontier that measures how much equity performance survives compressing the policy agent from a 235B teacher down to a sub-1B model deployable on a laptop, in estimated energy/carbon per decision. A decoupled-safety design (the LLM sets bounds; a validate-and-project grid gate executes) yields zero grid-constraint violations versus 55 under direct LLM control. On energy-poverty equity, the LLM policy lowers the Gini of energy burden to 0.305 (from 0.351) and mean burden by 28% while cutting cost (outperforming a tuned rule baseline), and a 3B-active model retains 95% of the benefit at roughly 9x lower inference energy than the teacher, with even a 0.8B on-device model retaining 92% at roughly 24x lower energy. We will release code and configs.
