title: A systematic Approach to constructing a Chance-and-Risk Matrix for Semiconductor Supply Chains
abstract: Semiconductor supply chains face escalating risks from geopolitical tensions, geographic concentration, and rapid technological shifts, yet no scalable system continuously extracts, structures, and prioritizes risk intelligence from public corporate disclosures. We present an end-to-end pipeline that retrieves corporate documents for semiconductor companies and uses large language models (LLMs) to extract the risks and opportunities they describe. It organizes these into a knowledge graph linking each item to its category, sources, and related events, then merges duplicates and ranks them with a three-layer mechanism combining an algorithmic formula, an LLM relevance adjustment, and expert validation. Applied to five companies across the value chain, the pipeline produces 76,207 scored items, of which an independent check finds 92.6% valid. The automated rankings match expert judgment at an average Spearman correlation of 0.55 for risks and 0.72 for opportunities, and the resulting matrices identify trade restrictions as the dominant cross-company risk.

title: Explore Before Committing: Hypothesis-Guided Search for Deep Research Agents
abstract: Deep-research agents answer complex questions by interacting with search and browsing tools, yet they often search along a single evolving trajectory. Our trajectory-level analysis reveals a common failure mode in which the agent may encounter an early search state with several plausible directions, but follow one direction before collecting enough comparative evidence. Once this happens, subsequent tool calls tend to reinforce the same path, increasing the chance of failure when the initial direction is misleading. We further find that successful trajectories reduce this risk through two behaviors: grounding vague exploration in concrete candidates and shifting directions when the current path is weak or incomplete. Based on these findings, we propose HypoSearch, which generates lightweight hypotheses as soft search hints, explores them through bounded independent branches, and compares branch-level evidence before commitment. Across four deep-research benchmarks and three backbone models, HypoSearch consistently outperforms single-trajectory search and standard parallel baselines, improving Qwen3.5-122B from 46.7 to 60.0 on BC-small while using fewer tool calls than five independent trajectories. A pilot supervised fine-tuning study further shows that these behavioral signals can curate compact training trajectories and reduce degradation from unfiltered data.

title: Reaching the optical propagation limit in temporal analog computing
abstract: A central goal of optical computing is to perform calculations on the timescale of light propagation. Yet many analog photonic solvers require feedback, storage or field build-up before the answer becomes available, introducing additional latency that limits real-time operation. Here we introduce the concept of two-time modulation for temporal analog computing, in which the material response is independently modulated along two temporal directions, allowing the computational operator to be constructed continuously as the waveform propagates. The solution can therefore form during optical transit, without an additional solution-formation timescale. This form of temporal control allows identical copies of a waveform separated only in time to reach entirely different target outputs within a single spatial channel, and enables nonlocal integral-equation solving in a single passage. The resulting framework brings compact, programmable, real-time analog computation within reach for ultrafast optical information processing.

title: Causal Evidentiary Governance for High-Risk Machine Learning Systems
abstract: Machine learning systems deployed for credit, hiring, and resource distribution are increasingly subject to regulatory oversight from policies such as the EU AI Act and GDPR. Current fairness governance practices rely on observational fairness metrics, post-hoc explainability, and immutable audit logs, but provide limited support for causal attribution and efficient evidentiary verification. We introduce Causal Evidentiary Governance (CEG), a framework in which regulated institutions commit to a versioned directed acyclic graph (DAG) that partitions causal pathways into allowable and disallowed groups. The Causal Harm Rate measures prediction variation attributable to disallowed causal pathways. Each decision is accompanied by a signed Decision-Evidence Packet (DEP), cryptographically binding the prediction to a digest of the published DAG and path-specific attributions. DEP digests can be appended to a Merkle tree to enable logarithmic-cost inclusion proofs. We validate CEG through a two-layer empirical methodology using demographic summaries from four years of PMA credit supervisory data to construct 10,000 synthetic credit applicants across four strategic DAG counterfactuals. Causal Harm Rate isolates injected causal effects more clearly than demographic parity or equalized odds. Cross-model validation and ablation studies assess robustness. Evaluation on the German Credit dataset shows that harm associated with specific causal pathways can be substantially understated by associational fairness metrics. Finally, a proof-of-concept implementation demonstrates operationally plausible throughput and highlights relevant performance tradeoffs.

title: Predicting Program Exit Code with LLMs and Programming Language Semantics
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown proficiency in various software engineering tasks, such as code generation and translation. However, a key limitation in their performance may be their (lack of) understanding of programming-language semantics. Even when explicit semantics are given, it remains unclear whether LLMs apply those rules or lean on priors learned during pre-training instead. We study if LLMs lean on priors or given semantics with a novel task--Program Executability Prediction (PrEx)--that asks models to predict whether a program is semantically valid or invalid (and, if invalid, which formal rule it violates) given the program's syntax and operational semantics. Because PrEx requires both valid and invalid programs, we build a dataset with systematically generated invalid transformations derived from valid programs. We evaluate open-source coding LLMs under two semantic formalisms and two semantic shifts across Human-Written, LLM-Translated, and Fuzzer-Generated program splits. Our findings show that LLMs lean on pre-training priors rather than systematically applying the given rules, performing especially poorly on modified semantics and degrading further as program complexity increases. PrEx is available at https://github.com/EngineeringSoftware/prex.

title: Phase-Sensitive Cascade Quantum Amplifier with Nearly Noiseless Operation
abstract: Abstract Phase-sensitive parametric devices facilitate quadrature-selective amplification with the possibility for sub-quantum-limited noise performance. In this work, we investigate the operation of a SQUID-based Josephson parametric amplifier (JPA), comparing its gain and noise performance in the phase-preserving and phase-sensitive regimes. The device, fabricated using VTT SWAPS technology, is driven in a three-wave mixing configuration and characterized in a reflection-based measurement setup at millikelvin temperatures. To directly probe the noise performance at low JPA gains, we employ a cascaded amplification scheme in which a traveling-wave parametric amplifier (TWPA) provides low-noise preamplification of the JPA output. In a phase-preserving operation, the JPA exhibits near-quantum-limited performance with a system noise temperature of $$351\pm 53$$ 351 ± 53 mK at 6 GHz. In contrast, phase-sensitive operation yields a minimum system noise temperature of $$94\pm 12$$ 94 ± 12 mK, well below the standard quantum limit of 288 mK. Our results demonstrate that a JPA–TWPA amplifier cascade opens the door to direct, high-fidelity probing of quantum devices without the need for background noise subtraction.

evidence.title: Phase-Sensitive Cascade Quantum Amplifier with Nearly Noiseless Operation
evidence.abstract: Abstract Phase-sensitive parametric devices facilitate quadrature-selective amplification with the possibility for sub-quantum-limited noise performance. In this work, we investigate the operation of a SQUID-based Josephson parametric amplifier (JPA), comparing its gain and noise performance in the phase-preserving and phase-sensitive regimes. The device, fabricated using VTT SWAPS technology, is driven in a three-wave mixing configuration and characterized in a reflection-based measurement setup at millikelvin temperatures. To directly probe the noise performance at low JPA gains, we employ a cascaded amplification scheme in which a traveling-wave parametric amplifier (TWPA) provides low-noise preamplification of the JPA output. In a phase-preserving operation, the JPA exhibits near-quantum-limited performance with a system noise temperature of $$351\pm 53$$ 351 ± 53 mK at 6 GHz. In contrast, phase-sensitive operation yields a minimum system noise temperature of $$94\pm 12$$ 94 ± 12 mK, well below the standard quantum limit of 288 mK. Our results demonstrate that a JPA–TWPA amplifier cascade opens the door to direct, high-fidelity probing of quantum devices without the need for background noise subtraction.

title: SELF-SUPERVISED LEARNING FOR FOUNDATION MODELS
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has become a central strategy for building foundation models because it converts the structure of unlabeled data into training signals. This chapter reviews the conceptual foundations, architectures, learning objectives, data pipelines, applications, challenges, and emerging directions of self-supervised foundation models. It first distinguishes SSL from conventional supervised and unsupervised learning and then examines Transformer, Vision Transformer (ViT), and multimodal architectures. Four major training paradigms are analyzed: autoregressive next-token prediction, masked modeling, contrastive learning, and joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs). The chapter also discusses large-scale data curation, deduplication, tokenization, image patchification, and vector quantization as essential components of foundation-model development. Representative applications in natural language processing, computer vision, multimodal AI, healthcare, robotics, scientific discovery, and industrial monitoring are reviewed. The chapter further examines computational cost, scaling behavior, hallucination, alignment, data quality, and downstream adaptation as continuing research challenges. Finally, it identifies emerging directions including latent-space world models, state-space architectures for long-context processing, hybrid neuro-symbolic systems, efficient adaptation, and trustworthy evaluation. The overall analysis shows that future progress will depend not only on larger models, but also on better objectives, better data, more efficient architectures, and mechanisms that support reliable reasoning and controllability.

title: AI-DRIVEN BUSINESS STRATEGY AND DECISION-MAKING: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES AND EMERGING TRENDS
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology that is reshaping business strategy, organizational processes, and managerial decision making. The integration of AI into business operations enables organizations to process large volumes of structured and unstructured data, identify patterns, predict market developments, automate routine activities, and support evidence based strategic decisions. Unlike traditional information systems that primarily provide historical information, AI enabled systems can generate predictive and prescriptive insights, thereby improving the speed, accuracy, and quality of managerial decisions. This paper examines the role of AI in business strategy and decision making, with particular emphasis on its opportunities, challenges, and emerging trends. The study adopts a conceptual and descriptive research approach based on secondary sources, including academic literature, industry reports, and institutional publications. The paper discusses AI applications in strategic planning, marketing, finance, human resource management, supply chain management, customer relationship management, and risk management. It also examines challenges relating to data quality, algorithmic bias, privacy, cybersecurity, transparency, ethical responsibility, employee displacement, and implementation costs. Emerging developments such as generative AI, AI agents, explainable AI, edge AI, AI powered analytics, and responsible AI are likely to further transform organizational decision making. The study concludes that organizations should view AI not merely as an automation technology but as a strategic capability requiring appropriate governance, human oversight, digital infrastructure, skilled employees, and ethical frameworks.

title: Abusing Vulnerable Drivers to Disable System Defenses: The Case of ThrottleStop
abstract: ThrottleStop.sys is a legitimate driver that has been abused by adversaries in recent years as part of Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attacks to elevate privileges on Windows systems and weaken their defenses by terminating processes associated with Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools. In this paper, we provide a detailed technical analysis of CVE-2025-7771, a vulnerability affecting this driver that was discovered by Kaspersky’s Global Emergency Response Team (GERT). We also present an indepth analysis of an advanced artifact that abuses this vulnerability in real-world attacks. Finally, we review the adversary’s tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) and propose best practices for mitigating this type of threat.

title: From Model to Scenario Engine: A Reproducible ABM for UK Net Zero Analysis
abstract: Agent-based modelling (ABMs) has increasingly been used to study socio-economic transitions. These computational models feature heterogeneous agents, decision-making, and feedback effects that are difficult to capture in aggregate models. Yet, these features that make ABMs valuable also make them hard to reproduce and evaluate as research software, especially when stochastic behaviour is involved. In this talk, we share the software engineering effort to transform a baseline ABM for macroeconomic analysis into a tool for comparing UK Net Zero policy intervention scenarios. The methodology combines design choices, including: Coding economic shocks targeting different economic markets A UK-specific data pipeline Monte Carlo simulation (MC) Reproducibility controls Visualisation dashboards Simulation-based inference (SBI) We show that a more straightforward separation of the main logic from scenario interventions in the code makes it easier to test, maintain, and extend with new economic behaviours. We also explain scenario uncertainty with MC and SBI. Finally, we discuss how dashboards make outputs easier to inspect and compare for both technical and non-technical audiences. Although the work is motivated by UK Net Zero policy analysis, the broader contribution is a dialogue of software engineering practices for making large-scale stochastic ABMs more credible and reusable as research software. The talk will be relevant to anyone working on computational models where scientific value depends as much on implementation rigour as on the underlying theory. In addition to making the ABM applicable to policy analysis, we argue that the design choices improve the model's implementation, enabling better software quality assessments.

title: Societies of Narrow Minds: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of multi-agent and cooperation as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

The parallel coordinate plot created by ParamSearch.show_results() could have incorrect tick labels in some cases. This has been fixed in #2215 by @jeromedockes. title: Warranted Extraction: A Verification Architecture for Machine-Read Coverage Policy
abstract: Large language models can read a payer medical-policy document and produce structured coverage criteria that look right. Nothing in the model's output distinguishes the criteria that are right from the criteria that are invented, and in clinical revenue-cycle use an invented criterion is acted on. We describe an architecture in which an LLM is treated as an untrusted proposer whose output becomes queryable only after a deterministic, separately built verifier has resolved every claim to a verbatim span in a hash-pinned rendering of the source document. Every served criterion carries that span, called a warrant, so any consumer can check any claim against the captured source bytes without trusting the extractor, the operator, or the model vendor. We define three evaluation metrics for this class of system (grounding rate, content recall, and exact-span rate) and report our own numbers, including the one that plateaued. The architecture is disclosed so that it cannot be enclosed; the measurements exist so that "the extraction is good" can be a claim with content.

title: Quantumization of Zero-Knowledge Proofs and Verifiable Computation Circuits
abstract: This paper explores the quantumization of zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) and verifiable computation circuits (VCCs), presenting a novel approach to achieving secure and verifiable execution of quantum computation programs. The core idea involves leveraging quantum circuit hashing techniques to construct ZKP protocols that demonstrate the correctness of a VCC without revealing its underlying structure. This approach addresses a critical need within the burgeoning field of quantum computing – the provision of robust and trustworthy execution validation mechanisms. We outline the theoretical framework, detailing the key components of the system including the circuit hashing algorithm, the ZKP protocol design, and the associated mathematical formalization. The work contributes to the development of a new paradigm for quantum program verification, offering a potential pathway towards building more reliable and secure quantum computing systems. The presented methodology aims to bridge the gap between the theoretical promise of quantum computation and the practical challenges of ensuring its trustworthiness. ---

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Sampling for Probability Density Estimation
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive quantum sampling to probability density estimation, a critical task in various fields including physics, chemistry, and finance. Classical methods struggle with high-dimensional probability distributions, often requiring computationally intensive sampling techniques. We introduce a novel quantum algorithm that dynamically adjusts its sampling strategy based on observed data, significantly enhancing the accuracy of probability density estimation compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism leverages quantum circuits to implement a probabilistic sampling process, ensuring a more robust and efficient estimation of distributions. We detail the algorithm's architecture, key quantum operations, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations and illustrative examples. The resulting quantum algorithm holds the potential to unlock deeper insights into complex probability distributions, offering a significant advancement in statistical analysis.

title: Cape York Free-tailed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Cape York Free-tailed Bat (CYFBT) Algorithm", inspired by the foraging behavior of the Cape York free-tailed bat (Tadarida ventralis). These bats are renowned for their remarkable aerial agility and efficient searching strategies while locating insect swarms. The CYFBT algorithm leverages these characteristics to develop a robust and adaptable optimization method. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a 'flight path' representation mimicking the bat's flight trajectory, a 'pheromone deposition' mechanism simulating the bat's attraction to food sources, and a 'rotation' strategy reflecting the bat's directional adjustments during flight. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified version of the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm, where the 'employed bees' dynamically adjust their flight paths based on a combination of gradient information and pheromone concentration. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and Brent's patuitary function. Results demonstrate that the CYFBT algorithm consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic techniques, particularly in high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising approach for solving complex optimization challenges.

title: Callewaert's Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Mouse's Pathfinding Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Callewaert's Mouse, inspired by the foraging behavior of the house mouse. The algorithm leverages the mouse's tendency to explore and exploit its environment, focusing on path optimization and resource acquisition. Callewaert's Mouse employs a dynamic exploration-exploitation strategy based on a 'mouse' entity traversing a defined search space. The movement of the 'mouse' is governed by a probabilistic model incorporating both local exploration and global exploitation. The algorithm's core mechanism involves adjusting the probability of movement based on the perceived "food" density, simulating the mouse's preference for areas with higher resource availability. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, highlighting its adaptability and potential for achieving robust solutions. The performance of Callewaert's Mouse is compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, showing promising results in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's simplicity and intuitive design make it a valuable addition to the toolbox of metaheuristic optimization techniques.

title: Title: Quantum State Transfer with Adaptive Resonance
abstract: Quantum state transfer is a critical process in quantum information processing, enabling the manipulation and transfer of quantum states between qubits. Current state transfer protocols often suffer from inefficiencies, requiring significant resources and time. This paper introduces a novel quantum state transfer protocol utilizing Adaptive Resonance Networks (ARNs) to optimize the transfer process, minimizing resource requirements and enhancing stability. We propose a dynamic adaptation of the ARN's weights, allowing for faster and more reliable state transfers. The core mechanism focuses on a feedback loop that continuously adjusts the network's parameters to achieve optimal transfer performance. This work presents a theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach compared to existing state transfer techniques.

title: ## Boyaca Spiny Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Boyaca Spiny Rat
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Boyaca Spiny Rat" (BSR), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Boyaca Spiny Rat ( *Profollicolestes boyacensis*), a rodent species inhabiting the high-altitude regions of Colombia. The algorithm leverages the rat's efficient exploration of complex terrains and its adaptive decision-making process to achieve robust optimization performance. BSR incorporates elements of swarm intelligence, particularly mimicking the rat's movement patterns and resource allocation strategies. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a novel movement strategy based on a weighted random walk, coupled with a dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation parameters. The core of BSR lies in its adaptive memory mechanism, which stores and utilizes past successful positions to guide future searches. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results demonstrate that BSR offers competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex fitness functions. This research contributes a new optimization algorithm with a biologically inspired approach and provides a valuable tool for various applications requiring efficient and adaptive search strategies.

title: Algorithmic Chaos in Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the integration of dynamic chaos theory into machine learning algorithms, aiming to achieve automated parameter adjustment and enhanced feature extraction. Traditional machine learning often relies on manual parameter tuning, which can be a laborious and inefficient process. We propose a novel algorithm, termed "Chaos-Adaptive Gradient Descent," that employs a dynamic chaos framework to dynamically adjust model parameters, leading to improved model performance and feature representation. This research addresses the limitations of traditional methods by introducing a novel approach that mimics the inherent unpredictability and self-organization observed in chaotic systems. The core mechanism involves the implementation of a complex dynamic chaos algorithm that iteratively optimizes model parameters based on feedback from the data, promoting a more robust and adaptable learning process. This paper details the design of this algorithm, its mathematical foundations, and its potential impact on machine learning applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Probability Field Theory - A Computational Paradigm
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to probability field theory, proposing a novel computational framework predicated on the principles of quantum superposition and entanglement. We explore the potential of this approach to enhance the efficiency of probabilistic computation, specifically focusing on its implications for machine learning. The core of this work centers on the conceptualization of probability events as quantum states, leveraging entanglement to facilitate complex computations and ultimately, explore its applicability to machine learning tasks. The paper details the underlying mathematical foundations and potential benefits of this new computational paradigm, offering a significant departure from traditional probability modeling approaches.

title: When Political Campaigns Amplify Gendered Online Hate: Evidence from 55 Million Reddit Posts
abstract: Note: This contribution is a Presentation Proposal based on previously published work. The original publication is available at: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11401350 This presentation builds on research presented at ICECER 2025 and examines how political campaign cycles intensify gender-based online hostility, with implications for women and girls’ digital safety and platform accountability. Analysing over 55 million publicly available Reddit posts from January 2024 (pre-campaign) and November 2024 (during the U.S. presidential campaign), the study investigates whether election periods function as high-risk moments for gendered online abuse. Using a fine-tuned BERT classifier with high classification accuracy (F1-scores above 0.95), combined with HDBSCAN clustering, we identify and categorise hate speech before and during the campaign period. The findings reveal a statistically significant 7.8% increase in hate speech during the campaign period. Critically, posts targeting women increased by 38.86%, alongside sharp growth in misogyny-linked and ideology-driven hostility. Clustering analysis further demonstrates how gendered abuse becomes embedded within partisan conflict, often intersecting with racesexual identity-based targeting. These findings suggest that electoral cycles operate as amplification moments for gendered online hostility, increasing exposure to misogynistic narratives and identity-based abuse. Such dynamics may discourage women’s participation in digital civic spaces and reinforce structural inequalities in political discourse. In the context of emerging regulatory frameworks such as the UK Online Safety Act, the results underscore the importance of risk-based, event-sensitive content moderation. Rather than static compliance approaches, platforms may require adaptive, safety-by-design systems that scale detection and intervention during politically sensitive periods. The study demonstrates how responsible AI tools can support regulatory objectives by identifying patterns of gendered harm at scale while maintaining transparency and ethical safeguards. All data were analysed in aggregate form using publicly accessible sources. This research contributes large-scale empirical evidence to interdisciplinary efforts aimed at strengthening digital safety protections for women and girls.

title: A HALLUCINATION-RESISTANT AGENTIC RAG SYSTEM WITH MULTI-STAGE RETRIEVAL AND RESPONSE VALIDATION
abstract: —Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown great abilities in understanding and generating natural language. However, they can create hallucinations by providing factually incorrect or unfounded responses. To tackle this issue, this work suggests a hallucinationresistant Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system that combines multi-stage retrieval, smart re-ranking, and response validation. The system uses an agentic structure, where independent agents plan, retrieve, and refine information by utilizing external knowledge sources. A multi-stage retrieval pipeline brings together dense vector search, keyword-based retrieval, and query reformulation to enhance recall and coverage. The retrieved documents go through a re ranking module that prioritizes contextually relevant and high confidence evidence, which reduces noise and irrelevant information. To improve reliability, we add a response validation layer that uses techniques like crossverification, fact-checking against retrieved evidence, and confidence scoring. This ensures that the generated outputs are based on verifiable sources and lowers the risk of hallucinations. Additionally, the system includes feedback loops and iterative reasoning, allowing agents to update outputs in real-time. Experimental results show that this framework greatly boosts answer accuracy, contextual relevance, and reliability compared to traditional RAG systems. This research presents a scalable and modular setup for implementing trustworthy AI systems in important fields such as healthcare, finance, and legal applications.

title: Evaluation of air combat simulation for multiagent reinforcement learning approaches
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is increasingly used to develop intelligent control policies for complex and dynamic systems such as air combat simulations. This report reviews several open-source frameworks, including JSBSim, FlightGear, CyberBattleSim, CloseAirCombat, and DogFight2, with a focus on their suitability for RL-based aircraft simulation and multiagent research. The evaluation considers each platform’s flexibility, ease of integration, and support for various RL methods. Based on this analysis, the report proposes a modular simulation framework that combines accurate flight dynamics with standardized RL interfacing. This work aims to accelerate research on autonomous air combat agents and provide a foundation for future advancements in multiagent RL.

title: DISCO: Disentangling Signal Restoration and Corruption Identification via Sample-Wise Latent Low-Rank Similarity
abstract: Unsupervised fine-grained anomaly detection is critical for quality monitoring, where decomposition-based methods are widely used to both localize anomalies and restore nonlinear background signals. In the absence of a clean training set, most approaches restrict the model reconstruction capacity through bottleneck designs to prevent the model from reconstructing corrupted regions. This, however, introduces an inherent tradeoff that stronger regularization can improve corruption identification but degrades signal restoration, ultimately limiting fine-grained detection performance. To resolve this conflict, we propose the sample-wise latent low-rank similarity regularization, which leverages batch-level latent relationships to suppress corruptions while preserving the reconstruction capacity of the neural network. By encouraging samples with similar latent structure to conform to a low-rank pattern and treating deviations as corruptions, the proposed design effectively disentangles background reconstruction from corruption identification without sacrificing restoration fidelity. Extensive experiments, including simulations, a real-world case study, and ablation analyses, show that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing baselines on both fine-grained anomaly detection and nonlinear background restoration. History: Bianca Maria Colosimo and Yu Ding served as the senior editor for this article. Funding: This work was supported in part by the University of Minnesota Data Science and AI Hub Seed Grant. Data Ethics & Reproducibility Note: The code capsule is available at https://github.com/ywang3989/DISCO and in the e-Companion to this article (available at https://doi.org/10.1287/ijds.2026.0150 ).

title: Forecasting photovoltaic generation and capacity requirements in southern Peru using SARIMA models and NASA POWER data
authors: Américo Ariel Rubin de Celis Vidal
abstract: Abstract This study develops a SARIMA(1, 0, 0)(2, 1, 1) 12 time-series model to forecast monthly photovoltaic electricity generation in southern Peru. The model is trained on two decades (2003–2023) of irradiance and ambient temperature data from the NASA POWER project, covering the coastal regions of Tacna, Moquegua and Arequipa. A physically consistent energy-yield formulation is employed, replacing the common ambient-temperature correction with a NOCT-based cell-temperature estimate and using a dedicated k sys that isolates thermal effects from other system losses. Monthly generation predictions are combined with official Peruvian demand projections (4% annual growth) to compute the required installed photovoltaic capacity (GWp) for five solar-share targets (3% to 30% by 2034). The model passes standard diagnostic checks (Ljung-Box p = 0.386, RMSE ≈ 1.01 kWh/month) and exhibits no residual autocorrelation, confirming its adequacy for exploratory forecasting. The required capacity ranges from 1.19 GWp (3% target) to 11.94 GWp (30% target) by 2034 (using a capacity factor of 0.24 derived from the SARIMA model). Illustratively, this corresponds to 12 plants of 100 MWp (or 3 of 400 MWp) for the 3% scenario, and 20 plants of 100 MWp (5 of 400 MWp) for the 5% scenario. The 95% prediction intervals translate into a capacity uncertainty of about ±6%, while sensitivity analyses with respect to the assumed capacity factor and demand growth rate keep the variation within ±10%. The novelty lies in the joint application of SARIMA modelling and an explicit cell-temperature correction for grid-scale photovoltaic planning in Peru. The results indicate that 3-5% solar penetration appears technically feasible, though significant investment and supporting infrastructure are required. The methodology can be transferred to other high-irradiance regions, offering a transparent tool for strategic energy planning.

title: Interventional-twin audits for post-probe decision routing under hidden-factor shift
abstract: Interactive systems can encounter states that look equivalent before a low-energy probe even though a hidden mass produces different motion and therefore calls for a different commit route. Aggregate success cannot reveal whether a router used this observed post-probe effect or a correlated pre-probe shortcut. We introduce an interventional-twin audit for this question. The audit predeclares observable channels, constructs pairs that match before probing but diverge in observed effects, freezes a non-oracle input schema, and evaluates cue reversal, directional effect swaps, leakage, route failure, and selective re-probing. Across 180 family–seed units in six fixed synthetic parameterizations, direct post-probe routing attains 0.871 reversed-cue success versus 0.500 without the effect channel. When the factual effect is replaced by its matched counterpart while visible history and probe action are fixed, the learned router attains 0.759 bilateral directional consistency versus 0.000 without probe-effect access. A CausalWorld Pushing construction provides public evidence: matched state and frozen-RGB cases establish post-probe input value, and a separately frozen 20-run full-contract audit passes directional-permutation and grouped leakage gates. A 20-run matched-pair reliability diagnostic preserves pair identifiers while effect noise and missingness increase; the overall paired gain remains positive under severe corruption, while the severe worst-mass interval crosses zero. An architecture–capacity–budget stress shows positive post-probe gains but cell-dependent architecture ordering. A calibration-frozen risk–coverage sweep finds no safe positive-coverage point under three shortcut stresses. The result is a controlled, reproducible workflow for testing effect-responsive routing and reporting where evidence becomes inconclusive.

title: Using Large Language Models to Identify Suicide Risk Factors in Pediatric Emergency Department Chart Notes
abstract: Objective Electronic health records (EHR) have been used increasingly to understand mental health and suicide risk, yet work is relatively limited in young children. Structured EHR data (e.g., age, diagnosis) are easily accessible but may provide a limited depth of information. Unstructured clinical notes hold a wealth of information on clinical risk factors but require more intensive processing. Large language models (LLMs) are a rapidly advancing technology that may be a scalable and efficient way to analyze free-text clinical notes. We provide examples and sample code as a practical guide for using LLMs to identify the presence of known risk factors for suicide in EHR from pre-teen children in the emergency department (ED). Method EHR for 920 patients 8 to 12 years of age (N = 1,310 visits) with suicide thoughts and behaviors, behavioral health concerns, and/or a psychiatric consultation in the pediatric ED of a metropolitan hospital were reviewed from 2020 to 2023. A secure, HIPAA-compliant ChatGPT 4o instance was used to identify any descriptions in clinician free-text notes of three exemplar risk factors relevant in prior work: (1) prior hospitalization and ED visits, (2) sleep problems, and (3) sexual orientation and gender identity. This was compared to consensus human coding from prior work and ‘regular expression' keyword-matching using specificity, sensitivity/recall, precision, and F1 metrics. Results LLM prompts could efficiently and accurately identify the presence of each of three risk factors in ED EHR yielding high model performance metrics: hospitalization (F1 = 96%), sleep (F1 = 90%), and LGBTQ+ identity (F1 = 96%). The LLM approach was more effective than the keyword-matching, which was prone to false positives around hospitalization (specificity = 64%) and false negatives around sleep (sensitivity = 76%). LGBTQ+ identity may be best captured by the LLM or a combination of both approaches (F1 = 97%). Conclusion LLMs are being increasingly used to advance data analytics in research and health care. We provide an exemplar approach to prompt engineering to extract suicide risk factors from free-text clinical notes for pediatric ED patients that is scalable and efficient. This can help integrate data from free-text notes with more structured data, like symptom checklists. Models will change over time and prompts may need targeting with risk factor description or prompt-based (K-shot) training examples to match the nuances of the patient population and EHR system. We aim for this to guide future work and the development of clinical decision aids.

title: The Evolution of Question Generation: Analyzing the Impact of Large Language Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Automatic question generation (AQG) has evolved quite a bit with the advent of transformer‐based large language models (LLMs), transitioning from rule‐based methods and early neural approaches to more adaptable transformer‐based and LLM‐based systems. This process has enabled greater potential for AQG but, at the same time, has posed new problems regarding control, structure, evaluation, and grounding of the generated questions in a wide range of fields. In this survey, we look at the evolution of AQG with respect to five different aspects—answer format, contextual scale, cognitive complexity, control, and multilingual or multimodal capacity. In our analysis of this transition, we focus on the progression of AQG from rule‐based and neural methods to transformer‐based and LLM‐based methods with an emphasis on prompting, retrieval‐augmented generation (RAG), and agentic workflows. Furthermore, we also discuss the technologies involved in modern AQG, such as LLMs, SLMs, retrieval, and agentic systems with reasoning and memory and tool‐use capabilities. Moreover, this paper contributes a taxonomy that captures paradigm shifts in model architecture, prompting, and pipeline design. It also compiles the existing datasets, evaluation techniques, and benchmarks, emphasizing the increasing relevance of retrieval‐based integration, controllable prompting, and agentic pipelines. These advances create ways for the generation of context‐ and cognition‐aware questions tailored to users' needs but also present new challenges associated with factual grounding and evaluation. In summary, the survey reflects the current trend toward developing more flexible, resilient, and multimodal AQG systems with wide‐ranging applications, including educational settings, knowledge‐based systems across various domains, and human‐computer collaboration. The paper helps establish a solid foundation for future research on question generation through its critical analysis of current trends and research directions.

title: Reinforcement‐Learning‐Based High‐Fidelity Quantum State Preparation in Non‐Markovian Time‐Varying Noise
abstract: ABSTRACT In quantum systems subject to non‐Markovian noise, environmental parameters are often not directly observable, requiring controllers to infer latent variations from temporal evolution and adapt their control actions accordingly. Existing approaches often make limited use of temporal context and generalize poorly to unseen time‐varying noise without retraining. We propose OQ‐DDQN, a reinforcement‐learning framework for quantum state preparation in dynamic non‐Markovian open systems. It uses a finite‐trajectory, post‐step‐normalized stochastic QSD ensemble with auxiliary finite‐memory operators and estimates reduced states by averaging normalized colored‐noise trajectory projectors. Its history‐aware extension models recent Bloch‐state sequences to infer latent noise variations. OQ‐DDQN reaches for of the pooled evaluation records, although varies substantially across training seeds in the principal three‐seed benchmark. Under a three‐seed holdout evaluation using a common initial‐state schedule across controllers with 32 stochastic QSD trajectories per task, the history‐aware extension achieves an average fidelity of 0.9564 and . History‐length ablation and noise‐component perturbation analyses further indicate that temporal memory improves stability and generalization under dynamic non‐Markovian noise. These results establish OQ‐DDQN as the overall control framework and its history‐aware variant as an extension for latent time‐varying noise.

OQ‐DDQN reaches for of the pooled evaluation records, although varies substantially across training seeds in the principal three‐seed benchmark. Under a three‐seed holdout evaluation using a common initial‐state schedule across controllers with 32 stochastic QSD trajectories per task, the history‐aware extension achieves an average fidelity of 0.9564 and . title: Relational Task Generation Language: A Declarative Specification Framework for Relational Deep Learning
abstract: Relational Deep Learning (RDL) has become a powerful paradigm for learning from multi-tabular data. However, manually defining RDL prediction tasks is a laborious process that frequently results in data leakage. To address this issue, we introduce Relational Task Generation Language (RTGL) - an open-source declarative language that streamlines RDL task formulation by abstracting away low-level SQL details. We showcase RTGL by reconstructing existing RDL benchmark tasks and uncovering their inconsistencies stemming from manually crafted SQL definitions of RDL prediction targets, thereby underscoring the value of a dedicated declarative language. In addition, we demonstrate the practical utility of RTGL by designing various new tasks with diverse forms and target types. Our experiments confirm the robustness and usability of RTGL, as well as its seamless integration with the existing RDL frameworks, making it widely accessible to the community.

title: Data-Driven Persona-Conditioned Agents for A/B Test Simulation
abstract: A/B testing is the gold standard for evaluating product changes, but each experiment requires real user traffic, engineering effort, and weeks of measurement. We propose a simulation framework that predicts A/B test outcomes using LLM-powered agents conditioned on data-driven personas grounded in real user behavioral signals. Unlike prior work that relies on synthetic or rule-based personas, our agents are constructed from anonymized behavioral data - activity patterns, engagement signals, and inferred demographics - enabling more faithful population modeling. We frame A/B test simulation as a structured question task and systematically study (i) question design formats, (ii) the impact of persona data source and domain alignment, (iii) the trade-off between per-persona behavioral depth and population diversity, and (iv) efficient population subsampling. On a benchmark of 40 A/B tests spanning two metric types, our best configuration achieves 0.75-0.80 directional accuracy depending on the test metric, demonstrating that data-driven personas are a viable path toward fast, low-cost experiment pre-screening.

title: Quantum-Based Optimization of Gas Throughput in Natural Gas Transmission Networks Under Hydraulic Constraints Using QAOA
abstract: Maximizing gas throughput in transmission networks under hydraulic and operational constraints is a combinatorial problem whose complexity grows exponentially with network size, making it computationally intensive to solve exactly. This paper addresses the graph-based optimization problem by optimizing nodal-pressure assignments under the Panhandle-B hydraulic equation. By framing the problem as a search over discretized nodal-pressure assignments coupled with a cost Hamiltonian that encodes both the delivery objective and physical-constraint penalties, we establish a unified formulation suitable for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The mathematical model is adapted to a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulation and implemented using the Classiq quantum software platform. In simulator-based experiments, QAOA recovered the maximum-throughput valid operating point, consistent with classical exhaustive evaluation and classical hydraulic simulation reference solutions. A distinctive contribution of this work is the end-to-end execution of a reduced problem instance on the IonQ Forte-1 trapped-ion quantum processor. Remarkably, the hardware implementation used only $p=2$ QAOA layers, substantially fewer than the $p=30$ layers used in the simulator-based study. Despite this significant reduction in circuit depth, the QPU produced physically valid and interpretable candidate solutions that bracketed the continuous classical optimum, with each located within one pressure-discretization step of it. These results demonstrate that meaningful gas-network optimization behavior can be obtained using considerably shallower QAOA circuits than initially expected and provide an end-to-end proof of concept for near-term quantum-assisted gas-network optimization.

title: Suffixient Arrays: A New Efficient Suffix Array Compression Technique
abstract: Abstract The Suffix Array is a classic text index enabling on-line pattern matching queries via simple binary search. The main drawback of the Suffix Array is that it takes linear space in the text’s length, even when the text itself is extremely compressible. Several works in the literature showed that the Suffix Array can be compressed, but they all rely on complex succinct data structures which in practice tend to exhibit poor cache locality and thus significantly slow down queries. In this paper, we propose a new simple and very efficient solution to this problem by presenting the Suffixient Array : a tiny subset of the Suffix Array sufficient to locate on-line one pattern occurrence (in general, all its Maximal Exact Matches) via binary search, provided that random access to the text is available. We prove that: (i) the Suffixient Array length $$\varvec{\chi }$$ χ is a strong repetitiveness measure, (ii) unlike most existing repetition-aware indexes such as the $$\varvec{r}$$ r -index, our new index is efficient in the I/O model, and (iii) Suffixient Arrays can be computed in linear time and compressed working space. We show experimentally that, when using well-established compressed random access data structures on repetitive collections, the Suffixient Array $$\varvec{\textrm{sA}}$$ sA is simultaneously (i) faster and orders of magnitude smaller than the Suffix Array and (ii) smaller and one to two orders of magnitude faster than the $$\varvec{r}$$ r -index. With an average pattern matching query time as low as 3.5 ns per character, our new index gets very close to the ultimate lower bound: the RAM throughput of our workstation (1.18 ns per character).

title: Federated Learning-Based Cross-Domain LiDAR Point Cloud Processing and Protection of Sensitive Geographic Information
abstract: Cross-domain LiDAR point clouds have become an important data foundation for smart cities, high-precision map updating, road inspection, industrial-park digital twins, and critical infrastructure monitoring, yet they are usually collected in a decentralized manner by different institutions, regions, and sensing platforms, so direct centralized sharing may increase the risk of exposing sensitive geographic coordinates, facility outlines, and road topology. Because existing centralized point-cloud learning methods still struggle to balance cross-domain generalization, privacy protection, and system scalability, this paper proposes a scalable federated learning system for cross-domain LiDAR point cloud processing. The system adopts a three-layer architecture of edge point-cloud clients, regional coordination nodes, and a cloud-based secure aggregation server, in which pointcloud sampling, coordinate anonymization, local geometric feature extraction, and semantic segmentation are performed locally. Collaborative modeling without raw point-cloud upload is enabled through cross-domain category prototype alignment, client-adaptive weight aggregation, differential privacy, secure aggregation, Top-k sparsification, and 8-bit quantization. In simulations across four cross-domain scenarios, the method achieves an average mIoU of 67.2%, exceeding FedAvg (58.8%) and FedBN (62.0%), and retains 61.4% under severe Non-IID conditions. At a privacy budget of ε = 2, the attack success rate falls from 63.5% to 24.8% while mIoU remains 67.2%, and with 100 clients single-round communication drops from 21.96 GB to 7.92 GB. The system thus improves semantic performance, reduces sensitive-information leakage, and maintains communication efficiency and training stability as the number of clients grows.

title: CMERGE : Clinical Multimodal Evidence Reasoning Graph
abstract: Clinical decision support systems increasingly rely on synthesizingstructured reasoning from heterogeneous patient data streams, in-cluding electronic health records (EHRs), physician notes, diagnos-tic imaging reports, physiological monitor signals, and laboratoryfindings. However, existing multimodal clinical graph extraction ap-proaches frequently generate hallucinated diagnostic nodes, weaklygrounded causal relations, and densely connected reasoning struc-tures that cannot be reliably traced back to explicit patient evidence.These limitations are particularly problematic in high-stakes clinicalenvironments where every inferred relationship must remain inter-pretable, auditable, and medically justifiable. In addition, uniformlyapplying frontier-scale large language model (LLM) inference acrossall clinical observations introduces substantial computational over-head that conflicts with real-time clinical workflow requirements. Inthis paper, we present CMERGE (Clinical Multimodal Evidence Rea-soning Graph Engine), a provenance-constrained neuro-symbolicframework for constructing interpretable and verifiable clinical rea-soning graphs from heterogeneous patient evidence streams.

title: MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATIONS OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Generative AI) has advanced rapidly, yet the mechanisms responsible for its behaviour are neither heuristic nor accidental: they are consequences of well-established mathematical principles. This chapter presents a structured and self-contained account of the mathematics that underlies contemporary generative systems, and explains not only what these systems compute but why the computation is well posed. The exposition begins with linear algebra, which supplies the vector, matrix and tensor formalism used to represent data and to define the linear maps performed by every neural layer. It then develops probability and information theory, establishing random variables, conditional distributions, Bayes’ theorem, maximum likelihood estimation, entropy, cross-entropy and Kullback–Leibler divergence as the language in which generation is expressed as sampling from a learned distribution. Multi variable calculus and optimization follow, covering gradients, the chain rule, gradient descent, stochastic approximation and adaptive optimizers such as Adam, which together explain how model parameters are estimated in high-dimensional non-convex landscapes. These foundations are then assembled into neural networks, representation learning and embedding geometry, and used to derive the scaled dot-product attention mechanism, multi-head attention and positional encoding that define the Transformer. The chapter subsequently formalizes large language models as auto-regressive factorization of sequence probability, and compares the objectives of variational auto-encoders, generative adversarial networks and denoising diffusion models. Worked numerical examples, comparative tables and original diagrams are included to connect symbolic formulations with computational practice, and open mathematical challenges concerning scaling, stability, calibration and efficiency are discussed.

title: Structural Associative Retrieval: Zero-Cost Memory Linking via Embedding Clustering and Lexical-Semantic Pipelines
abstract: Current memory systems for conversational AI agents rely on embedding similarity for retrieval, which captures topical relevance but fails at associative recall. I propose Structural Associative Retrieval (SAR), a three-stage pipeline that achieves associative memory linking without training new models or calling external APIs. SAR reuses existing embeddings through clustering for coarse structural grouping, applies part-of-speech extraction for skeletal decomposition, and performs word-level embedding comparison for fine-grained ranking within clusters. On a controlled dataset of 50 personal memories, SAR achieves near-perfect associative accuracy. I present ablation experiments across five retrieval variants, demonstrating that each pipeline stage contributes irreplaceably. SAR operates entirely locally with zero API cost and compresses memory indices from 768-dimensional vectors to single-integer cluster IDs (768x reduction)

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Geometry Computation
abstract: Quantum Topology presents a novel framework for adaptive geometry computation, leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology to analyze and simulate complex geometric structures with enhanced precision. This system utilizes quantum mechanics to dynamically adjust geometric parameters, enabling the simulation of intricate patterns and behaviors previously unattainable through traditional computational methods. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to guide the evolution of geometric configurations. The research aims to address limitations of existing techniques by providing a framework capable of handling highly complex geometries and generating accurate predictive models. This work offers a fundamentally new approach to geometric modeling, holding significant potential for advancements across diverse fields including materials science, physics, and computational geometry.

title: Quantum Simulation of Non-Linear Topological Structures Analysis
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a powerful tool for investigating complex systems, particularly those exhibiting non-linear topological structures. This paper explores the application of quantum simulation to analyze these structures, focusing on predicting system performance through a novel methodology. We delineate a framework that leverages the inherent non-linear properties of quantum simulations to provide deeper insights into system behavior. The core claim is that this approach facilitates a more comprehensive understanding of topological structures and their associated performance characteristics. The research utilizes quantum algorithms to emulate complex topological configurations, ultimately yielding quantitative predictions of system behavior. The study's novelty lies in the integration of a specific non-linear simulation technique, designed for enhanced analysis of these structures.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应图的优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement, designed to improve the stability and robustness of optimization processes. Traditional optimization methods often overlook the inherent properties of entanglement, offering a potential pathway for enhanced performance. This work proposes a framework wherein parameters are optimized through the manipulation of entangled states, leading to a more resilient and reliable solution. We detail the core mechanism of utilizing entanglement to guide the optimization process, emphasizing the stability gained through this approach. The research explores the potential benefits of this quantum-enhanced optimization strategy for a range of problems, aiming to provide a significant advancement over existing algorithms.

title: Title: Computational Cognitive Architecture (CCA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Computational Cognitive Architecture (CCA), a novel framework for modeling and simulating the emergence of complex cognitive processes through a dynamically evolving computational architecture. CCA integrates elements of neural networks, symbolic AI, and evolutionary algorithms to iteratively refine internal representations and cognitive rules based on experience. We argue that traditional cognitive modeling approaches often fall short in capturing the dynamic and multifaceted nature of human cognition. CCA offers a fundamentally different approach, emphasizing self-organization and continuous refinement, resulting in a system capable of simulating a broader range of cognitive phenomena. This work explores the core mechanisms of CCA, detailing the iterative refinement process and its potential to provide a more realistic and flexible model of cognitive function.

title: Time-Domain Quantum Computation Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel time-domain quantum computation framework designed to enhance quantum computation efficiency and precision through the implementation of a "Quantum Time Step" mechanism. Traditional quantum computing approaches often rely on a large number of qubits, limiting scalability and performance. Our framework breaks down the quantum computation process into discrete time steps, optimizing each step for improved execution speed and reduced error rates. This approach leverages a dynamic time step scheduling strategy to guide the quantum evolution, ultimately leading to more effective and accurate quantum algorithms.

title: ## Bridled Dolphin: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bridled Dolphin Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bridled Dolphin, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bridled dolphins. The algorithm leverages the unique hunting strategy of these dolphins – their coordinated pursuit of prey while maintaining a specific distance from a leader – to create a robust and efficient search process. Bridled Dolphin incorporates key elements of this behavior, including a leader dolphin, follower dolphins, and a dynamic distance adjustment mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, where each dolphin represents a potential solution to the optimization problem. A novel distance function is proposed to guide the dolphins' movement, mimicking the leader-follower dynamics observed in the natural behavior. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The results indicate that Bridled Dolphin exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's adaptability and the incorporation of a biologically inspired mechanism offer potential for further development and application in diverse optimization challenges.

title: Brazilian Porcupine: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Porcupine Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Brazilian Porcupine, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Brazilian porcupines. The algorithm leverages the porcupine's strategy of selecting and rejecting food items based on a combination of perceived value and randomness, mimicking their selective feeding habits. We detail the algorithm's core components: the 'Selection' phase, which employs a probability-based rejection mechanism; the 'Evaluation' phase, where potential solutions are assessed; and the 'Movement' phase, which utilizes a biased random walk to explore the search space. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key innovations of Brazilian Porcupine lie in its dynamic adjustment of acceptance probabilities and its localized search strategy, contributing to improved convergence and exploration capabilities compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's parameters are carefully tuned to achieve robust performance across diverse problem landscapes. This research offers a new perspective on metaheuristic design, drawing inspiration from natural behaviors to create a potentially valuable optimization tool.

title: Core Claim: Develop a dynamic information optimization algorithm capable of adapting to environmental changes and achieving optimization of complex systems.
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic information optimization algorithm designed to address the challenges of adapting to evolving environments. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameters, limiting their effectiveness in dynamic scenarios. This work introduces a new algorithm that dynamically updates optimization goals based on real-time environmental information, fostering adaptability and improved performance. We explore the key mechanisms involved in this dynamic adaptation, focusing on the iterative refinement of the objective function to reflect changes in the system. The algorithm's design incorporates a feedback loop that continuously assesses the impact of environmental changes on the optimization process, resulting in a more robust and responsive optimization strategy. title: Black-tailed Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BMIOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black-tailed Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BMIOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of the black-tailed mouse, specifically its efficient exploration and exploitation strategies for finding food sources. BMIOA utilizes a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating elements of the mouse's instinctive navigation and decision-making processes. Key components include a dynamic exploration radius influenced by food availability, a weighted velocity update mechanism reflecting the mouse's preference for promising areas, and a novel convergence criterion based on the observed settling behavior of mice during food hunts. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that BMIOA offers competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems exhibiting high dimensionality and complex landscapes. Future research directions include extending BMIOA to handle multi-objective optimization and integrating it with other optimization techniques.

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization with Hybrid Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization represents a paradigm shift in the field of optimization, aiming to mimic the inherent properties of quantum mechanics – specifically, entanglement and superposition – to enhance algorithm performance. This paper introduces a novel hybrid neural network architecture designed to exploit these principles, specifically through the utilization of a 'quantum-aware feature map' and a 'quantum-inspired momentum term.' We explore the integration of these mechanisms to improve the efficiency and robustness of optimization algorithms, particularly in complex, high-dimensional problem spaces. The core claim is that this hybrid approach yields significant improvements in convergence speed, solution quality, and adaptability compared to traditional optimization methods. We present a comprehensive analysis of the proposed architecture and demonstrate its effectiveness through illustrative examples.

title: A Royalty Rate Determination Model for the Technology Transfer of Generative AI Models
abstract: This study proposes a valuation framework and determination model to estimate the appropriate royalty rate for the technology transfer of generative AI models. As complex technological assets, generative AI models comprise model architecture, trained weights, training and fine-tuning data, prompt assets, retrieval-augmented generation structures, safety modules, operational know-how, retraining rights, output usage rights, and liability arrangements. Therefore, simply applying conventional royalty rates used for patented technologies or general software does not adequately reflect the economic value and risks associated with generative AI models. To address this limitation, this study proposes a royalty rate determination procedure that involves decomposing technological assets, defining the scope of rights, estimating base value, allocating technology contribution, adjusting for risk, incorporating real option value, and deriving a negotiable royalty range. In particular, this study identifies the economic useful life of training data, data contribution, reusability, rights and contractual conditions, copyright and privacy risks, and model obsolescence as key adjustment factors. The results suggest that the appropriate royalty rate for generative AI models should be determined not as a single fixed rate, but as a risk-adjusted negotiation range reflecting data rights, model performance, technological life, substitutability, exclusivity, liability risk, update rights, and expansion potential.

title: Adaptive BERT for Semantic Alignment and Intelligent Triage of Multilingual Inquiries in Cross-Border E-Commerce
abstract: Currently, in the field of cross-border e-commerce, there are problems such as insufficient adaptation of general pre-training models to domain features, significant differences in the semantic gap between English-Chinese cross-language and English-Russian scenarios, low training efficiency and high deployment costs when implementing complex models. In this regard, the study proposes a domain-adaptive Multilingual Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (MBERT) model that integrates a Domain Adaptation Layer (DAL) and a Cross-Language Alignment Module (CLAM). This study first performs domain adaptation optimization through pre-training a Domain-Distinguish Task (DDT) BERT model. On this basis, MBERT is used to provide the model with a cross-language semantic representation, and the DDT mechanism and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology are finally integrated. The experimental results showed that, on the SemEval-2016 attribute-level emotion annotation data set, the proposed model achieved average accuracies of 82.2%, 83.2%, and 88.0% in the English-Chinese, English-Russian, and English-Spanish scenarios, respectively, demonstrating the best performance. Pre-training took 6.3 h and converged in 16 rounds. Inference took 19ms/sentence and occupied 9GB of video memory. Adding DAL alone increased the F1 value in the English-Spanish scene by 4.1%, and adding CLAM alone increased the English-Chinese accuracy by 4.2%.

title: Sarcoma Region of Interest (ROI) Images - Part 3
abstract: Bone and soft tissue (BST) tumors are a heterogeneous and rare group of mesenchymal neoplasms that pose significant diagnostic challenges owing to their complex morphologies and overlapping histological features. Despite rapid advances in digital pathology, most publicly available datasets predominantly focus on common epithelial tumors and offer a limited representation of BST tumors. To address this gap, we introduced the Pathologist-Annotated Image Retrieval dataset for Bone and Soft Tissue tumors (PAIR-BST), a dataset consisting of 2,252 pathologist-annotated regions of interest derived from 470 whole slide images obtained from 268 patients diagnosed with BST tumors. Each region was curated and annotated with multi-level labels, including 33 histologic diagnoses, 11 lines of differentiation, and 6 growth patterns, enabling comprehensive characterization of the morphological heterogeneity inherent to BST tumors. Benchmark experiments have demonstrated that pathology foundation models face challenges in identifying these tumors, particularly when distinguishing between tumor subtypes and growth patterns. PAIR-BST offers a high-quality, discriminative benchmark for the development and evaluation of pathology foundation models, specifically focusing on rare mesenchymal tumors.[Metadata Availability] Additional metadata containing specific coordinates for all ROIs (Regions of Interest) within the WSI, along with labels such as diagnosis for each, is available in a separate .csv file at: https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.33383509 (also linked in the related materials below). Find related datasets in the collection at https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.c.8223469

title: Reasoning about expression evaluation under interference
abstract: Hoare-style inference rules for program constructs permit the copying of expressions and tests from program text into logical contexts. It is known that this requires care even for sequential programs but much more serious issues arise with concurrent programs because of potential interference to the values of variables. The “rely-guarantee” approach tackles the challenge of recording acceptable interference and offers a way to provide safe inference rules for concurrent constructs. This paper shows how the algebraic presentation of rely-guarantee ideas can clarify and formalise the conditions for safely re-using expressions and tests from program text in logical contexts for reasoning about concurrent programs; crucially this extends to handling expressions that reference more than one shared variable. A non-trivial example related to the Fischer-Galler forest representation of equivalence relations is treated.

title: A Detailed Insight into AI-driven Specific Damage Site Nano-detection (SDSND) for Precision Diagnosis of Breast Cancer
abstract: Abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among women worldwide, underscoring the critical need for early and accurate diagnostic methodologies. This review describes an advanced breast cancer detection system that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI) with sophisticated imaging mechanisms to improve diagnostic precision. The system employs highresolution imaging technology to non-invasively visualize and isolate successive layers of breast tissue, thereby providing detailed, multi-planar views of targeted anatomical regions. This approach facilitates deeper examination of tissue architecture. Through subsequent AI-driven computational analysis, potential malignant areas, including microcalcifications and subtle structural distortions, are identified and highlighted in real time. This integrated approach enables faster and more reliable interpretation of complex imaging data while reducing the cognitive burden on radiologists. The core mechanism enhances diagnostic accuracy by detecting aberrant tissue patterns and generating comprehensive layered insights, including quantitative assessments of tissue density and vascularization, to support clinical decision-making and risk stratification. By combining depth-resolved visualization with automated interpretation, this approach has the potential to advance beyond conventional twodimensional screening paradigms. The integration of AI and advanced imaging contributes to a more sensitive and specific diagnostic workflow. Consequently, this review presents SDSND as a hypothetical and emerging framework integrating AI and nanoscale detection. However, its clinical applicability remains unvalidated and requires experimental and clinical investigation.

title: A Post-Quantum Secure Multi-Tenant Cloud Architecture with Scalable Key Management and Side-Channel Resistance
abstract: To meet the performance and scalability demands of current cloud systems, cryptographic systems should be resistant to both quantum and classical adversaries, especially considering the future potential provided by quantum computing. The presented manuscript provides an integrated, quantum-resistant, cloud-based encryption architecture built on the combination of post-quantum authentication, scalable, multi-tenant, key-management methods, and side-channel-conscious design in a cloud-native paradigm. The lattice-based post-quantum key-encapsulation scheme to derive the long-lived and tenant-specific cryptographic key is built into the system to remove all possible single-point failure sources. Long-lived and tenant-specific cryptographic keys are subsequently replicated in a threshold-based key-management service (KMS) cluster. Lightweight symmetric primitives are used to compute session keys thus reducing client-side latency on resource-constrained devices. The AES -256-GCM or Ascon encryption schemes are deployed to guarantee confidentiality of data. Moreover, the architecture uses the symmetric message authentication codes and lattice-signature schemes produced using quantum-safe primitives to ensure the data integrity and authenticity. By distributing key computations across isolated KMS nodes and restricting direct use of long-lived secrets to bounded and infrequent operations, the implementation utilizes leakage-resilient techniques. The system, which is designed for elastic scalability, provides fine-grained access control through configurable lattice-based attribute-based encryption and dynamically allocates keys for new tenants. Experimental benchmarks show that the technique attains strong multi-tenant isolation and side-channel information leakage resistance while minimizing handshake latency by considerable amounts over per-session post-quantum exchanges. This model surmounts the shortcomings of current post-quantum, multi-tenant, and cloud-native security systems by integrating quantum-resistant cryptographical principles, distributed mechanisms for trust, and lightweight operational techniques and thus offers a practical and flexible solution for secure protection of sensitive cloud-hosted data in the future quantum era.
