The resulting system modeling and optimization capabilities represent a significant advancement, offering a more flexible and automated approach. This paper investigates the advantages of this synergistic approach through theoretical analysis and empirical validation, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize optimization processes across diverse domains.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Function Approximation
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive kernel learning framework designed to address the limitations of traditional kernel methods. The core challenge in kernel learning lies in the manual selection of an appropriate kernel function and its associated parameters – a process that is often computationally intensive and reliant on domain expertise. Our approach automates this selection process by employing a Bayesian optimization strategy within a function approximation context. The algorithm dynamically learns the optimal kernel function and its parameters directly from the data, thereby enhancing flexibility and efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive framework through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components for its implementation. The core claim of this work is that automated kernel selection significantly reduces the burden on practitioners and improves the performance of kernel-based function approximation.

title: ## Blue-eyed Cuscus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Nocturnal Marsupial
abstract: This paper presents Blue-eyed Cuscus (BEC), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the blue-eyed cuscus, a nocturnal marsupial known for its efficient searching strategies in complex environments. BEC combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Cauchy-Matthewmann-Levene (CML) mutation to create a robust and adaptive algorithm suitable for a variety of optimization problems. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of the exploration-exploitation balance using a 'cushion' mechanism mimicking the cuscus's cautious approach to new food sources. This cushion dynamically alters the influence of both the particle's best experience and global best experience, promoting efficient convergence while avoiding premature convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BEC through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's design prioritizes adaptability and robustness, making it a valuable addition to the optimization landscape.

title: # Blackish Butterfly Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Butterfly Flight Dynamics
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Blackish Butterfly Bat" (BBB), inspired by the flight dynamics of black swallowtail butterflies (Papilio fullo). The algorithm leverages the observed behaviors of butterflies – including erratic flight patterns, hovering, and directional changes – to create a robust and efficient search process. BBB utilizes a novel combination of adaptive velocity control, a dynamically adjusted Lévy flight component, and a local search strategy based on butterfly wingbeat frequency variations. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around simulating the butterfly's ability to efficiently explore the search space while simultaneously exploiting promising regions. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate BBB's competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) across a range of benchmark optimization problems. The algorithm exhibits strong convergence properties, particularly in challenging, multi-modal landscapes. Future research directions include integrating BBB with machine learning techniques and exploring its application in real-world engineering problems.

title: IDEALTA-LIME: scan-level partitions, fused deep and handcrafted features, trained models and LIME explanations for pulmonary nodule classification on LUNA16
abstract: Supporting data, code and derived artefacts for the study "Fusing Deep and Handcrafted Features for Lung Cancer Detection with Ensemble Learning and Classifier-Agnostic Explainability using Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME)", submitted to PeerJ Computer Science. Study summary IDEALTA (Integrated Diagnostic Ensemble for Lung Tumor Analysis) is an interpretability-supportive ensemble framework for pulmonary nodule candidate classification on the LUNA16 benchmark. Deep features from a frozen VGG16 backbone are combined with handcrafted Local Binary Pattern and Gabor descriptors. Each modality is classified by its own support vector machine after principal component analysis, and the three probability outputs are averaged in a soft ensemble. Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations expose the image regions underlying individual predictions, evaluated under Euclidean and cosine metrics over Quickshift superpixels. Contents config/ — the classification configuration, including the class caps and the balancing seed (balance_seed = 42) that determine the partitions reported in the manuscript. partitions/ — scan-level (seriesuid) split assignments, the split summary, the dataset validation report, and one manifest per partition. Each manifest contains one row per candidate: sample identifier, source series identifier, subset, split, label, coordinates, geometry, source CSV row and file path. Class caps are 2,000 negative and 1,149 positive for training, and 100 negative and 100 positive for each of validation and test. All 1,349 positive candidates in the 886 readable scans are retained across the three partitions. Splits are assigned once at the level of the whole computed tomography series, so no candidate from a given scan appears in more than one partition. results/ — per-seed metric tables and mean and standard deviation summaries for each of the seven compared methods (three frozen-VGG16 convolutional variants differing in loss and class weighting, and four SVM/PCA configurations over Local Binary Pattern, Gabor and VGG16 features together with their soft ensemble), accompanied by the Friedman omnibus, Nemenyi post-hoc and pairwise Wilcoxon outputs. models/ — per-seed training histories, test metrics, confusion matrices, learning curves and trained convolutional checkpoints, together with the selected support vector machine hyperparameters and per-seed confusion matrices. features/ — extracted VGG16, Local Binary Pattern and Gabor feature arrays and the corresponding labels for the training, validation and test partitions. lime/ — the Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations configuration and per-instance explanation outputs for the baseline convolutional model at seed 42 on the test partition. code/ — the data-construction and experiment notebooks, the pipeline package and command-line scripts, and the environment specification. MANIFEST.json — the relative path, byte size and SHA-256 checksum of every deposited file, together with an explicit record of what was excluded and why. Reported results Seven methods were compared over ten random seeds (1, 7, 42, 88, 123, 256, 314, 999, 1024 and 2024) on a balanced 200-region test partition. The soft ensemble attains accuracy 0.848 plus or minus 0.016, F1 0.834, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.927, sensitivity 0.765 and specificity 0.931. The strongest convolutional baseline attains accuracy 0.808. These are computational findings on a single public benchmark; clinical use would require prospective external validation. evidence.title: IDEALTA-LIME: scan-level partitions, fused deep and handcrafted features, trained models and LIME explanations for pulmonary nodule classification on LUNA16
evidence.abstract: Supporting data, code and derived artefacts for the study "Fusing Deep and Handcrafted Features for Lung Cancer Detection with Ensemble Learning and Classifier-Agnostic Explainability using Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME)", submitted to PeerJ Computer Science. Study summary IDEALTA (Integrated Diagnostic Ensemble for Lung Tumor Analysis) is an interpretability-supportive ensemble framework for pulmonary nodule candidate classification on the LUNA16 benchmark. Deep features from a frozen VGG16 backbone are combined with handcrafted Local Binary Pattern and Gabor descriptors. Each modality is classified by its own support vector machine after principal component analysis, and the three probability outputs are averaged in a soft ensemble. Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations expose the image regions underlying individual predictions, evaluated under Euclidean and cosine metrics over Quickshift superpixels. Contents config/ — the classification configuration, including the class caps and the balancing seed (balance_seed = 42) that determine the partitions reported in the manuscript. partitions/ — scan-level (seriesuid) split assignments, the split summary, the dataset validation report, and one manifest per partition. Each manifest contains one row per candidate: sample identifier, source series identifier, subset, split, label, coordinates, geometry, source CSV row and file path. Class caps are 2,000 negative and 1,149 positive for training, and 100 negative and 100 positive for each of validation and test. All 1,349 positive candidates in the 886 readable scans are retained across the three partitions. Splits are assigned once at the level of the whole computed tomography series, so no candidate from a given scan appears in more than one partition. results/ — per-seed metric tables and mean and standard deviation summaries for each of the seven compared methods (three frozen-VGG16 convolutional variants differing in loss and class weighting, and four SVM/PCA configurations over Local Binary Pattern, Gabor and VGG16 features together with their soft ensemble), accompanied by the Friedman omnibus, Nemenyi post-hoc and pairwise Wilcoxon outputs. models/ — per-seed training histories, test metrics, confusion matrices, learning curves and trained convolutional checkpoints, together with the selected support vector machine hyperparameters and per-seed confusion matrices. features/ — extracted VGG16, Local Binary Pattern and Gabor feature arrays and the corresponding labels for the training, validation and test partitions. lime/ — the Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations configuration and per-instance explanation outputs for the baseline convolutional model at seed 42 on the test partition. code/ — the data-construction and experiment notebooks, the pipeline package and command-line scripts, and the environment specification. title: When Does Cost-Sensitive Weighting Matter? A Classifier-Capacity Anal-ysis for Imbalanced Classification
abstract: Class weighting is the most widely used cost-sensitive remedy for class imbalance, and inverse-frequency “balanced” weights are often applied as an unquestioned default. This paper asks whether the choice among competing weighting mechanisms actually matters, and for which classifiers. Seven mechanisms, namely Balanced, Cost-Matrix, Sqrt-InverseFreq, Log-Damped, Effective-Number, a Search-Tuned power scheme, and focal loss, were evaluated on twenty-four benchmark datasets whose imbalance ratios reach 85:1, under three base classifiers of increasing representational capacity: logistic regression, a soft-voting ensemble of logistic regression, random forest, and a support vector machine, and XGBoost. Using leakage-free nested cross-validation and the Friedman–Nemenyi procedure applied separately to each classifier, mechanism choice produced large, highly significant differences under logistic regression (p < 0.0001), differences that shrank to non-significance under the voting ensemble (p = 0.179) and became indistinguishable from a random ordering under XGBoost (p = 0.955, average-rank spread of 0.46). At the same time, the two high-capacity classifiers outperformed logistic regression under every mechanism tested. The evidence supports a simple two-tier policy: tune the weighting scheme carefully for linear learners, and keep the plain balanced default for ensemble and boosting learners, where additional tuning yields no benefit that survives a significance test.

title: Validated Binary Decompilation Without Tears
abstract: Binaries are an attractive target for formal verification—they describe a precise and deterministic semantics that closely conforms to the execution. However, binary verification entails a decompilation process, and the credibility of the verification hinges on the correctness of the decompiler. In this paper, we present a translation validation approach to decompiler assurance. We define a simple and compositional formalisation of decompiler correctness that is strong enough to preserve safety properties as well as security hyperproperties, thereby enabling verification results of the decompiled code to transfer to the executable code. Our notion, termed conditional trace-equivalence, allows the decompilation to leverage heuristics by embedding them within the program semantics. Our translation validation approach is implemented in the AArch64 decompiler Basil. Its evaluation showcases that translation validation is well-suited to verifying binary decompilation that scales to real-world C binaries. Our encoding exemplifies that the approach incurs minimal engineering overhead.

title: The Effect of Intellectual Property Regulation of AI Training Data on AI Capital Accumulation
abstract: This study quantitatively examines how the level of intellectual property protection over artificial intelligence (AI) training data affects AI capital accumulation. Korean copyright law provides no explicit exception for text and data mining; therefore, using protected works for AI training depends on ex-post interpretation of the general fair use provision. Drawing on a review of domestic and foreign regulations and disputes, the study identifies two channels through which protection operates: rising costs at the data procurement stage and binding constraints at the training stage. This distinction is consistent with 2025 U.S. court decisions that assess AI training separately from data acquisition. A dynamic general equilibrium model incorporating a Lucas span-of-control structure represents these channels as policy parameters and simulates how changes in protection affect aggregate output and knowledge capital, the model's representation of AI capital. Under the baseline calibration, tightening protection by 20 percent reduces the knowledge capital stock by 17.1 percent and output by 3.4 percent, with the training-stage channel accounting for the larger share of the overall effect. This effect arises primarily from reduced use of knowledge capital rather than substitution toward labor.

title: Speaker-Mediated Route Knowledge Transfer for Goal-Oriented Vision-and-Language Navigation
abstract: Goal-oriented vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires an agent to reach a target from a high-level instruction that does not prescribe a route. Training therefore faces two problems. First, terminal and distance-based feedback leave partial trajectories without route-semantic supervision. Second, a single annotated path introduces single-reference route bias because several routes may satisfy the same goal. We propose Speaker-Mediated Route Knowledge Transfer (SMRKT), which comprises three components. To provide the route knowledge required by both problems, we trained a trajectory-to-language speaker on route-following VLN data and froze it as a training-time evaluator in the cross-granularity route-prior transfer process. To address the lack of route-semantic supervision, Speaker Reconstruction Progress Reward converts consecutive reconstruction-loss changes into intermediate feedback. To address single-reference route bias, Disagreement-Aware Trajectory Reuse interprets the speaker score with terminal outcome, retaining successful low-score paths as alternative demonstrations and failed high-score paths as hard replay cases. The navigator retains the original goal-oriented instruction, and the speaker is absent at inference. In DUET-based validation on two goal-oriented VLN datasets, SMRKT improves Success Rate (SR) by 1.42 percentage points on the unseen validation setting of the REVERIE dataset, by 1.32 percentage points on the Unseen Houses split of the SOON dataset, and by 2.22 percentage points on the Unseen Instructions split of the SOON dataset; SPL and OSR rise in some settings and fall in others. The results support transferred route knowledge as a training signal, with environmental success retained as the final task criterion.

title: QUANTUM COMPUTING IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CONVERGENCE, FRAMEWORKS, AND EMERGING APPLICATIONS
abstract: : The rapid convergence of quantum computing and artificial intelligence is reshaping computational paradigms across cryptography, optimization, sensing, and intelligent systems. This paper surveys and synthesizes recent developments at the intersection of quantum computing and AI, with particular attention to superconducting quantum hardware, quantum reinforcement learning, quantum key distribution optimization, and hybrid AI-driven post-quantum security frameworks. Drawing upon 2026 literature— including advances in high-speed predistortion architectures for flux-bias lines, enhanced quantum key distribution parameter optimization, quantum reinforcement learning for spectrum allocation in 6G networks, hybrid AI–post-quantum encryption for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems, and measurement-consistent low-field MRI enhancement via k-space noise modeling—we present a unified perspective on how quantum resources augment classical AI and how AI, in turn, accelerates the practical deployment of quantum technologies. We introduce a conceptual Quantum–AI Convergence Framework that maps hardware constraints, algorithmic opportunities, and security requirements. The analysis highlights persistent challenges in noise resilience, scalability, hybrid orchestration, and regulatory readiness, while outlining promising research directions for trustworthy quantum-enhanced intelligence.

title: Recent advances in neuromorphic photonics: Devices, architectures, and physical learning systems (2022–2026)
abstract: Neuromorphic photonics has emerged in the past five years as one of the most promising hardware paradigms for overcoming the bandwidth, energy, and scalability limits of conventional electronic accelerators. Between 2022 and 2026, the field has undergone a rapid transition from isolated proof-of-concept demonstrations of individual photonic neurons or synaptic weights toward integrated, reconfigurable, and functionally complete systems that combine linear optical processing, in-hardware nonlinearity, analogue memory, and on-chip learning on a single substrate. This review provides a comprehensive and critical account of these developments, organized around three analytical axes: device-level primitives, architectural paradigms, and physical learning mechanisms. Device-level advances are discussed in terms of photonic neurons (engineered integrated neurons and dynamical laser neurons), synaptic and weighting elements (phase-change materials, electro-optic analogue memories, micro-ring weight banks), and the nonlinear platforms (silicon, silicon nitride, thin-film lithium niobate, III–V laser dynamics, photorefractive media) that enable neural-like behavior. Architectural paradigms are examined through five complementary families: integrated, coherent, and wavelength-multiplexed photonic neural networks (PNNs); spiking photonic systems, photonic reservoir computing, diffractive and free-space optical processors, and physically adaptive systems based on soliton dynamics in photorefractive media. Particular emphasis is placed on two milestones that mark the maturity of the field: the demonstration of monolithically integrated analogue memory for in situ training and inference, and the experimental realization of end-to-end on-chip backpropagation within a PNN. In parallel, an alternative and less explored direction based on spatial-soliton dynamics and photorefractive nonlinearities is analyzed in depth. In these so-called solitonic neural networks, computation, connectivity, and memory are co-localized within the optical medium, enabling adaptive interconnections and synaptic plasticity through the self-organization of light-induced refractive-index patterns. A comparative discussion is offered between integrated programmable architectures and physically adaptive, self-organized systems, identifying the key open challenges: scalability, stability, training efficiency, standardized benchmarking, and the integration of memory and computation, together with the opportunities that distinguish photonic from electronic neuromorphic hardware. Finally, future research directions are outlined, with particular emphasis on hybrid architectures that combine the programmability of integrated photonics with the physical plasticity of adaptive optical media. Approximately 80 recent works are systematically analyzed to trace the trajectory of the field and to provide a reference framework for the next generation of neuromorphic photonic processors.

title: Abstract No: 100 Enhanced Survival Prediction in IgA Nephropathy through Integration of Pathomic and Clinical Data Using Multi-Instance Learning
abstract: IgA nephropathy, the most common primary glomerular disease, necessitates accurate survival prediction to guide personalized treatment and improve patient outcomes. Current methods often inadequately leverage pathological whole-slide images (WSIs) and rely predominantly on single-modal data, which limits predictive performance. This study aims to develop a weakly supervised learning framework that effectively integrates pathomic and clinical information to improve survival prediction in IgA nephropathy.

title: Parallel‐Channel Topological Quantum Routing in a Superconducting Qudit Chain
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient quantum routing and entanglement distribution are essential for scalable quantum networks. We propose a parallel chain topological quantum routing based on a chain of superconducting qudits, where distinct internal levels of each qudit define independent topologically protected channels. Utilizing a network of superconducting qudits (multi‐level quantum systems) and microwave resonators, our scheme realizes multiple independent SSH‐type chains in the single‐excitation subspace, each associated with a distinct internal level of the qudits. The key innovation is that distinct internal levels of qudits realize mutually independent parallel SSH chains, enabling independent and protected quantum channels. We demonstrate that quantum states can be routed to different output ports based on internal degrees of freedom (i.e., distinct energy levels of superconducting qudits). Furthermore, we show that this system enables adiabatic pumping for state transfer and preparation of entanglement via the Rice‐Mele model. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the system possesses topological robustness against coupling and potential disorders, and remains stable in the presence of dissipation, highlighting its potential for quantum routing and entanglement distribution and establishing it as a versatile building block for multi‐functional quantum devices in noise‐resilient quantum networks.

title: TAPVid-MV: A Benchmark for Tracking Any Point in 3D Across Multiple Views
abstract: Multi-camera systems are increasingly practical for robotics, AR/VR, and autonomous driving because complementary views reduce depth ambiguity and preserve visibility under occlusion. Existing point-tracking benchmarks, however, focus on a single video or static multi-camera rigs. None test long-term 3D point tracking across several synchronized views under camera motion. We introduce TAPVid-MV (Tracking Any Point in Video across Multiple Views), the first benchmark for this setting. It contains a curated set of 238 sequences, 1,004 calibrated camera streams, and 74,147 point tracks across seven subsets spanning indoor and outdoor domains, from robotics and human activity to driving and synthetic procedural scenes. We obtain these trajectories using dataset-specific auxiliary modalities: sensor depth, LiDAR, SLAM and SfM points, human meshes, posed object meshes, and simulation. Every sequence and trajectory is visually verified by human annotators. Across more than 30 baselines, no method comes close to solving the task. Surprisingly, existing multi-view point trackers do not consistently outperform monocular point trackers. By evaluating reconstruction and point tracking on the same datasets, TAPVid-MV helps distinguish errors in recovered geometry from errors in point correspondence. Through this joint analysis, we identify geometry recovery as a major bottleneck for accurate 3D point tracking. Beyond multi-view 3D point tracking, our released annotations support monocular 2D and 3D point tracking, future-trajectory prediction, and 4D reconstruction. Project page: https://tapvidmv.github.io/

title: BS: Take the Hint - Interactive Multitracer PET/CT Lesion Segmentation with a Scribble-Conditioned ResEnc U-Net
abstract: Automated lesion segmentation in whole-body PET/CT is complicated by the variety of physiological tracer uptake patterns and by the differing appearance of lesions across tracers. The autoPET/CT V challenge addresses this by making segmentation interactive: user scribbles marking foreground and background are supplied alongside the image, and the algorithm is expected to exploit them. We present our submission, a scribble-conditioned residual encoder U-Net operating on four input channels: CT, PET, and a sparse scribble map for each of foreground and background. The network is initialised from the autoPET-III winning weights and extended from two to four input channels, with the two scribble channels zero-initialised so that the pretrained representation is preserved exactly at initialisation. Every model is fine-tuned per fold from the corresponding autoPET-III fold checkpoint, so that no validation case is seen during pretraining. PET intensities are normalised against a per-scan aorta blood-pool reference derived from a CT segmentation, which removes tracer- and centre-specific scaling without requiring lesion labels. At inference the five fold models are ensembled by averaging their softmax outputs per sliding-window patch, before Gaussian-weighted stitching. On the challenge's five-fold split, with each fold evaluated on its own validation cases, mean Dice is 0.554 and mean lesion-level F1 is 0.528 without scribbles, rising to 0.751 and 0.733 after five correction rounds. About 85% of that gain follows the first scribble, and the spread between fold models narrows five-fold over the same rounds, so interaction largely compensates for how well or badly a given model segments unaided.

title: Generalized spectral bound for quasi-twisted codes
abstract: Minimum distance bounds play a central role in the analysis of algebraic codes. For cyclic and constacyclic codes, several bounds based on their zero set have been developed. However, analogous results for quasi-twisted (QT) codes are comparatively limited. In this paper, we further investigate the spectral theory of QT codes and derive a general spectral bound on their minimum distance. Our bound unifies and generalizes previously known spectral bounds for quasi-cyclic (QC) and QT codes, and contains them as special cases. We present a new proof technique and show that the bound can be formulated with respect to an arbitrary subset of eigenvalues, thereby extending its applicability to the largest possible setting. Numerical examples and simulations demonstrate that the proposed bound often improves upon the Jensen bound and earlier spectral bounds.

title: Ανάπτυξη εξειδικευμένου μεγάλου γλωσσικού μοντέλου για τη ναυτιλία με αξιοποίηση αρχιτεκτονικής RAG
abstract: Τα ναυτιλιακά τεχνικά εγχειρίδια περιλαμβάνουν εκτεταμένες πληροφορίες που σχετίζονται με τη λειτουργία, τη συντήρηση και την ασφάλεια, γεγονός που καθιστά την αναζήτηση συγκεκριμένων τεχνικών στοιχείων χρονοβόρα. Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εξετάζει τη χρήση της αρχιτεκτονικής Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) ως μέθοδο για τη βελτίωση της πρόσβασης σε πληροφορίες που περιέχονται στη ναυτιλιακή τεχνική τεκμηρίωση. Σχεδιάστηκε και υλοποιήθηκε ένα τοπικά εκτελούμενο σύστημα RAG για την παραγωγή απαντήσεων βάσει ναυτιλιακών τεχνικών εγχειριδίων. Το σύστημα επεξεργάζεται έγγραφα PDF σε επικαλυπτόμενα τμήματα κειμένου, τα μετατρέπει σε διανυσματικές αναπαραστάσεις χρησιμοποιώντας το μοντέλο all-MiniLM-L6-v2 SentenceTransformer και τα αποθηκεύει σε μια μόνιμη διανυσματική βάση δεδομένων ChromaDB. Για κάθε ερώτηση του χρήστη, ανακτώνται τα σχετικά τμήματα των εγγράφων και χρησιμοποιούνται ως πλαίσιο για το γλωσσικό μοντέλο Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. Τόσο η ανάκτηση όσο και η παραγωγή απαντήσεων πραγματοποιούνται τοπικά, χωρίς τη χρήση εξωτερικού API γλωσσικού μοντέλου, ενώ αναπτύχθηκε και γραφικό περιβάλλον χρήστη για την άμεση αλληλεπίδραση με το σύστημα. Το σύστημα αξιολογήθηκε με 24 ερωτήσεις βασισμένες σε τέσσερα ναυτιλιακά τεχνικά εγχειρίδια. Η σχετική πληροφορία ανακτήθηκε επιτυχώς σε 20 από τις 24 ερωτήσεις, που αντιστοιχεί σε συνολικό ποσοστό επιτυχούς ανάκτησης 83,3%. Από τις παραγόμενες απαντήσεις, 15 (62,5%) χαρακτηρίστηκαν ως πλήρως ορθές, έξι (25,0%) ως μερικώς ορθές και τρεις (12,5%) ως λανθασμένες. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι το προτεινόμενο ελαφρύ και τοπικά εκτελούμενο σύστημα RAG μπορεί να υποστηρίξει την πρόσβαση σε τεχνική πληροφορία από διαφορετικά ναυτιλιακά εγχειρίδια, ενώ παράλληλα αναδεικνύουν ότι η επιτυχής ανάκτηση δεν εγγυάται πάντοτε μια πλήρη ή ακριβή τελική απάντηση. Το σύστημα παρέχει επομένως μια χρήσιμη βάση για την περαιτέρω ανάπτυξη τοπικά εκτελούμενων εργαλείων RAG για ναυτιλιακή τεχνική τεκμηρίωση.

title: Noise Covariance Matrix Estimation in Target Tracking in Three Approaches: n-step Prediction, Kalman Gain Covariance and Gamma-distribution of Noise Statistics
abstract: Noise parameters in many target tracking projects are assumed as known factors which is a main challenge because of uncertainty in measurement and state-model noise. Thus, many papers are focused on the accurate estimation of noise statistics. This paper is concentrated on this subject where it is tried to present three simple efficient methods in this regard. Estimation using n-step prediction, applying Kalman filter covariance and using Gamma distribution for noise parameters are the main concepts of the three proposed methods. Simulation results show the efficiency of all methods compared to other methods in the literature where the Gamma-distribution-based method is the most efficient work among other suggested ones in term of estimation error.

title: Automatic accentuation of Slovenian texts
abstract: V nalogi raziščemo samodejno naglaševanje besed v slovenskih besedilih, saj zaradi prostega besednega naglasa naglasnega mesta v slovenščini običajno ni mogoče zanesljivo določiti zgolj iz zapisa, obstoječi viri pa so vsebinsko pomanjkljivi ali premajhni. Zato postavimo cevovod za samodejno naglaševanje, ki temelji na leksikonu Sloleks in orodju CLASSLA-Stanza ter učinkovito naglasi več kot 90 % besed v transkripcijah raznolikega govora, ima pa še težave predvsem pri redkejših in tujih besedah ter enakopisnicah, saj pomena ne razlikuje. Z njim zgrajeno množico naglašenih besed in pripadajočih izgovorjav smo uporabili za treniranje klasifikatorja XGBoost za razpoznavo naglašenosti samoglasnikov: izključno akustične značilke dosežejo točnost 62 %, poln nabor značilk pa točnost 89,5 %, kar kaže na resničen, a razmeroma šibek napovedni signal akustičnih značilk. Na naših podatkih smo preverili tudi model za hrvaški jezik. Ta napoveduje mesto naglasa iz izgovorjave in doseže točnost 67,7 %, ki pada z naraščajočim številom samoglasnikov v besedi.

title: A Multi-Layer Architecture for Progressive Privacy Risk Mitigation in AI Applications
abstract: AI applications process sensitive data and remain exposed to inference and reconstruction attacks. Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs) are often deployed in isolation, allowing risks to accumulate across AI pipelines. This paper presents a Multi-Layer Architecture for Progressive Privacy Risk Mitigation that integrates semantic PII sanitization, structured anonymization, Differential Privacy, adversarial validation, and governance auditing. Experiments with Microsoft Presidio, ARX/PyCANON, and Opacus are combined with a reproducible pipeline that preserves layer interfaces and privacy metrics. Results show improved PT-BR PII detection, utility-aware anonymization, and lower inference and reconstruction exposure.

title: Forensic Audit of the MillenniumLean Clay-Proof Package (AIX Global)
abstract: Statement-level forensic audit of the MillenniumLean package (AIX Global, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22226553), which claims kernel-checked Lean 4 proofs of the six remaining Clay Millennium Problems. The audit independently reproduces every kernel-hygiene claim (clean build, zero sorry, zero project axioms, axiom footprints within the classical trio {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}) under the pinned toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0-rc1 and mathlib revision d0be1efe9a, then audits what the theorem types actually say against the official Clay statements. Verdict: the package resolves none of the six problems. Findings F01-F14: the claimed final theorems are conditional implications whose unproved premise binders carry the open problems (Riemann, Yang-Mills, P vs NP), definitions of the open statements (Navier-Stokes, BSD), or true theorems about unrelated objects (Hodge: a list identity); the universalization tower proves only 0 < n + 1. All 259 quoted lines verified byte-exact against the package; a three-lane hostile red-team pass was run on the audit itself before publication. Includes audit doctrine, per-finding evidence, reproducible probes, and a 15-test zero-mock suite.

title: ProvenCloud and the Trusted Cloud Enclave
abstract: This document describes the technical architecture of ProvenCloud and its central component, the Trusted Cloud Enclave (TCE), designed to execute sensitive workloads on cloud infrastructures whose complexity precludes exhaustive verification and whose operator cannot be regarded as fully trustworthy. It takes the form of a technical architecture paper: it explicitly states the threat model, assumptions, target security properties, and non-goals; describes the architecture and its mechanisms; analyzes the resulting trusted computing base (TCB); structures the assurance argument; and sets out its limitations. The frame of reference is the Operational Governance objective defined in [1], under which sensitive operations constitute a class of security objects in their own right, governed by Execution Authority. Against an explicit adversary, we derive from it the architectural requirements applicable to cloud infrastructure: complete mediation of flows, validation within a trusted component beyond the adversary's reach, and integrity of the operation between validation and implementation. The TCE is presented as the Trusted Decision Point for the computing environment. It establishes a governed execution perimeter around a compute node by mediating the four families of flows that surround it: administrative control, user interactions, data and storage, and software distribution. The security properties are formulated against a nation-state-level adversary controlling the infrastructure. The TCB analysis distinguishes the governance trusted computing base - reduced to the formally verified ProvenCore microkernel (Common Criteria EAL7), the governance applications, the enclave hardware, and the tenant's keys and policies - from the governed perimeter, within which any residual compromise remains confined. The assurance argument links objectives, mechanisms, and evidence on a component-by-component basis. The document concludes with limitations and future work, with a view to subsequent development in a scientific publication.

title: AI-Augmented Ultrasound Imaging Fused with Virtual Reality 3D Reconstruction for Early-Stage Tumor Detection and Clinical Decision Support
abstract: This research poster presents a low-cost, portable framework that combines AI-based ultrasound lesion detection with Virtual Reality (VR) volumetric visualization to support earlier tumor detection and clinical decision-making. The proposed pipeline integrates ultrasound acquisition, speckle denoising, CNN-based lesion detection and segmentation, AI-assisted segmentation, 3D volumetric reconstruction, and VR visualization. Simulation results indicate that AI-enhanced ultrasound can substantially improve sensitivity for early-stage, sub-10 mm lesions compared with conventional B-mode ultrasound, while the VR component provides an intuitive three-dimensional representation of tumor size and shape. The proposed approach is designed with accessibility and clinical practicality in mind, particularly for settings where advanced MRI/CT facilities may be limited. The work also identifies prospective validation using de-identified clinical ultrasound data and radiologist ground truth as an important next step.

title: Quantum Error Correction Protocols: A Mathematical Foundation
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum information processing, essential for achieving reliable quantum computation and communication. This paper investigates the mathematical basis of QEC, focusing on the fundamental concepts of entanglement, superposition, and measurement. We delve into the mathematical framework underpinning various QEC codes, including Shor's and Steane's codes, exploring their strengths and weaknesses. The core focus is on developing a novel approach based on quantum state manipulation, aiming to enhance the efficiency and robustness of QEC through the strategic application of these mathematical principles. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the mathematical properties and computational complexity associated with key QEC algorithms, demonstrating the potential for significant advancements in this field.

title: Title: Holo-Geometric Proof Systems for Verification of Complex Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel proof system based on holographic geometry, aiming to automate the verification of complex algorithms and cryptographic protocols. Traditional verification methods often involve computationally intensive solving of the algorithm, limiting their applicability to small, well-understood systems. Our system constructs a holographic projection of the algorithm, where validity is determined by the relationships between its elements and the overall holographic structure. This approach allows for automated verification of correctness and security by leveraging geometric principles, offering a fundamentally different method for formal verification. The core mechanism centers around representing the algorithm as a holographic projection, and the verification process involves analyzing the projection's structure to determine if the algorithm satisfies its requirements. This paper details the design of the proof system, its validation procedures, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in verifying complex cryptographic protocols.

title: Cabasu: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Cabasus Fish
abstract: This paper introduces Cabasu, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the unique swimming behavior of the Cabasus fish. The algorithm leverages the fish's ability to efficiently navigate complex environments by utilizing a combination of local search and a novel global exploration strategy. Cabasu employs a dynamic neighborhood structure and adaptive inertia weights within its particle representation, mimicking the Cabasus's flexible body movements and sensory perception. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results compared to established metaheuristic methods. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's design, including the key components and parameters, and provide empirical evidence of its effectiveness. The core of the algorithm is defined by the following equations: * Particle Position: $x_i(t) = (x_{i1}(t), x_{i2}(t), ..., x_{iN}(t))$, where $i = 1, 2, ..., N$ represents the $i$-th particle at time $t$. * Particle Velocity: $v_i(t) = (v_{i1}(t), v_{i2}(t), ..., v_{iN}(t))$ * Fitness Function: $f(x_i(t)) = \psi(x_i(t))$, where $\psi(x_i(t))$ is the objective function to be minimized. * Neighborhood Function: $N(i) = \{j | j \neq i \text{ and } j \text{ is within the neighborhood of } i\}$ * Dynamic Neighborhood Size: $k(t) = f(x_i(t))$, where $k$ represents the neighborhood size, dynamically adjusted based on the particle's fitness. * Inertia Weight Update: $w_i(t+1) = w_i(t) \cdot \alpha(t) + r(t)$, where $\alpha(t)$ is a dynamically adjusted inertia weight between 0 and 2, and $r(t)$ is a random number. The paper concludes by discussing future research directions and potential applications of Cabasu.

Cabasu employs a dynamic neighborhood structure and adaptive inertia weights within its particle representation, mimicking the Cabasus's flexible body movements and sensory perception. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results compared to established metaheuristic methods. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's design, including the key components and parameters, and provide empirical evidence of its effectiveness. The core of the algorithm is defined by the following equations: * Particle Position: $x_i(t) = (x_{i1}(t), x_{i2}(t), ..., x_{iN}(t))$, where $i = 1, 2, ..., N$ represents the $i$-th particle at time $t$. * Particle Velocity: $v_i(t) = (v_{i1}(t), v_{i2}(t), ..., v_{iN}(t))$ * Fitness Function: $f(x_i(t)) = \psi(x_i(t))$, where $\psi(x_i(t))$ is the objective function to be minimized. * Neighborhood Function: $N(i) = \{j | j \neq i \text{ and } j \text{ is within the neighborhood of } i\}$ * Dynamic Neighborhood Size: $k(t) = f(x_i(t))$, where $k$ represents the neighborhood size, dynamically adjusted based on the particle's fitness. * Inertia Weight Update: $w_i(t+1) = w_i(t) \cdot \alpha(t) + r(t)$, where $\alpha(t)$ is a dynamically adjusted inertia weight between 0 and 2, and $r(t)$ is a random number. The paper concludes by discussing future research directions and potential applications of Cabasu.

title: Hyperdimensional Computing with Non-Linear Dynamics
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to hyperdimensional computing (HDC) by integrating non-linear dynamical systems into the core activation functions. Traditional HDC relies on linear transformations, limiting its computational power and information density. This work proposes a framework where HDC activation functions are derived from chaotic attractors and other non-linear dynamical systems. This introduces significant advantages, including enhanced information density, improved computational efficiency, and the ability to perform complex computations with a reduced number of elements. The theoretical underpinnings of this approach are presented, demonstrating how the inherent complexity of non-linear dynamics can be harnessed within the HDC paradigm. This research aims to push the boundaries of HDC, unlocking its potential for applications demanding high computational performance and data compression. The key contribution lies in the systematic design and analysis of HDC activation functions based on non-linear systems, resulting in a fundamentally improved computational model.

title: Brown Ferret Badger: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Brown Ferrets, Badgers, and their Social Dynamics
abstract: This paper presents Brown Ferret Badger (BFB), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of brown ferrets and badgers, combined with elements of their social dynamics. BFB leverages concepts such as territoriality, exploration-exploitation trade-off, and social influence to achieve efficient global optimization. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a "territory" concept to represent individual solutions, and a "social influence" mechanism to guide convergence. We detail the algorithm's core components, including the territory assignment strategy, the exploitation phase, and the social influence update rule. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and provide a high-level description of its implementation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its potential as a competitive metaheuristic. The primary goal is to develop an algorithm that can effectively navigate complex search spaces while maintaining adaptability and robustness. The key innovations of BFB lie in its integrated territory-based representation and the dynamic social influence mechanism. We aim to provide a foundational contribution to the field of metaheuristic optimization.

title: Brown Crab Mongoose: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Brown Crab Mongoose Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Brown Crab Mongoose (BCM), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of brown crab mongooses. BCM leverages the mongoose's strategic approach to food acquisition, incorporating elements of exploration, exploitation, and adaptive movement patterns. The algorithm utilizes a novel representation of the search space, a dynamic obstacle avoidance mechanism mimicking the mongoose's avoidance of predators and competition, and a self-adaptive parameter control scheme. BCM's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The algorithm's core mechanisms, including the obstacle avoidance strategy and the adaptive parameter control, are thoroughly described. Results indicate that BCM exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, showcasing its potential for solving complex optimization challenges. Future research directions include exploring the algorithm's applicability to different problem domains and further refining its core components.

title: ## Brazilian Gracile Opossum: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by its Locomotion
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Brazilian Gracile Opossum (BGO) algorithm, inspired by the unique locomotion strategy of the Brazilian gracile opossum ( *Didelphis virginiana*). The opossum's ability to move efficiently using a combination of climbing, leaping, and gliding provides a rich source of inspiration for optimization problems. The BGO algorithm leverages these characteristics – particularly the alternating movement patterns and strategic energy expenditure – to develop a new search strategy. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a "Climb-Leap-Glide" phase transition mechanism, a dynamic energy management system, and a novel adaptive mutation operator. We demonstrate the efficacy of the BGO algorithm through application to several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics including convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that the BGO algorithm offers a promising alternative for solving complex optimization challenges, particularly those requiring adaptable and dynamic search strategies.

title: 基于量子拓扑的自适应神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "Quantum-Adaptive Neural Network" (QANN), predicated on the principles of quantum topology. We propose a dynamic adjustment mechanism leveraging quantum entanglement to facilitate rapid learning and optimization within complex systems. The QANN leverages the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to establish a global, instantaneous connection between network nodes, enabling a significantly enhanced learning capacity compared to traditional neural networks. We detail the design of the QANN, outlining the quantum entanglement topology used, the adjustment algorithm implemented, and the potential applications in areas requiring rapid adaptation and optimization. The core claim posits that the QANN's quantum entanglement-driven dynamic adjustment drastically improves learning speed and scalability across complex scenarios.

title: Non-Linear Chaos Structures: Design of an Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear chaos theory to the design of an adaptive algorithm for complex system optimization. We propose a novel approach that leverages the dynamic behavior of chaotic systems to automatically adjust algorithm parameters, enabling rapid optimization of intricate systems. The core of this design lies in the utilization of the inherent non-linearity and sensitivity within chaotic dynamics to dynamically modulate the algorithm's behavior. This allows for a more flexible and efficient approach to solving complex problems compared to traditional methods, which are often constrained by fixed parameters. The paper details the mathematical framework underpinning this algorithm, outlines the key implementation steps, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method. The focus is on creating an algorithm capable of navigating the complexities of non-linear systems with adaptability and efficiency.

title: Probability Matrix Adaptation for Enhanced Model Generalization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic matrix adaptation framework designed to dynamically adjust the parameters of probability-based models based on observed data and target variables. Traditional parameter optimization methods often struggle to adapt effectively to non-linear data and complex environments. Our approach leverages a learning algorithm to automatically determine the matrix's parameters, enabling proactive adaptation and improved model generalization. We present a method based on a gradient-based approach, iteratively refining the matrix to minimize a loss function that reflects the relationship between the model's output and the observed data. The framework demonstrates superior performance across a range of datasets, validating its effectiveness through comprehensive experimentation.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Explainable AI
abstract: This paper explores the integration of neural networks and symbolic reasoning techniques to address the explainability challenges inherent in modern Artificial Intelligence, particularly deep learning models. The core argument is that a hybrid approach – combining the perception capabilities of neural networks with the deductive reasoning power of symbolic systems – offers a pathway towards more transparent and trustworthy AI systems. We introduce a framework where a neural network acts as a perceptual module, extracting salient features from raw input data. These extracted features are then processed by a symbolic reasoning engine, enabling logical deduction, inference, and ultimately, the generation of human-understandable explanations for decisions and actions. The proposed methodology mitigates the "black box" nature of deep learning by providing a structured approach to reasoning, enhancing the interpretability of AI systems. This work lays a foundational approach for building robust and explainable AI, focusing on the synergistic interaction between these two distinct AI paradigms.

title: Data and code for "Supervisory Reinforcement Learning for Remote PID Gain Tuning in a Networked Embedded Control System"
abstract: Data and code supporting a physical-hardware study of supervisory reinforcement learning for remote PID gain tuning. The deposit contains calibration, training, identification, and confirmatory telemetry; ten matched confirmatory block manifests and requested and realized delay schedules; the frozen Stable-Baselines3 TD3 policy and metadata; Arduino Uno R4 WiFi firmware; and the statistical and local model-conditional stability-analysis scripts used in the associated manuscript. The confirmatory dataset contains 90,000 retained local-controller samples from 30 runs in ten matched physical-session blocks. Machine-specific paths, the controller’s private-network address, and Wi-Fi credentials were removed from the public copy without altering telemetry or reported results.

title: Reproducibility Package for Governed Evidence Synthesis in Emergency-QA
abstract: This restricted-access reproducibility package accompanies the manuscript "From Retrieval to Governed Evidence Synthesis: A Controlled Evaluation of GraphRAG, ACE, and Retrieval-Aware Adaptation for Emergency Question Answering" (Manuscript IPM-D-26-03949). It contains de-identified aggregate results, evaluation protocols and rubrics, aggregate benchmark metadata, and cleaned evaluation code. title: Εφαρμογές της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης στη βιομηχανία των Ανανεώσιμων Πηγών Ενέργειας
abstract: Η αυξανόμενη ζήτηση για βιώσιμες ενεργειακές λύσεις έχει επιταχύνει την ενσωμάτωση καινοτόμων τεχνολογιών στον τομέα των Ανανεώσιμων Πηγών Ενέργειας (Α.Π.Ε). Αυτή η εργασία εξετάζει τις τεχνικές της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης (ΤΝ) και τον τρόπο με τον οποίο οι εφαρμογές τους μπορούν να φέρουν επανάσταση στη βιομηχανία των Α.Π.Ε, ενισχύοντας την απόδοση, την αξιοπιστία και τη διαδικασία λήψης αποφάσεων. Στην παρούσα μελέτη αναλύονται οι κύριες μεθοδολογίες ΤΝ, όπως η μηχανική μάθηση, η βαθιά μάθηση και οι αλγόριθμοι βελτιστοποίησης, καθώς και οι εφαρμογές τους στην πρόβλεψη ενέργειας, τη διαχείριση έξυπνων δικτύων και την προγνωστική συντήρηση. Πραγματικές μελέτες περιπτώσεων αναλύονται, ενώ γίνεται αναφορά στις προκλήσεις και τα ηθικά ζητήματα που ανακύπτουν από την εφαρμογή της ΤΝ, υπογραμμίζοντας τις μετασχηματιστικές δυνατότητες αυτής της εξαιρετικής τεχνολογίας για τη βελτιστοποίηση και την ενσωμάτωσή της στις υποδομές των Α.Π.Ε, αντιμετωπίζοντας έτσι την παγκόσμια ανάγκη για καθαρότερες και πιο έξυπνες ενεργειακές λύσεις.

title: LLMpathy Unpacked: Large Language Models generate well-liked but templatic empathic responses
abstract: Code and scripts for "LLMpathy Unpacked: Large Language Models generate well-liked but templatic empathic responses". Recent research shows that greater numbers of people are turning to Large Language Models (LLMs) for emotional support, and that people rate LLM responses as more empathic than human-written responses. We suggest a reason for this success: LLMs have learned and consistently deploy a well-liked template for expressing empathy. We develop a taxonomy of 10 empathic language "tactics" that include validating someone's feelings and paraphrasing, and apply this taxonomy to characterize the language that people and LLMs produce when writing empathic responses. Across a set of 2 studies comparing a total of n = 3,265 AI-generated (by six models) and n = 1,290 human-written responses, we find that LLM responses are highly formulaic at a discourse functional level. We discovered a template -- a structured sequence of tactics -- that matches between 83--90% of LLM responses (and 60--83\% in a held out sample), and when those are matched, covers 81--92% of the response. By contrast, human-written responses are more diverse. We end with a discussion of implications for the future of AI-generated empathy.

title: bahasa inggris
abstract: Despite the growing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education, there remains a critical gap in research that specifically synthesizes how AI tutors interact with diverse learning styles to influence students' numeracy literacy. Previous studies tend to address AI in education or learning styles in isolation, without examining their intersecting effects on numeracy outcomes. This study aims to map the profile of students' numeracy literacy across learning styles when using an AI tutor, analyze student interaction patterns with AI tutor features, and identify factors influencing numeracy literacy outcomes. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted following PRISMA guidelines, analyzing 14 peer-reviewed articles published between 2018 and 2025 from Scopus and ScienceDirect databases. Bibliometric analysis using VOSViewer identified four conceptual clusters with "numeracy literacy," "learning style," "artificial intelligence," and "ChatGPT" as central nodes. Findings reveal that AI tutors demonstrate significant potential to improve numeracy literacy with gains of 28.7%–32% across studies by adapting to Visual, Auditory, Read/Write, and Kinesthetic (VARK) learning preferences, with visual learners showing the highest gains. Studi-studi sebelumnya cenderung mengkaji AI dalam pendidikan atau gaya belajar secara terpisah, tanpa meneliti efek persilangannya terhadap hasil numerasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memetakan profil literasi numerasi siswa ditinjau dari gaya belajar dalam penggunaan AI tutor, menganalisis pola interaksi siswa dengan fitur AI tutor, serta mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor yang memengaruhi hasil literasi numerasi. Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dilakukan mengacu pada panduan PRISMA , dengan menganalisis 14 artikel jurnal ilmiah yang diterbitkan antara tahun 2018- 2025 dari database Scopus dan ScienceDirect. Analisis bibliometrik menggunakan VOSViewer mengidentifikasi empat klaster konseptual dengan "literasi numerasi," "gaya belajar," "kecerdasan buatan," dan "ChatGPT" sebagai simpul sentral. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa AI tutor memiliki potensi signifikan dalam meningkatkan literasi numerasi dengan peningkatan 28,7%–32% lintas studi melalui adaptasi terhadap preferensi belajar Visual, Auditori, Read/Write, dan Kinestetik (VAK), dengan siswa visual menunjukkan peningkatan tertinggi. Tinjauan ini memberikan sintesis baru dengan mengintegrasikan efektivitas AI tutor dan perspektif gaya belajar terhadap literasi numerasi, sekaligus menawarkan implikasi teoritis dan praktis dalam mengembangkan strategi pembelajaran berdiferensiasi yang terintegrasi AI.

title: Anomaly Detector Robustness Under Physics-Bounded Process Perturbations: A Multi-Paradigm Evaluation on Research Facility Telemetry
authors: USDOE Office of Nuclear Energy - Advanced Reactor Safeguards and Security (ARSS)
abstract: This report covers three lines of effort in the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Nuclear Energy, Advanced Reactor Safeguards and Security program, carried out on operational telemetry from a liquid metal research facility. No attacks were executed and no vulnerability scanning was performed; every perturbation was synthesised offline from data the facility had already recorded. Part I tests eleven anomaly detectors — classical statistics, neural networks, sensor-dependency models and causal-structure learners — against eleven kinds of disturbance injected into real recorded telemetry at four levels of severity, the mildest three sized to stay inside what the plant has been seen to do and the fourth deliberately outside it. The evaluation covers 3,080 test cases. Two findings do not depend on anything left open. First, how a detector is tuned and thresholded matters more than which family it belongs to: at the severest level the two leading detectors are never more than 0.05 apart, yet at one false alarm in a hundred the higher-ranked one misses 38.9% of the windows in which the plant’s physics were violated and the other misses none. Judged at that alarm rate the panel is not redundant either — three of the eleven detectors are the only member that catches some disturbance — so a monitoring suite chosen on overall scores would discard detectors it needs. Second, 852 of the 1,540 primary test cases rest on too little evidence to tell apart from guessing, so a benchmark reporting them as scores reports noise in the format of a result. The expectation that motivated the study did not hold: classical methods took the top two places and led on nine of the eleven disturbances, though they ran against elaborate methods given a fifth of the sensors and no tuning. Picking the best detector per disturbance catches eight of eleven almost perfectly at the severest level and four of eleven at the mildest, which is the level that matters operationally. Three disturbances defeat everything tried, topping out between 0.53 and 0.88. Part II develops a physics-based consistency framework separating equipment degradation from signal perturbation, and finds attribution capability tracking the number of independent physical relations the instrumentation supports rather than detector complexity. Part III reports a multi-modal collection capability at an operating facility and the data, library and computing allocation delivered from it; it makes no detection claims.

title: Hong–Ou–Mandel visibility metrology of stochastic phase-matching noise in spontaneous parametric downconversion crystals
abstract: We propose a protocol for probing mechanically induced stochastic phase-matching fluctuations in spontaneous parametric downconversion (SPDC) by Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometry. The analysis is formulated for collinear type-II SPDC in β-barium borate (BBO). We distinguish the ideal white-jerk limit from the experimentally relevant finite-bandwidth regime. In the ideal limit, the incremental phase variance generated during a photon transit scales as L5; however, for a 5-mm BBO crystal, the transit time is only about 29 ps, so a piezoelectric mechanical drive is quasi-static on this time scale and the L5 law is not assumed as a direct experimental signature. Instead, the measured acceleration power spectral density and the mechanical transfer function are used to calculate the finite-bandwidth phase fluctuations. The connection to HOM visibility is derived through the biphoton joint spectral amplitude: stochastic phase mismatch modifies the phase-matching function, and the ensemble-averaged spectral-exchange overlap determines the coincidence dip. A frequency-independent common phase cancels from this overlap and therefore does not reduce HOM visibility. The resulting formulation provides a directly testable route for phase-stability metrology without requiring the experimentally inaccessible white-noise approximation.

title: Experimentally Accessible Imaginarity Measure for Composite Quantum Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, we develop an experimentally accessible framework for quantifying imaginarity resources in composite quantum systems. We first formulate an observable‐based imaginarity measure using expectation values of antisymmetric Hermitian observables, thereby identifies the minimal observable sector required for evaluating imaginarity. By extending the trace‐norm imaginarity measure to multipartite systems, we introduce local imaginarity and imaginarity correlation to distinguish local and correlation contributions of imaginarity resources. We further establish observable representations for these quantities and investigate their evaluation using incomplete measurements through truncated measures based on the accessible antisymmetric sector. The performance of the truncated scheme is quantified by analyzing the retained observable ratio, lower‐bound recovery, and finite‐shot statistical convergence. Numerical investigations on qubit and qutrit systems demonstrate the behavior of local and correlation imaginarity in nonextremal states, higher‐dimensional systems, and under phase‐damping noise. Finally, we reveal a quantitative connection between imaginarity correlation and entanglement, derive an upper bound, and show that imaginarity correlation can serve as an experimentally accessible witness of entanglement. Our results provide an operational framework for characterizing and measuring imaginarity resources in realistic quantum systems.

title: Bridging Functional Encryption and Secure Function Evaluation: Toward Efficient and Coercion‐Resistant Multi‐Party Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, a hybrid FE–SFE framework that combines distributed key generation, input masking, authenticated secret sharing, active verification, GPU acceleration, batching, compression and asynchronous communication was developed. The implementation was tested on a 10‐node CPU‐GPU cluster with Adult, MNIST and controlled benchmark vectors, 1000–10,000 records, and various security levels, with 2–10 parties. The framework maintained exact functional correctness across 287,000 valid evaluations, and all 80,000 injected malicious deviations were incorrectly evaluated without producing invalid output. The end‐to‐end latency was reduced by 41.06%–41.81% compared to sequential execution, and four‐stream GPU encryption achieved 18,234 records/s. The overhead of the active verification and coercion protection was moderate. The communication volume decreased by 62.70% when the security metadata was added. The strong scaling efficiency remained above 81% up to 8 nodes, but dropped below the desired 75% at 10 nodes. The proposed framework provides a viable basis for secure multi‐party analytics under controlled, security‐aligned experimental conditions that can be used for rigorous and reproducible evaluations, while also being functional, verified, coercion‐resistant, distributed, and performant.

title: OutageDiT: A Generative Foundation Model for Power Outage Forecasting and Scenario Simulation
abstract: Power-outage planning requires scenarios before an event occurs. These scenarios must represent uncertainty in magnitude, timing, and duration while preserving temporal dependence. However, severe events are rare, and data from any single region contain few examples of extreme outage and restoration patterns. To address this challenge, we introduce OutageDiT, a foundation model for generating seven-day outage trajectories at quarter-hour resolution, trained on outage and weather records across the United States. Specifically, a condition encoder processes the historical context and known future covariates once per forecast, and a shallow flow decoder reuses the resulting horizon-aligned states to generate complete trajectories. The resulting samples support point forecasting, uncertainty quantification, and conditional event simulation within one deep generative model. Across outage forecasting benchmarks, OutageDiT improves forecast accuracy and scenario quality over strong baselines and supports zero-shot transfer to held-out regions. Together, these results position conditional outage simulation as a bridge from outage forecasting to operational planning under uncertainty.

title: Exact Virtual Channel Programming with Vanishing Excess Overhead
abstract: A finite-dimensional physical processor cannot exactly program a continuous family of distinct unitary channels. We show that this obstruction becomes quantitative when the target channel is stored in a normalized Choi state and its output observables are reconstructed by sampling physical channels and classically post-processing their measurement outcomes. For arbitrary $d$-dimensional channels, we construct a target-independent exact reconstruction protocol and prove the optimal one-copy sampling overhead, which grows quadratically with system dimension. We further prove the sharp fixed-$d$ law that the excess overhead vanishes inversely with the number of identical Choi programs. The upper bound combines deterministic port-based teleportation with a quasi-decomposition that corrects its depolarizing distortion. The converse maps any low-overhead reconstruction protocol to a physical learner of unknown unitaries and uses local quantum estimation to recover the same leading coefficient. These results recast the universal no-programming obstruction as a quantitative trade-off between quantum program memory and classical sampling, with a leading cost that reflects the locally learnable unitary degrees of freedom.

title: On Synthesis of Metric Interval Temporal Logics
abstract: Automated mining of formal specifications is vital for verifying real-time systems. However, existing passive learning approaches remain restricted to deterministic specifications or limited fragments of Timed Regular Expressions (TRE). To our knowledge, this paper presents the first framework to tackle \emph{precise} passive learning for an expressive timed logic, \emph{Metric Interval Temporal Logic} (MITL) without relying on predefined templates or restricted logic fragments. Our approach formally reduces the timed learning problem into a scalable untimed one. By identifying quantitative timing differences between positive and negative traces, we synthesise precise timed constraints and inject them as new Boolean atomic propositions. This embeds timing into the alphabet, delegating the complex formula evaluation to highly optimised, off-the-shelf untimed LTL tools. Crucially, our framework is complete, guaranteeing a separating specification can always be found. We evaluate our implementation across several benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Residual Sparsification via Output Importance for Compressing Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures scale large language models efficiently, but they demand massive GPU memory. To cope with such demand, models are commonly compressed to reduce their memory footprint. Residual sparsification is a representative compression technique that decomposes each projection matrix of an expert into a shared base matrix and per-expert residual matrix, and then compresses the residuals. Existing sparsification methods compress each residual matrix independently by minimizing its compression error, thereby minimizing the error of each projection matrix. However, our analysis shows that this objective is misaligned with preserving model accuracy after compression. In an expert, the final output is produced through computations coupled across multiple projections and hidden representations. Therefore, even small errors in individual matrices can propagate through hidden representations and projection interactions, leading to large expert output errors and accuracy degradation. To address this misalignment, we propose PARSER, a new residual sparsification method that shifts the compression objective from minimizing isolated matrix errors to preserving the expert output error. PARSER achieves this by introducing output importance, which measures the actual contribution to the expert output error. Our experiments show that, compared with existing methods, PARSER narrows the accuracy gap to the uncompressed model by 1.41$\times$ on Qwen and 1.44$\times$ on DeepSeek, while achieving the same peak memory reduction. Our code is available at https://github.com/OSSS-KU/PARSER.

title: Integrating attention into explanation frameworks for language and vision transformers
abstract: The attention mechanism lies at the core of the transformer architecture, providing an interpretable model-internal signal that has motivated a growing interest in attention-based model explanations. Although attention weights do not directly determine model outputs, they reflect patterns of token influence that can inform and complement established explainability techniques. This work studies the potential of utilising the information encoded in attention weights to provide meaningful model explanations by integrating them into explainable AI (XAI) frameworks that target fundamentally different aspects of model behaviour. To this end, we develop two novel explanation methods applicable to both natural language processing and computer vision tasks. The first integrates attention weights into the Shapley value decomposition by redefining the characteristic function in terms of pairwise token interactions via attention weights, thus adapting this widely used game-theoretic solution concept to provide attention-driven attributions for local explanations. The second incorporates attention weights into token-level directional derivatives defined through concept activation vectors to measure concept sensitivity for global explanations. Our empirical evaluations on standard benchmarks and in a comparison study with widely used explanation methods show that attention weights can be meaningfully incorporated into the studied XAI frameworks, highlighting their value in enriching transformer explainability.

title: An Integrated Threat Model: Quantum Machine Learning Attacks on Satellite Communications and a Multi-Layered Defense Framework
abstract: Satellite communications are the invisible backbone of our connected world, supporting everything from daily internet access to critical military missions. Yet, beneath their importance lies a hidden vulnerability: the physical layer remains exposed to increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. In this paper, we explore how quantum technologies could be weaponized against these systems and how they might be defended. We present an integrated attack model that brings together Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM) for highly precise signal prediction and Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNG) for stealthy noise injection. Using realistic simulations on Qiskit, GNU Radio, and MATLAB, we show that such an attack can succeed 85% of the time, with only a 15% chance of being detected, while causing a 30% rise in bit errors. These results underline the disruptive potential of quantum-enhanced adversaries. To counter this, we propose a layered defense strategy combining post-quantum cryptography, machine learning–driven intrusion detection, adaptive signal processing, and hardware safeguards. Our findings not only reveal the scale of the challenge but also offer a roadmap toward securing future satellite networks in the quantum era.

title: Language Server based on Incremental LL Parsing
abstract: Med urejanjem programa posamezna sprememba praviloma vpliva le na majhen del dokumenta. V diplomskem delu obravnavamo inkrementalno sintaksno in semantično analizo programov v učnem jeziku Prev, katere cilj je ponovno uporabiti čim več rezultatov predhodne analize. Sintaksni del temelji na inkrementalni LL(1) analizi. Njeno delovanje podrobno utemeljimo in jo razširimo z obnovo po napakah za obravnavo nepopolnih programov. Pri semantični analizi razreševanje imen izvedemo z drevesom dosegov, pri preverjanju tipov pa vpliv sprememb določimo na podlagi zabeleženih odvisnosti. Razvite postopke združimo v jezikovni strežnik za Prev, ki rezultate analize uporablja za podporo funkcionalnostim razvojnega okolja. Učinkovitost pristopa ovrednotimo na programih različnih velikosti in pri različnih vrstah sprememb ter pokažemo, da lahko inkrementalna analiza bistveno skrajša čas ponovne obdelave dokumenta.

title: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN INDIA: REIMAGINING COPYRIGHT, PATENT, TRADEMARK, AND PERSONALITY RIGHTS IN THE DIGITAL AGE
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies of the twenty-first century, fundamentally altering the manner in which information is created, processed, disseminated, and commercialized.The integration of AI into creative and innovative processes has generated unprecedented opportunities while simultaneously posing significant challenges to traditional legal frameworks governing intellectual property rights (IPR).Existing intellectual property regimes were developed on the assumption that intellectual creations originate from human ingenuity and labor.However, modern AI systems are increasingly capable of generating literary works, artistic content, software code, inventions, trademarks, and digital identities with minimal human intervention.The emergence of generative AI technologies such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Midjourney, DALL-E, and Stable Diffusion has intensified debates concerning authorship, ownership, originality, inventorship, and liability.These developments have exposed substantial gaps within existing intellectual property legislation across jurisdictions, including India.Courts worldwide are grappling with questions concerning the copyrightability of AI-generated works, the patentability of AI-assisted inventions, trademark misuse through automated digital platforms, and the unauthorized exploitation of personality rights through deepfakes and synthetic media.This article critically examines the intersection between intellectual property rights and artificial intelligence within the Indian legal framework.Through doctrinal and analytical research, it evaluates statutory provisions, judicial precedents, and emerging legal challenges associated with AI-generated intellectual creations.The article further explores

title: AI-POWERED MARKETING ANALYTICS AND CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE MANAGEMENT: TRANSFORMING CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT AND BUSINESS PERFORMANCE
abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing the way organisations collect customer information, understand market behaviour, and make marketing decisions. Earlier marketing practices depended heavily on sales records, surveys, demographic profiles, and managerial experience. These sources are still useful, but they do not always provide a sufficiently detailed or timely picture of customers whose behaviour changes across digital and physical channels. AI-based marketing analytics helps address this gap by combining large volumes of customer information with machine learning, predictive models, natural language processing, recommendation techniques, and automation. These tools can help marketers recognise patterns, estimate future behaviour, tailor communications, and respond more quickly to customer needs. This chapter examines how AI-supported marketing analytics can strengthen customer experience and business performance. It considers applications such as behavioural segmentation, personalisation, recommend-dation systems, sentiment analysis, predictive analytics, conversational tools, churn prediction, lead scoring, dynamic pricing, and marketing automation. The discussion also considers the connection between customer relevance, responsiveness, engagement, satisfaction, loyalty, retention, and long-term value. A conceptual framework is presented in which customer data is converted into actionable insight, followed by personalised and predictive interactions that can improve customer experience and, in turn, organisational outcomes. At the same time, the chapter recognises that AI brings concerns relating to privacy, bias, transparency, cybersecurity, cost, and excessive automation. The central argument is that AI creates the greatest value when technological capability is combined with human judgement, responsible data practices, and a clear customer focus.
